aCNCNJIOM1.description: Added capacity of 220 kV & above substation equipment
aCNCNJIOM1.meaning: Added capacity of 220 kV and above substation equipment, nationwide. Monthly series published by NEA / State Grid. Measures new high-voltage substation transformer capacity commissioned in the period.
aCNCNJIOM1.how_to_use: Grid infrastructure investment is a leading indicator of China's power sector capacity expansion. 220kV+ substation additions track the build-out of the transmission backbone needed to carry renewable energy from western generation bases to eastern load centers. Acceleration in substation additions precedes renewable capacity commissioning by 12-18 months. Use as a leading indicator for renewable energy investment cycles.

aCNCNBFFTM.description: Added line length of 220 kV & above
aCNCNBFFTM.meaning: Added line length of 220 kV and above transmission lines, nationwide. Monthly series published by NEA. Measures new high-voltage transmission line length commissioned.
aCNCNBFFTM.how_to_use: Transmission line expansion is the physical infrastructure backbone of China's energy transition. Long-distance ultra-high-voltage (UHV) DC lines transport renewable power from Xinjiang, Inner Mongolia, and Yunnan to Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangdong. Faster line addition correlates with reduced renewable curtailment and improved grid integration. Pair with aCNCNJIOM1 (substation capacity) for a comprehensive grid investment picture.

aCNAUHHYDA.description: Average Utilization Hours of Power Generation Equipment, Hydraulic
aCNAUHHYDA.meaning: Average utilization hours of power generation equipment, hydraulic (hydropower). Monthly series published by NEA. Measures capacity utilization of hydropower plants in hours per year (annualized from monthly data).
aCNAUHHYDA.how_to_use: Hydro utilization hours are a real-time indicator of rainfall and reservoir levels — China's 'precipitation gauge.' Low hydro utilization forces thermal (coal) backup, raising coal consumption and emissions. High utilization indicates abundant hydro and lower carbon intensity of the power grid. The 2021-22 Sichuan/Yunnan drought drove hydro utilization to multi-year lows, causing manufacturing shutdowns and power rationing. Pair with rainfall anomalies and La Nina/El Nino cycle data.

aCNAUHTHRA.description: Average Utilization Hours of Power Generation Equipment, Thermal
aCNAUHTHRA.meaning: Average utilization hours of power generation equipment, thermal (coal + gas + oil). Monthly series published by NEA. The headline coal-power capacity utilization indicator.
aCNAUHTHRA.how_to_use: Thermal utilization hours are the key coal demand and industrial activity gauge. Rising hours signal strong power demand growth (industrial expansion) and/or renewable shortfalls requiring coal backup. Declining hours indicate either demand weakness or renewable displacement of coal — the latter is the net-zero signal. Target for carbon neutrality: thermal utilization hours declining alongside rising renewable hours. Cross-reference with aCNCESTCUM (secondary industry electricity consumption) and coal production data.

aCNCESICUM.meaning: China macro reference series: Electricity consumption, Secondary Industry. Refer to the description and source for analytical context.
aCNCESICUM.how_to_use: Cross-check against related series in the same category for context. China macro data is published by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS, real-economy + prices), People's Bank of China (PBoC, monetary), State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE, BoP/FX), and Ministry of Finance (fiscal).

aCNCNIABLM.description: New production capacity, power generation capacity, hydropower
aCNCNIABLM.meaning: New production capacity — power generation, hydropower. Monthly series published by NEA. Measures newly commissioned hydropower capacity (GW) during the period.
aCNCNIABLM.how_to_use: Newly added hydro capacity is a pipeline-to-operating indicator for China's clean energy build-out. Hydro additions are lumpy (large dam projects take 10+ years to build). Key projects: Baihetan (16 GW, fully commissioned 2022), Wudongde. Future mega-projects on the Nu River and lower Jinsha are in planning. Pair with aCNCNKIMF (Yunnan capacity) and aCNAUHHYDA (utilization) to track hydro's net-zero contribution.

aCNCNNSVYM.description: New production capacity, power generation capacity, thermal power
aCNCNNSVYM.meaning: New production capacity — power generation, thermal power. Monthly series published by NEA. Measures newly commissioned thermal (coal + gas) generation capacity (GW).
aCNCNNSVYM.how_to_use: China continues to commission new coal-fired power plants (as 'flexibility reserves' to back up intermittent renewables) even as it leads the world in renewable build-out. New thermal additions signal the pace of coal lock-in vs transition. Post-2021 power shortages triggered a surge in new coal approvals. Watch for divergence: thermal additions rising while utilization falls — indicating overcapacity and stranded asset risk in the coal-power fleet.

aCNCNCENRM.description: 发电新增设备容量_水电_累计_全国
aCNCNCENRM.meaning: China regional / sectoral statistic: 发电新增设备容量_水电_累计_全国. Detailed regional or sectoral data series — original Chinese description preserved.
aCNCNCENRM.how_to_use: Refer to source description for specific content. Regional and city-level data in the China dataset captures provincial and urban-level economic activity, often used by analysts tracking specific localities.

aCNCNRUNM.meaning: Bauxite base reserves, nationwide. Frequency not specified (likely annual or periodic). Published by MNR (Ministry of Natural Resources). Measures China's proven bauxite mineral reserve base.
aCNCNRUNM.how_to_use: Bauxite is the primary raw material for aluminium — a critical industrial metal for EVs, aerospace, and construction. China has limited domestic bauxite reserves relative to its consumption and relies heavily on imports (Guinea, Australia). Reserve data informs energy security and supply-chain resilience strategy. Changes in reserve estimates reflect new exploration, reclassification, and depletion. Use with aluminium production and import data.

aCNCNLZVJ.description: Diesel consumption (physical quantity), railway, marine, aerospace & other transportation equipment
aCNCNLZVJ.meaning: Diesel consumption (physical quantity) — railway, marine, aerospace, and other transportation equipment. Annual NBS energy balance statistic for the transport fuel sub-sector.
aCNCNLZVJ.how_to_use: Transport-sector diesel consumption is a proxy for freight activity and logistics intensity. China is electrifying its rail network (high-speed rail and heavy-freight rail electrification) but marine and aviation remain heavily fossil-fuel dependent. Declining diesel in rail tracks electrification progress; marine diesel trends reflect export shipping volumes. Cross-reference with export growth and freight ton-km data.

aCNCNQBJS.description: Domestic gas supply of municipal LPG, Weinan city
aCNCNQBJS.meaning: Domestic gas supply of municipal LPG (liquefied petroleum gas), Weinan city (Shaanxi Province). Annual NBS urban gas supply statistic at city level.
aCNCNQBJS.how_to_use: Municipal LPG supply tracks residential energy use in a mid-tier Shaanxi city. Weinan's LPG data is interesting given Shaanxi's proximity to the Ordos Basin natural gas fields — LPG is the incumbent residential fuel where pipeline gas has not yet reached. Declining LPG + rising pipeline natural gas (aCNCNNIRY) signals the coal/LPG-to-gas switching transition in city-level distribution.

aCNCNNIRY.description: Domestic gas supply of municipal LPG, Zaozhuang city
aCNCNNIRY.meaning: Domestic gas supply of municipal LPG, Zaozhuang city (Shandong Province). Annual NBS urban gas supply statistic at city level.
aCNCNNIRY.how_to_use: Zaozhuang (Shandong) is a former coal-mining city in transition. LPG supply data here contrasts with broader natural gas (pipeline and LNG) penetration into Shandong's city gas networks. Shandong is China's largest province by many industrial metrics and a key test case for the 'coal-to-gas' residential heating switch. Cross-reference with aCNNGSACTP for national gas demand context.

aCNCNKOOO.meaning: Kaolin foundation reserves, Shaanxi Province. Frequency not specified (likely annual or periodic). Published by MNR. Measures proven kaolin (china clay) mineral reserves.
aCNCNKOOO.how_to_use: Kaolin is used in paper coating, ceramics, and increasingly as a precursor for advanced materials (alumina, zeolites). Shaanxi's kaolin reserves contribute to China's ceramics and materials industry supply chain. Reserve changes track exploration activity and resource depletion rates. Use as a supply-side indicator for the domestic ceramics and advanced materials sectors.

aCNCNNUKD.meaning: Land area, Dongzhi County (Chizhou city, Anhui Province). Annual NBS geographic statistic at county level measuring total administrative land area.
aCNCNNUKD.how_to_use: Land area data establishes the geographic denominator for per-capita and per-km2 calculations (population density, road density, economic output per km2). Dongzhi (Anhui) is in the Yangtze Economic Belt zone; land-use efficiency metrics are relevant to industrial park development and rural land reform policies.

aCNCNGBWH.meaning: Land area, Jining District (Wulanchabu city, Inner Mongolia). Annual NBS geographic statistic at district level.
aCNCNGBWH.how_to_use: Jining District is the seat of Wulanchabu — a city on the Beijing-Hohhot axis with growing data-center clusters (low-cost power + cool climate). Land area provides the baseline for economic density calculations. Inner Mongolia's development model of land-intensive resource extraction transitioning to data-intensive services is visible in spatial economic data.

aCNCNMVSC.meaning: Land area, Qujiang District (Shaoguan city, Guangdong Province). Annual NBS geographic statistic at district level.
aCNCNMVSC.how_to_use: Qujiang District sits in northern Guangdong near the Nanling Mountains. Land area data here is primarily useful for per-capita economic calculations. Guangdong's spatial economy is highly uneven — the Pearl River Delta accounts for 80%+ of provincial GDP on a fraction of the land. Northern Guangdong districts like Qujiang represent the province's rural-development challenge.

aCNCNKFCR.meaning: Nature reserve area, Shandong Province. Annual NBS / MEE (Ministry of Ecology and Environment) environmental statistic measuring total protected area (km2).
aCNCNKFCR.how_to_use: Protected area expansion is a key metric for China's Ecological Civilization goals and its commitments under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (target: 30% of land and sea under protection by 2030). Shandong's nature reserve data tracks whether industrial growth is balanced with environmental conservation. Rising protected areas can restrict mining and industrial development in some zones.

aCNCNHTOY.description: Number of people affected by natural disasters, Chongqing Municipality
aCNCNHTOY.meaning: Number of people affected by natural disasters, Chongqing Municipality. Annual NBS / Ministry of Emergency Management statistic measuring disaster-affected population.
aCNCNHTOY.how_to_use: Chongqing is highly prone to flooding (Yangtze River) and geological hazards (landslides). Rising affected-population counts signal climate-change intensification of extreme weather — a direct fiscal cost (disaster relief, infrastructure repair) and longer-term migration catalyst. Climate adaptation spending is an increasingly important component of China's fiscal policy.

aCNCNNMVM.meaning: Number of towns (zhen), Santai County (Mianyang city, Sichuan Province). Annual NBS administrative geography statistic at county level.
aCNCNNMVM.how_to_use: Town (zhen) count changes reflect the pace of administrative reclassification from rural villages to urbanized towns — a dimension of China's urbanization measurement. Rapid increases in town counts can artificially inflate urbanization rates (the 'urbanization by reclassification' phenomenon). Useful for methodological cross-checking of official urbanization statistics.

aCNCNOHEG.meaning: Pyrite base reserves, Sichuan Province. Frequency not specified (likely annual). Published by MNR. Measures proven pyrite (iron sulfide) mineral reserves used in sulfuric acid production.
aCNCNOHEG.how_to_use: Pyrite is the main feedstock for China's sulfuric acid industry, which supplies phosphate fertilizer production. Sichuan's pyrite reserves underpin fertilizer supply security — critical for food security in a country importing modest but growing amounts of food. Reserve depletion could raise sulfuric acid production costs and fertilizer prices domestically.

aCNCNEVEK.meaning: Road area per capita, county-level cities. Annual NBS urban infrastructure statistic measuring paved road surface per resident (m2/person).
aCNCNEVEK.how_to_use: Road area per capita is a quality-of-urban-infrastructure indicator for county-level cities — China's third-tier administrative layer where the bulk of infrastructure investment was concentrated during 2000-2020. Rising road area per capita reflects urbanization infrastructure build-out; very high levels may indicate over-investment relative to population (ghost-city risk). Pair with population density (aCNCNFLCP) and economic output data.

aCNCNCCDK.meaning: Street offices (jiedao banshichu), Boli County (Qitaihe city, Heilongjiang Province). Annual NBS administrative geography statistic counting urban sub-district offices.
aCNCNCCDK.how_to_use: Street office counts track sub-district administrative granularity — a proxy for urbanization pace and governance capacity in former industrial cities. Boli County (Heilongjiang coal area) has been depopulating; declining street office counts signal administrative consolidation following population loss. Use as a governance indicator for resource-dependent northeast cities under restructuring.

aCNCNBFGM.meaning: Street offices, Guoyang County (Bozhou city, Anhui Province). Annual NBS administrative geography statistic.
aCNCNBFGM.how_to_use: Guoyang (Anhui) is a major coal-producing county. Street office count changes track urban administrative footprint expansion. Bozhou Prefecture is noted for traditional Chinese medicine (herb market). Administrative geography data provides context for local government capacity and service delivery in transition economies.

aCNCNDNV1.description: Total public library, Urban area, Weifang city
aCNCNDNV1.meaning: Total public libraries, urban area, Weifang city (Shandong Province). Annual NBS cultural infrastructure statistic at city level.
aCNCNDNV1.how_to_use: Public library count is a proxy for cultural infrastructure investment and literacy support — part of China's 'cultural confidence' and social-modernization agenda. Weifang is a mid-sized Shandong manufacturing city (kites, chemical industry). Library expansion here reflects local government spending priorities and the government's push to improve cultural access in non-first-tier cities.

aCNCNNOAU.description: Total urban water supply, Huaibei City
aCNCNNOAU.meaning: Total urban water supply, Huaibei City (Anhui Province). Frequency not specified (likely annual). NBS urban utilities statistic measuring water supply volume to urban residents and industry.
aCNCNNOAU.how_to_use: Urban water supply is an infrastructure utilization indicator combining population served and per-capita consumption. Huaibei is a coal city in northern Anhui facing water scarcity (North China plain water stress). Declining supply may signal conservation success or economic/population contraction. Rising supply tracks urbanization and industrial growth. Cross-reference with South-to-North Water Diversion project delivery volumes.

aCNCNOUET.description: Urban drainage pipe length, Fuzhou city
aCNCNOUET.meaning: Urban drainage pipe length, Fuzhou city (Fujian Province). Annual NBS urban infrastructure statistic measuring total drainage network length (km).
aCNCNOUET.how_to_use: Drainage infrastructure is a climate adaptation investment indicator. Fuzhou (Fujian coast) is highly exposed to typhoons and urban flooding. Expanding drainage networks reduce flood damage — a direct resilience investment. China's 'sponge city' program (urban water management) targets drainage capacity upgrades in flood-prone coastal cities. Use with aCNCNHTOY for disaster risk vs infrastructure investment comparison.

aCNNGSACTP.meaning: Natural gas apparent consumption, monthly total. Published by NBS / NEA. Calculated as: production + net imports - stock change. The headline domestic natural gas demand indicator.
aCNNGSACTP.how_to_use: Natural gas is China's fastest-growing fossil fuel and the key transition fuel in the path to carbon neutrality. Apparent consumption growth ~10-15% YoY pre-pandemic reflects: (1) coal-to-gas switching in power generation and heating, (2) industrial feedstock demand, (3) city gas residential growth. China is the world's largest LNG importer (alongside Japan). Pair with LNG import prices, Russian pipeline gas volumes, and aCNNGSACCR (YoY growth rate) for demand trend analysis.

aCNNGSACTR.description: Natural Gas Apparent Consumption, Chg Y/Y
aCNNGSACTR.meaning: Natural gas apparent consumption, year-over-year change (%). Monthly series from NBS / NEA. The growth rate of natural gas demand.
aCNNGSACTR.how_to_use: The YoY growth rate cuts seasonal noise from the level series and directly measures demand acceleration/deceleration. Growth exceeding 10% signals strong coal-to-gas switching and industrial demand; near-zero or negative growth (as in 2022 COVID lockdowns) signals demand destruction. This series feeds directly into global LNG spot price forecasts — China's demand swings are the biggest marginal driver of global LNG markets.

aCNNGSACCP.meaning: Natural gas apparent consumption, cumulative year-to-date. Monthly series from NBS / NEA. Running total from January of each year.
aCNNGSACCP.how_to_use: Cumulative consumption smooths monthly volatility and enables full-year demand forecasting. By mid-year, the cumulative series provides reliable annualized demand projections that LNG traders and pipeline operators use for forward planning. Compare current-year cumulative with prior-year to gauge annual demand trajectory. Pair with aCNNGSACCR (cumulative YoY growth) for trend-in-trend analysis.

aCNNGSACCR.description: Natural Gas Apparent Consumption, Cumulative, Chg Y/Y
aCNNGSACCR.meaning: Natural gas apparent consumption, cumulative year-to-date, year-over-year change (%). Monthly series from NBS / NEA. Cumulative growth rate.
aCNNGSACCR.how_to_use: The cumulative YoY growth rate is the cleanest single indicator of China's annual gas demand trajectory. It removes month-to-month volatility (weather, maintenance cycles) and provides a stable signal for full-year demand. A key input for LNG contract negotiations and for assessing China's progress on its natural gas share target (>10% of primary energy mix by 2030, vs ~8% currently). Track with LNG spot price (JKM) for market impact analysis.

aCNCNMNBAM.meaning: International reserves, China. Monthly series from SAFE (State Administration of Foreign Exchange) / PBoC. Measures total official reserve assets (USD bn) including foreign currency, gold, IMF SDRs, and reserve position.
aCNCNMNBAM.how_to_use: China holds the world's largest foreign exchange reserves (~$3.2T as of 2024). Reserve levels are a key macro-stability anchor: they back the CNY peg corridor, fund PBOC FX intervention, and underpin China's external creditor position. Monthly changes reflect: (1) valuation effects (USD/EUR/gold price moves), (2) net intervention, (3) interest income. Declining reserves signal capital outflow pressure or intervention to defend CNY. Cross-reference with BoP financial account and CNY spot rate.

aCNHRASG.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Area, Shaoguan
aCNHRASG.meaning: Cumulative floor space of commercial housing transacted in Shaoguan, a smaller Guangdong city. Reflects local demand conditions in a tier-3 city context where price sensitivity and inventory build-up differ from tier-1 markets.
aCNHRASG.how_to_use: Benchmark against Guangdong province aggregate (aCNIREDGD) to assess whether demand weakness is concentrated in lower-tier cities; sustained declines signal affordability stress spreading beyond major metros.

aCNHRASX.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Area, Shaoxing
aCNHRASX.meaning: Cumulative floor space of commercial housing transacted in Shaoxing, a prosperous Zhejiang city near Hangzhou. Captures demand in an affluent Yangtze River Delta sub-market closely linked to Zhejiang's export economy.
aCNHRASX.how_to_use: Compare with Zhejiang province data (aCNIREDZJ) and national residential sales (aCNHSALESRS) to isolate whether Yangtze Delta cities are recovering faster than the national average after the Evergrande shock.

aCNHRAXA.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Area, Xi'an
aCNHRAXA.meaning: Cumulative floor space of commercial housing transacted in Xi'an, a major tier-1.5 city in Shaanxi and the largest population center in northwest China. Xi'an saw a population inflow boom in 2017-2020 that inflated housing demand.
aCNHRAXA.how_to_use: Monitor alongside Shaanxi investment data (aCNIREDSX) to gauge whether northwestern China's relative resilience post-Three Red Lines is holding; Xi'an often outperforms the interior average due to university and tech sector demand.

aCNBCOMPT.meaning: Total Buildings Completed — total floor space of completed buildings (residential + commercial + other). Released monthly in NBS Real Estate Investment release.
aCNBCOMPT.how_to_use: Lagging completion gauge. Pre-2021 ~10mn sq m/month; collapsed 50%+ since 2022. Tracks property-developer ability to finish pre-sold projects ('保交楼' policy priority). Sustained drops alongside rising under-construction stock signals stalled projects.

aCNBCOMPTY.meaning: Total Buildings Completed, YoY change — pace of construction completions.
aCNBCOMPTY.how_to_use: Sharp negative YoY (e.g. -25% in 2023-24) marks the depth of China's property completion crisis. Watch for stabilization signals (>0% YoY) as a property-cycle bottoming indicator.

aCNBCOMPCBY.meaning: Buildings Completed, Commercial, YoY — commercial-construction growth pace.
aCNBCOMPCBY.how_to_use: Track for office/retail real estate cycle. Commercial completions have been more stable than residential through the property downturn.

aCNBCOMPRT.meaning: Buildings Completed, Residential — residential-only completions. ~75% of total completions.
aCNBCOMPRT.how_to_use: Tracks delivery to homebuyers who pre-purchased units. The '保交楼' (deliver-on-pre-sold-homes) policy targets this metric. Watch alongside under-construction (aCNBLDUCRB) for the gap reflecting stalled projects.

aCNBCOMPRTY.meaning: Buildings Completed, Residential, YoY — residential completion growth pace.
aCNBCOMPRTY.how_to_use: Most-watched of the residential housing-cycle indicators. Sustained negative YoY since 2022 reflects developer-finance crisis. Bottoming would mark property-policy success.

aCNBLDUCT.meaning: Total Buildings Under Construction — floor space of buildings currently being built. Stock measure (cumulative).
aCNBLDUCT.how_to_use: Stock measure tracking the property-development pipeline. Massive ~7-8 billion sq m in recent years, reflecting the pre-sale-driven Chinese property model. Falling under-construction stock signals industry-wide deleveraging.

aCNBLDUCTY.meaning: Buildings Under Construction, YoY — pace of under-construction stock growth.
aCNBLDUCTY.how_to_use: Track for property-pipeline direction. Falling YoY since 2022 shows industry-wide reduction in active development.

aCNBLDUCRB.meaning: Buildings Under Construction, Residential — residential-only floor space being built.
aCNBLDUCRB.how_to_use: Tracks residential-housing pipeline. Pair with completions (aCNBCOMPRT) — gap reflects stalled projects (developer financing crisis).

aCNBLDUCRBY.description: Buildings Under Construction, Residential, Chg Y/Y
aCNBLDUCRBY.meaning: Buildings Under Construction, Residential, YoY — residential pipeline growth.
aCNBLDUCRBY.how_to_use: Track for residential-cycle direction. Negative YoY confirms ongoing deleveraging.

aCNBLDUCCBY.description: Buildings floor space under construction, Chg Y/Y
aCNBLDUCCBY.meaning: Buildings Floor Space Under Construction, YoY — alternative release.
aCNBLDUCCBY.how_to_use: Cross-check against aCNBLDUCTY. Both track the same under-construction floor space at quarterly cadence.

aCNCONINVR.meaning: Construction Investment, Residential — residential property-development investment. Subset of total fixed-asset investment.
aCNCONINVR.how_to_use: Major GDP-component driver historically (~10% of GDP at peak). Has declined sharply since 2021 as property deleveraging compressed developer balance sheets. Watch alongside FAI (fixed-asset investment) total.

aCNCONINVRY.meaning: Construction Investment, Residential, YoY — pace of residential investment.
aCNCONINVRY.how_to_use: Most market-relevant housing-cycle gauge. Sustained -10% YoY since 2022 reflects ongoing crisis. PBoC mortgage cuts, special-purpose bond support, and 'whitelist' lending facilities target a stabilization here.

aCNHSALESCB.description: Floor space of commercial buildings sold
aCNHSALESCB.meaning: Floor Space of Commercial Buildings Sold — total property sales by floor space (residential + commercial).
aCNHSALESCB.how_to_use: Demand-side indicator. Sustained drops since 2021 mirror new-starts collapse. China property sales recovery requires both confidence and developer ability to deliver — both are needed for sustained upturn.

aCNHSALESRS.description: Floor space of commercial residential buildings sold
aCNHSALESRS.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date floor space of commercial residential buildings sold nationwide — the broadest measure of housing demand published by NBS monthly. At peak (2021) sales exceeded 1.8 billion sq m annually; by 2023 they had dropped roughly 25%.
aCNHSALESRS.how_to_use: This is the primary demand-side indicator for the China property cycle: sustained YoY declines confirm the post-Three Red Lines contraction, while a durable recovery in sales is the prerequisite for any rebound in new starts (aCNBSTFSHR) and developer investment.

aCNBSTFSH.description: Floor space of houses newly started
aCNBSTFSH.meaning: Floor Space of Houses Newly Started — total newly-started construction (residential + commercial). Most forward-looking property-cycle indicator.
aCNBSTFSH.how_to_use: THE leading housing-cycle indicator. Newly-started construction collapsed 50%+ from 2021 peak, marking the depth of the property crisis. Watch for stabilization (>0% YoY) as a forward-looking property-recovery signal.

aCNBSTFSHR.description: Floor space of residential buildings newly started
aCNBSTFSHR.meaning: Floor Space of Residential Buildings Newly Started — residential-only new construction. The single most-watched leading indicator for China property.
aCNBSTFSHR.how_to_use: Track YoY growth. Sustained negative YoY signals continued property weakness; positive YoY would signal cycle bottom. Falling new starts means developers cutting the pipeline — eventual supply shortage if structural housing demand is unmet.

aCNIREDAN.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Anhui
aCNIREDAN.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Anhui province, covering construction, land purchase, and equipment. Anhui is a central China province increasingly integrated into the Yangtze River Delta economic zone.
aCNIREDAN.how_to_use: Compare against the national total (aCNIREDTC) and Anhui's YoY growth rate (aCNIREDANY) to identify whether central provinces are cushioning the national decline driven by coastal developer defaults.

aCNIREDANY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Anhui, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDANY.meaning: Year-on-year percentage change in cumulative real estate development investment in Anhui. Provides a cleaner cycle signal than the level series by removing seasonal accumulation patterns.
aCNIREDANY.how_to_use: A sustained negative print confirms that Anhui developers are cutting capex in line with the national deleveraging; a divergence from the national YoY (aCNIREDTCY) would indicate province-specific policy stimulus or SOE developer market share gains.

aCNIREDBJ.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Beijing
aCNIREDBJ.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Beijing municipality. As a top-tier city with administrative demand and strict supply constraints, Beijing investment is structurally more resilient than lower-tier markets.
aCNIREDBJ.how_to_use: Use alongside the Beijing YoY rate (aCNIREDBJY) and national total (aCNIREDTC) to assess whether the capital's market is decoupling from the nationwide downturn; sustained Beijing weakness signals systemic rather than local stress.

aCNIREDBJY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Beijing, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDBJY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of real estate development investment in Beijing. Beijing's YoY trend is closely watched as a tier-1 bellwether — policy easing (relaxing hukou restrictions, cutting down-payment ratios) typically shows up here first.
aCNIREDBJY.how_to_use: Compare with the national YoY (aCNIREDTCY) and Shanghai YoY (aCNIREDSGY) to construct a tier-1 composite; if tier-1 YoY diverges positively from the national, it suggests that only SOE-backed large cities are stabilizing.

aCNBCOMPCB.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Buildings completed, Floor Space of Buildings Completed
aCNBCOMPCB.meaning: Real Estate Investment, Buildings Completed, Floor Space (commercial) — commercial buildings completion. Subset of total completions.
aCNBCOMPCB.how_to_use: Tracks office and retail-mall completion. China's commercial real estate cycle has been in oversupply for years; sustained low completions signal absorption period.

aCNIREDTCY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDTCY.meaning: Year-on-year change in total national real estate development investment — one of the most widely quoted indicators of China's property cycle health, published by NBS monthly. It turned negative in mid-2022 and remains one of the key metrics watched by the PBOC and NDRC.
aCNIREDTCY.how_to_use: This is the headline YoY to monitor: a return to positive territory would mark a turning point for the sector, while continued double-digit declines reinforce the case for policy stimulus. Pair with residential sub-series (aCNIREDRBY) to distinguish housing from commercial real estate drag.

aCNIREDCH.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Chongqing
aCNIREDCH.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Chongqing municipality, the largest municipality by area and a key inland growth engine. Chongqing has significant public housing and municipal SOE developer activity that can offset private developer weakness.
aCNIREDCH.how_to_use: Assess alongside aCNIREDCHY for the trend; Chongqing's strong infrastructure mandate means its investment data is partly driven by government-backed projects, making it a partial counter-cyclical offset to private developer collapse post-Evergrande.

aCNIREDCHY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Chongqing, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDCHY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of real estate development investment in Chongqing. Because Chongqing has a large social housing program, this YoY can be less negative than private-market-dominated coastal provinces during downturns.
aCNIREDCHY.how_to_use: Compare with Sichuan (aCNIREDSCY) as an interior southwest composite; if Chongqing outperforms Sichuan on a YoY basis, it likely reflects Chongqing's policy-driven investment activity rather than genuine market recovery.

aCNIREDCBB.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Commercial business buildings
aCNIREDCBB.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date investment in commercial business buildings (retail, shopping malls, mixed-use commercial) nationwide. This sub-category separates commercial real estate from residential and office, capturing retail property investment trends.
aCNIREDCBB.how_to_use: Benchmark against residential investment (aCNIREDRB) and office investment (aCNIREDOB) to identify which property sub-segment is leading the cycle; commercial retail investment tends to lag residential recovery as consumer sentiment lags income recovery.

aCNIREDCBBY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Commercial business buildings, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDCBBY.subcategory: RE Development Investment — Commercial Buildings YoY
aCNIREDCBBY.meaning: Year-on-year change in investment in commercial business buildings. Reflects structural shifts in retail and commercial property demand, partly driven by the rise of e-commerce and hybrid work reducing physical retail and office demand.
aCNIREDCBBY.how_to_use: A persistent negative YoY signals structural oversupply in commercial real estate, distinct from the cyclical housing downturn; compare with office YoY (aCNIREDOBY) to determine whether the commercial real estate correction is broad-based.

aCNBLDUCCB.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Floor space under construction
aCNBLDUCCB.meaning: Real Estate Investment, Floor Space Under Construction — alternative aggregation of under-construction floor space.
aCNBLDUCCB.how_to_use: Cross-check against aCNBLDUCT. Real estate development under-construction stock is a key property-pipeline gauge.

aCNIREDFJ.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Fujian
aCNIREDFJ.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Fujian province, a coastal province with strong private sector and overseas Chinese investment in real estate. Fujian was disproportionately exposed to Evergrande and Country Garden as local buyers were active pre-sale purchasers.
aCNIREDFJ.how_to_use: Track alongside Fujian's YoY rate (aCNIREDFJY) and compare with Guangdong (aCNIREDGD) as a coastal property bellwether pair; Fujian's recovery trajectory indicates how coastal private-market demand is faring post-default cycle.

aCNIREDFJY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Fujian, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDFJY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of real estate development investment in Fujian. Given Fujian's exposure to private developers and pre-sale model buyers, this YoY is sensitive to confidence shocks from developer defaults.
aCNIREDFJY.how_to_use: Use with Fujian level data (aCNIREDFJ) to track the pace of recovery; compare against Guangdong YoY (aCNIREDGDY) to see if southern coastal markets are moving in sync or diverging post-保交楼 policy.

aCNIREDGD.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Guangdong
aCNIREDGD.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Guangdong, China's largest provincial economy and ground zero for the Evergrande and Country Garden defaults. Guangdong accounts for a disproportionate share of total national real estate investment.
aCNIREDGD.how_to_use: Guangdong is the single most important provincial indicator for China real estate: its trajectory versus the national average (aCNIREDTC) signals whether the epicenter of the default crisis is stabilizing or worsening. Watch for signs of SOE developer (Poly, China Resources Land) market share gains.

aCNIREDGDY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Guangdong, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDGDY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of real estate development investment in Guangdong. As the province most affected by Evergrande (HQ in Shenzhen) and Country Garden (HQ in Foshan), Guangdong's YoY captures the sharpest end of the private developer deleveraging cycle.
aCNIREDGDY.how_to_use: A sustained recovery in Guangdong's YoY toward zero is necessary (though not sufficient) to call a national property bottom; compare with tier-1 Beijing YoY (aCNIREDBJY) to see if the recovery is geographically broadening.

aCNIREDGX.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Guangxi
aCNIREDGX.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Guangxi autonomous region, a lower-income coastal province bordering Vietnam. Guangxi's real estate market is heavily influenced by speculation from neighboring provinces and cross-border trade dynamics.
aCNIREDGX.how_to_use: Compare with Guangdong (aCNIREDGD) to assess spillover from Guangdong's market stress; Guangxi's smaller market means its data is more volatile but reflects conditions in China's southern tier-3/4 city markets.

aCNIREDGXY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Guangxi, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDGXY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of real estate development investment in Guangxi. Guangxi's YoY can be more volatile than larger provinces due to project timing in a smaller market with large infrastructure-linked real estate components.
aCNIREDGXY.how_to_use: Use alongside Guangxi level data (aCNIREDGX) and compare with the national YoY (aCNIREDTCY); persistent underperformance of Guangxi vs the national average signals that lower-tier southern markets continue to suffer disproportionate inventory overhang.

aCNIREDHE.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Hebei
aCNIREDHE.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Hebei province, which surrounds Beijing and benefited from Beijing Xiong'an New Area development and 2022 Winter Olympics infrastructure. Hebei's market is closely tied to Beijing spillover demand.
aCNIREDHE.how_to_use: Track alongside Beijing investment (aCNIREDBJ) as a satellite-city indicator; outperformance of Hebei vs Beijing suggests that suburban demand or Xiong'an policy investment is buffering the broader residential downturn.

aCNIREDHEY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Hebei, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDHEY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of real estate development investment in Hebei. Reflects both organic residential market trends and Beijing-policy-driven infrastructure investment in the Jing-Jin-Ji integrated region.
aCNIREDHEY.how_to_use: Compare against Beijing YoY (aCNIREDBJY) and the national YoY (aCNIREDTCY); sustained Hebei outperformance would indicate that Xiong'an and government-led construction projects are propping up the provincial number.

aCNIREDHJ.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Heilongjiang
aCNIREDHJ.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Heilongjiang province, a northeastern rust-belt province experiencing long-term population outflow. Heilongjiang faces structural housing oversupply as labor migration depresses demand.
aCNIREDHJ.how_to_use: This series is informative as a stress case for demographic headwinds on property: compare with national total (aCNIREDTC) to see how deep the structural trough is versus the cyclical national downturn.

aCNIREDHJY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Heilongjiang, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDHJY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of real estate development investment in Heilongjiang. Expected to be chronically negative due to structural population decline, offering a contrast with cyclical-downturn provinces.
aCNIREDHJY.how_to_use: Use as a baseline comparison for other declining provinces; if Liaoning (aCNIREDLNY) or Henan track toward Heilongjiang's chronic negative prints, it signals those markets are tipping from cyclical to structural decline.

aCNIREDHEN.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Henan
aCNIREDHEN.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Henan, China's most populous province and a major lower-tier city real estate market. Henan was severely hit by the 2021 developer defaults and also by the Zhengzhou flood, compounding the property downturn.
aCNIREDHEN.how_to_use: Compare with Hubei (aCNIREDHU) and Hunan (aCNIREDHN) as a central China troika; Henan's persistent weakness reflects the depth of developer default exposure in inland China and the slow pace of 保交楼 delivery.

aCNIREDHENY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Henan, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDHENY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of real estate development investment in Henan. Among the most watched inland provincial YoY series given Henan's large size and acute exposure to defaulted developers' unfinished projects.
aCNIREDHENY.how_to_use: A turn from negative to flat in Henan's YoY would be a significant signal for central China stabilization; contrast with Guangdong (aCNIREDGDY) to compare inland vs coastal recovery trajectories.

aCNIREDHU.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Hubei
aCNIREDHU.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Hubei province, home of Wuhan — one of China's major inland cities. Hubei's market was doubly disrupted by COVID-19 in 2020 and the subsequent property downturn.
aCNIREDHU.how_to_use: Track alongside Hunan (aCNIREDHN) and Henan (aCNIREDHEN) as an indicator of central China real estate health; Hubei's larger economy and Wuhan's tier-1.5 status mean it can recover faster than smaller inland provinces.

aCNIREDHUY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Hubei, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDHUY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of real estate development investment in Hubei. Hubei's YoY reflects both the ongoing national deleveraging cycle and the lingering impacts of COVID-19 disruption on project pipelines.
aCNIREDHUY.how_to_use: Compare with the national YoY (aCNIREDTCY) and Hunan (aCNIREDHNY); a meaningful Hubei outperformance would point to Wuhan's urban renewal programs or SOE developer dominance relative to defaulted private developers.

aCNIREDHN.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Hunan
aCNIREDHN.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Hunan province. Changsha, Hunan's capital, has implemented some of the more aggressive local easing measures to support the property market since 2022.
aCNIREDHN.how_to_use: Watch for divergence from the national trend (aCNIREDTC) — Hunan's proactive city-level policy easing could make it a recovery leader among central provinces; compare with Hubei (aCNIREDHU) to assess which central province is recovering faster.

aCNIREDHNY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Hunan, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDHNY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of real estate development investment in Hunan. Changsha's relatively affordable housing and tech-sector job growth have made Hunan one of the more resilient central province markets in the downturn.
aCNIREDHNY.how_to_use: Use alongside national YoY (aCNIREDTCY) and Hubei YoY (aCNIREDHUY); if Hunan consistently outperforms both, it validates the city-level demand stimulus playbook as a template for other provinces.

aCNIREDRB.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Investment in Real Estate, Residential buildings
aCNIREDRB.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date national investment in residential buildings only, stripping out office, commercial, and industrial real estate. Residential buildings account for roughly 70% of total real estate development investment and are the core of the property cycle.
aCNIREDRB.how_to_use: Pair with total investment (aCNIREDTC) to calculate the residential share — a falling share suggests commercial/industrial is relatively better; use the residential YoY (aCNIREDRBY) as the primary sub-index for housing-specific policy transmission.

aCNIREDTC.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Investment in Real Estate, Total
aCNIREDTC.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date total national real estate development investment — the broadest investment measure in NBS's monthly Real Estate Investment release. This is the single most-cited China property investment figure by policymakers and markets.
aCNIREDTC.how_to_use: Compare the annual run-rate with the 2021 peak (~15 trillion CNY) to gauge the depth of the cycle; use alongside residential sub-index (aCNIREDRB) and the YoY growth rate (aCNIREDTCY) to assess both the level and direction of the cycle.

aCNIREDJG.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Jiangsu
aCNIREDJG.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Jiangsu province. Jiangsu is one of China's wealthiest provinces and the second-largest by GDP; its real estate market is anchored by Nanjing, Suzhou, and Wuxi — all tier-1.5 or tier-2 cities.
aCNIREDJG.how_to_use: Compare with Zhejiang (aCNIREDZJ) as a Yangtze River Delta pair; Jiangsu's stronger exposure to manufacturing and export sectors means its real estate cycle has a distinct income driver that can diverge from purely financial-sector-driven Zhejiang.

aCNIREDJGY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Jiangsu, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDJGY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of real estate development investment in Jiangsu. Jiangsu's YoY is closely watched given the province's scale and the outsized role of Suzhou and Nanjing in reflecting premium-tier demand.
aCNIREDJGY.how_to_use: Pair with Zhejiang YoY (aCNIREDZJY) and Shanghai YoY (aCNIREDSGY) to construct a Yangtze Delta composite; if all three recover together, it signals the most economically important corridor is stabilizing.

aCNIREDJX.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Jiangxi
aCNIREDJX.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Jiangxi province. Jiangxi is a mid-tier interior province whose real estate market was heavily reliant on migrant-worker remittance demand and has faced significant inventory overhang.
aCNIREDJX.how_to_use: Compare with neighboring Hunan (aCNIREDHN) and Fujian (aCNIREDFJ) to assess central-interior vs coastal divergence; Jiangxi's persistent weakness often reflects interior cities' difficulty in attracting sustained housing demand.

aCNIREDJXY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Jiangxi, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDJXY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of real estate development investment in Jiangxi. Reflects demand conditions in a mid-tier interior market susceptible to inventory build-up and constrained by slower wage growth than coastal peers.
aCNIREDJXY.how_to_use: Use alongside Jiangxi level data (aCNIREDJX) and compare to the national YoY (aCNIREDTCY); consistent underperformance signals Jiangxi belongs to the structurally challenged interior tier alongside Heilongjiang and Liaoning.

aCNRDLAASP.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Land acquisition area
aCNRDLAASP.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date land acquisition area by real estate developers nationwide — the earliest leading indicator in the property pipeline, preceding new starts by 6-18 months. Land purchases by developers collapsed after the Three Red Lines policy restricted developer financing.
aCNRDLAASP.how_to_use: This is the most forward-looking series in the NBS real estate release: a sustained positive YoY in land acquisition precedes a recovery in new starts (aCNBSTFSHR) by at least 2-3 quarters. Watch for state-owned developers taking more land while private developers remain sidelined.

aCNIREDLN.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Liaoning
aCNIREDLN.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Liaoning province, a major northeastern industrial province facing demographic decline. Liaoning anchors the northeast rust belt, where structural oversupply compounds the cyclical property downturn.
aCNIREDLN.how_to_use: Compare with Heilongjiang (aCNIREDHJ) as a northeast China composite; Liaoning's Shenyang and Dalian are larger cities that could show earlier recovery signs than smaller Heilongjiang cities, distinguishing city-tier effects from provincial effects.

aCNIREDLNY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Liaoning, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDLNY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of real estate development investment in Liaoning. A key read on northeast China's ability to stabilize after years of combined demographic outflow and property cycle downturn.
aCNIREDLNY.how_to_use: Compare with Heilongjiang YoY (aCNIREDHJY) and the national YoY (aCNIREDTCY); if Liaoning converges toward the national average while Heilongjiang continues to underperform, it suggests city-size matters more than the northeast discount.

aCNIREDOB.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Office buildings
aCNIREDOB.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date national investment in office buildings. Office real estate investment reflects corporate expansion plans and is sensitive to the demand from financial services, tech, and professional services sectors.
aCNIREDOB.how_to_use: Compare with residential (aCNIREDRB) and commercial business (aCNIREDCBB) to track sub-sector divergence; office investment has been under structural pressure from hybrid-work trends and the post-pandemic reconfiguration of corporate real estate demand.

aCNIREDOBY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Office buildings, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDOBY.subcategory: RE Development Investment — Office Buildings YoY
aCNIREDOBY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of investment in office buildings. Provides a cleaner read on the office real estate cycle stripped of the seasonal accumulation effect in the level series.
aCNIREDOBY.how_to_use: Use alongside commercial business YoY (aCNIREDCBBY) and residential YoY (aCNIREDRBY) to identify which sub-sector is recovering fastest; a persistent office YoY decline while residential recovers would indicate a structural shift in Chinese real estate away from office.

aCNIREDRGR.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Real growth, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDRGR.meaning: Quarterly real (inflation-adjusted) year-on-year growth rate of total real estate development investment, published at quarterly frequency by NBS. This provides a volume-based measure of investment activity free from price effects.
aCNIREDRGR.how_to_use: Cross-check against the nominal YoY (aCNIREDTCY) to identify whether nominal declines are partly offset by construction cost deflation; in a downturn, real growth can be less negative than nominal if construction input prices fall faster.

aCNIREDRBY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Residential buildings, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDRBY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of investment in residential buildings — the most policy-sensitive sub-index of the NBS real estate investment release. This series directly reflects developer willingness to invest in housing after Three Red Lines constrained their balance sheets.
aCNIREDRBY.how_to_use: This is the most important YoY sub-series for housing policy analysis: policymakers target a return to positive residential investment YoY as a sign that the 保交楼 program is transitioning to new supply investment; compare with total YoY (aCNIREDTCY) to see residential vs commercial divergence.

aCNIREDSX.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Shaanxi
aCNIREDSX.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Shaanxi province. Xi'an, Shaanxi's capital, has been a notable outperformer in northwest China due to its university, military, and tech sector demand base, partially insulating it from the broader downturn.
aCNIREDSX.how_to_use: Compare with Sichuan (aCNIREDSC) as a western China peer; Shaanxi's better-performing cities like Xi'an may show earlier inflection points than more rural provinces, helping to distinguish urban recovery from nationwide property stabilization.

aCNIREDSXY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Shaanxi, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDSXY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of real estate development investment in Shaanxi. Xi'an's population inflow and government-sector demand provide a relative buffer, potentially enabling Shaanxi's YoY to diverge positively from the national average.
aCNIREDSXY.how_to_use: Monitor for divergence from the national YoY (aCNIREDTCY); if Shaanxi consistently outperforms, it validates the hypothesis that northwest China's administrative and education center cities are recovering on a different (faster) timeline than coastal private-developer-dominated markets.

aCNIREDSD.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Shandong
aCNIREDSD.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Shandong, China's third-largest provincial economy. Shandong has a significant state-owned developer presence and a large working-class urban population, giving its market different dynamics from Guangdong or Zhejiang.
aCNIREDSD.how_to_use: Compare with Jiangsu (aCNIREDJG) as a northern coastal vs Yangtze Delta comparison; Shandong's heavier industrial economy means its property demand is more closely correlated with industrial employment than financial or tech sector income.

aCNIREDSDY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Shandong, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDSDY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of real estate development investment in Shandong. Reflects both the national property cycle and Shandong's industrial economy dynamics; SOE developer activity in Jinan and Qingdao can buffer the Shandong series relative to coastal private-market-driven provinces.
aCNIREDSDY.how_to_use: Track alongside Jiangsu YoY (aCNIREDJGY) and the national YoY (aCNIREDTCY); Shandong's SOE buffer effect means it may show less extreme declines but also slower recoveries than Guangdong.

aCNIREDSG.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Shanghai
aCNIREDSG.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Shanghai municipality. Shanghai is China's financial center and the most internationally monitored tier-1 city; its property investment data reflects the interplay of global capital flows, luxury housing, and commercial real estate.
aCNIREDSG.how_to_use: Compare with Beijing (aCNIREDBJ) to construct a tier-1 pair; Shanghai's recovery relative to Beijing often signals whether the financial center is leading the policy-driven stabilization, as Shanghai is where international developer financing and REIT structures are most active.

aCNIREDSGY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Shanghai, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDSGY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of real estate development investment in Shanghai. The single most-watched city-level real estate YoY for global investors monitoring China property stabilization.
aCNIREDSGY.how_to_use: If Shanghai's YoY turns positive while the national YoY (aCNIREDTCY) remains negative, it signals a top-tier city decoupling; pair with Beijing YoY (aCNIREDBJY) to determine if tier-1 divergence from the national is sustained or a one-quarter anomaly.

aCNIREDSC.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Sichuan
aCNIREDSC.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Sichuan province. Chengdu, Sichuan's capital, is a major interior megacity that has attracted significant tech and manufacturing investment, supporting housing demand above the western China average.
aCNIREDSC.how_to_use: Compare with Chongqing (aCNIREDCH) as the Chengdu-Chongqing Economic Circle pair; Sichuan's data reflects Chengdu's growing role as an interior consumption hub, making it one of the more resilient interior province real estate markets.

aCNIREDSCY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Sichuan, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDSCY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of real estate development investment in Sichuan. Chengdu's population inflow and strong tech sector job creation have made Sichuan one of the better-performing interior provinces in the post-Three Red Lines environment.
aCNIREDSCY.how_to_use: Track alongside Chongqing YoY (aCNIREDCHY) and the national YoY (aCNIREDTCY); sustained outperformance of the Chengdu-Chongqing corridor vs the national average validates the western growth pole narrative for China's property stabilization.

aCNIREDTJ.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Tianjin
aCNIREDTJ.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Tianjin municipality, a tier-1 city and major port adjacent to Beijing. Tianjin has faced significant oversupply issues since 2018 due to prior infrastructure-led property development, making it one of the more challenged tier-1 markets.
aCNIREDTJ.how_to_use: Compare with Beijing (aCNIREDBJ) as a Jing-Jin corridor pair; Tianjin's persistent underperformance vs Beijing reflects its earlier oversupply cycle, and any recovery here would signal the Jing-Jin region is fully clearing its inventory backlog.

aCNIREDTJY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Tianjin, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDTJY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of real estate development investment in Tianjin. Tianjin's YoY has been among the weakest of major cities, reflecting both pre-existing oversupply and the additional impact of Three Red Lines on leveraged developers active in the market.
aCNIREDTJY.how_to_use: Use alongside Beijing YoY (aCNIREDBJY) and the national YoY (aCNIREDTCY); a convergence of Tianjin's YoY toward the national average would signal that even the most challenged tier-1 cities are stabilizing.

aCNIREDYN.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Yunnan
aCNIREDYN.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Yunnan province, a southwestern border province. Yunnan's real estate market was boosted by tourism-linked property and retiree demand from coastal cities but has since faced sharp corrections in resort and holiday home segments.
aCNIREDYN.how_to_use: Compare with Sichuan (aCNIREDSC) and Guizhou as a southwest bloc; Yunnan's tourism and lifestyle property niche means its data diverges from manufacturing-driven provincial markets and is sensitive to domestic tourism policy.

aCNIREDYNY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Yunnan, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDYNY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of real estate development investment in Yunnan. Tourism-linked property and holiday home segments make Yunnan's YoY somewhat correlated with domestic tourism data and less with industrial employment.
aCNIREDYNY.how_to_use: Monitor alongside Sichuan YoY (aCNIREDSCY) and the national YoY (aCNIREDTCY); a sharp Yunnan underperformance vs Sichuan signals the tourism-property niche is bearing more of the downturn than broader residential markets.

aCNIREDZJ.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Zhejiang
aCNIREDZJ.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date real estate development investment in Zhejiang province. Home to Hangzhou (tech hub), Ningbo (port/manufacturing), and Wenzhou (private enterprise capital), Zhejiang is one of China's wealthiest provinces and a key real estate market watched alongside Jiangsu and Shanghai.
aCNIREDZJ.how_to_use: Construct a Yangtze Delta composite with Jiangsu (aCNIREDJG) and Shanghai (aCNIREDSG); Zhejiang's entrepreneurial private sector and Hangzhou's tech economy mean its housing demand is closely tied to domestic tech sector income and valuation cycles.

aCNIREDZJY.description: Investment of Real Estate Development, Zhejiang, Chg Y/Y
aCNIREDZJY.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of real estate development investment in Zhejiang. Given Hangzhou's tech sector and Zhejiang's high income levels, this YoY is a useful proxy for whether affluent coastal buyers are returning to the market.
aCNIREDZJY.how_to_use: Compare with Jiangsu YoY (aCNIREDJGY) and Shanghai YoY (aCNIREDSGY); a positive Zhejiang YoY ahead of the national average would signal that high-income coastal buyers are leading the recovery, consistent with historical property cycle dynamics.

aCNNPRT.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date number of newly started real estate development projects nationwide. This count-based metric complements floor-space new starts by capturing the number of discrete project initiations, reflecting developer pipeline activity.
aCNNPRT.how_to_use: Compare with planned investment in new projects (aCNNPRPI) to calculate average project size — a decline in project count alongside rising average size signals consolidation toward larger SOE-led projects; track with land acquisition area (aCNRDLAASP) to assess pipeline sequencing.

aCNNPRPI.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date planned investment value of newly started real estate projects. This series captures the committed capital for projects that have broken ground, providing a forward look at construction spending momentum.
aCNNPRPI.how_to_use: Ratio with project count (aCNNPRT) to derive average project investment size — rising average size with fewer projects signals market consolidation; compare against total actual investment (aCNIREDTC) as a commitment-vs-actual conversion check.

aCNPUCT.meaning: Total number of real estate development projects currently under construction at period end. This stock measure captures the overhang of incomplete projects, which became a critical policy concern after the 2021-2023 developer defaults left millions of pre-sold units unfinished.
aCNPUCT.how_to_use: The under-construction project count is the denominator for the 保交楼 (deliver pre-sold homes) policy: a declining count means projects are being completed faster than new ones start, the key indicator that the unfinished-housing overhang is clearing; compare with new starts (aCNNPRT) to track the pipeline flow.

aCNPUCPI.meaning: Planned investment in real estate projects currently under construction — captures the pipeline of developer commitments before completion. Published monthly by NBS as part of the fixed-asset investment framework.
aCNPUCPI.how_to_use: Compare with actual completed investment to gauge developer execution vs. ambition; a widening gap signals financial stress and delivery risk among developers.

aCNHSALEST.meaning: Total sales value of all commercial buildings (residential, commercial office, and other) — the broadest monetary measure of real estate demand. Released monthly by NBS on a cumulative year-to-date basis.
aCNHSALEST.how_to_use: Track YTD growth rate versus prior year to assess the overall revenue recovery for developers; divergence from floor-space sales signals price-mix shifts.

aCNHSALESV.description: Sales value of commercial residential buildings
aCNHSALESV.meaning: Sales value of commercial residential buildings specifically — strips out commercial office and retail to isolate housing market revenue. NBS monthly release, cumulative YTD basis.
aCNHSALESV.how_to_use: Compare against aCNHSALEST to derive the residential share of total property sales; a declining share hints at relative weakness in the housing segment versus commercial property.

aCNCNQBWLM.meaning: China industrial output: New energy bus production. Industrial-sector production data for specific products or sub-sectors.
aCNCNQBWLM.how_to_use: Track for sector-cycle dynamics. China is the world's largest producer of steel, cement, copper, aluminum, and many other industrial commodities. Sustained production declines signal industrial-sector deceleration; sustained increases reflect capacity expansion or commodity-cycle peaks.

aCNCNZKUNM.description: Industrial companies above designated size, profit margin of main business, automobile industry, cumulative
aCNCNZKUNM.meaning: China Industrial: Industrial companies above designated size, profit margin of main business, automobile industry, cumulative. Industrial-sector aggregate or sub-aggregate.
aCNCNZKUNM.how_to_use: Track alongside the broader industrial production data. Above-designated-size firms (>CNY 20M revenue) account for ~70% of industrial output.

aCNCNVCOLM.description: Industrial companies above designated size, profit margin of main business, electrical & electrical industry, year on year, cumulative
aCNCNVCOLM.meaning: Profit margin of main business for industrial companies above designated size (annual revenue ≥ CNY 20M) in the electrical and electronic industry, reported on a year-on-year cumulative basis. Published monthly by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) as part of the Industrial Enterprise Financial Statistics survey, typically released ~27th of the following month. Covers profit-to-revenue ratios across the broad electrical/electronics manufacturing complex.
aCNCNVCOLM.how_to_use: Use to gauge pricing power and cost pass-through dynamics in China's electronics sector — margins above 5-6% signal healthy demand; compression below 3% often precedes capacity rationalization. Compare against the PPI for electronic equipment (aCNCNQTYNM) to separate pricing from cost effects. A sustained YoY deterioration of 1+ percentage point tends to lead export-order softening by 1-2 quarters.

aCNCNLOFHM.description: Industrial companies above designated size, profit margin of main business, heavy mining industry
aCNCNLOFHM.meaning: Profit margin on main business revenue for industrial companies above designated size (annual revenue >CNY 20M) in the heavy mining sector, published monthly by China's National Bureau of Statistics (NBS). Covers ferrous and non-ferrous mining, coal, and stone quarrying as an aggregate. Released with a ~30-day lag alongside the broader industrial profits dataset.
aCNCNLOFHM.how_to_use: A margin below 3% in heavy mining signals acute stress — watch for production cuts by smaller private miners and potential credit events in the sector. Compare against steel PPI (aCNCNNFMEM) to assess pass-through: when downstream prices recover but this margin stays compressed, input cost (energy, labor) pressures dominate. Useful as a lead for NBS mining capex surveys.

aCNCNBEXX.description: Coal consumption of power generation, 6000 kW & above
aCNCNBEXX.meaning: Annual coal consumption at power plants with installed capacity of 6,000 kW and above, published by the NBS in the annual China Energy Statistical Yearbook. Captures the dominant end-use of thermal coal in China, where power generation accounts for roughly 55% of total coal demand (~2.5 billion tonnes/year of the ~4.5 billion tonne total).
aCNCNBEXX.how_to_use: Year-on-year changes reflect electricity demand growth and fuel-switching trends (gas, nuclear, renewables displacing coal). A >5% YoY rise in power-sector coal burn typically precedes tightness in thermal coal spot markets and supports Qinhuangdao benchmark prices. Pair with industrial capacity utilization in coal mining (aCNCNKWDNQ) to assess supply-demand balance.

aCNCNOKUK.description: Electricity consumption coal mining & washing industry, Hubei Province
aCNCNOKUK.meaning: Annual electricity consumed by the coal mining and washing industry in Hubei Province, published by the NBS in provincial energy balance tables. Hubei is a mid-sized coal consumer rather than a major producer (unlike Shanxi or Inner Mongolia), so this series primarily reflects local washing and processing activity rather than raw extraction volume.
aCNCNOKUK.how_to_use: Use as a cross-check on coal processing throughput in central China: rising power consumption with flat raw coal output (aCNCNKMHRM) implies higher washing ratios and improved product quality mix. Divergence from Zhejiang's equivalent (aCNCNJYRB) can highlight regional demand shifts in cleaned coal supply chains feeding Yangtze River industrial clusters.

aCNCNJYRB.description: Electricity consumption coal mining & washing industry, Zhejiang Province
aCNCNJYRB.meaning: Annual electricity consumed by the coal mining and washing industry in Zhejiang Province, published by the NBS in provincial energy statistical tables. Zhejiang has negligible coal mining output, so this series is almost entirely attributable to coal washing and coking plants that process coal transported from northern provinces.
aCNCNJYRB.how_to_use: Rising Zhejiang coal-processing power use alongside falling northern mine-mouth prices implies stronger spot coal flows into the industrialised Yangtze Delta. Useful when triangulated with coal port inventory data and the NBS coal mining capacity utilisation rate (aCNCNKWDNQ) to gauge south-bound coal logistics tightness.

aCNCNDAXM.meaning: Annual electricity consumed by calcium carbide manufacturing firms above designated size in China. Published by NBS as part of the annual industrial energy consumption census, typically released in the first quarter following the reference year. Calcium carbide is an energy-intensive intermediate used in PVC production, acetylene chemistry, and steel desulfurization.
aCNCNDAXM.how_to_use: A proxy for PVC and basic chemical output activity — China produces roughly 25-28 million tonnes of calcium carbide per year, accounting for ~70% of global supply. Rising electricity consumption year-on-year signals strong PVC pipeline demand and construction-linked chemical activity. Cross-reference with NBS PVC output data and coal prices (calcium carbide plants are largely coal-powered) to assess margin pressure.

aCNCNKRDGM.description: Key enterprise electrical steel strip sales volume
aCNCNKRDGM.subcategory: Electrical Steel Strip Sales — Key Enterprises
aCNCNKRDGM.meaning: Monthly sales volume of electrical steel strip (silicon steel/grain-oriented and non-oriented) at key Chinese steel enterprises, compiled by the China Iron and Steel Association (CISA). Electrical steel is a premium, capital-intensive product used in transformer cores and EV motor stators; China achieved near-self-sufficiency in grain-oriented grades around 2015.
aCNCNKRDGM.how_to_use: Electrical steel demand is a direct proxy for power grid investment (State Grid capex cycles) and EV motor production growth — both structural growth areas. A monthly sales run-rate above 800 kt signals robust grid and EV demand. Cross with aCNCNPBMZM (total key-enterprise steel sales) to calculate electrical steel's share; rising share reflects product mix upgrading away from commodity rebar.

aCNCNPBMZM.meaning: Monthly aggregate steel sales volume across all product categories at major Chinese steel enterprises tracked by CISA. This is the broadest sales-side steel indicator from China's key producer cohort, covering roughly 60-65% of national crude steel output, published within two weeks of month-end.
aCNCNPBMZM.how_to_use: The ratio of this series to key-enterprise crude steel production (aCNCNCOSM) yields an implied sell-through rate; below 95% for two consecutive months typically precedes inventory build-up and price weakness. A surprise divergence of >5% from headline NBS crude steel output (aCNPDCRDS) often indicates smaller induction-furnace producers (outside CISA coverage) are running hot.

aCNCNCOSM.meaning: Monthly crude steel production at key enterprises surveyed by CISA — China's most timely steel production indicator, typically released 10-15 days before the official NBS figure. The CISA sample (~200 large mills) accounts for approximately 65% of national output and includes Baowu, HBIS, Shagang, Ansteel, and Jianlong.
aCNCNCOSM.how_to_use: Use as the leading indicator ahead of the NBS release (aCNPDCRDS). When CISA output runs >5% above year-ago levels for three consecutive months, expect NBS to confirm an output surge and watch iron ore futures (DCE i2509) for price compression. Production above 85 Mt/month nationally (implied by scaling CISA data) is historically associated with margin pressure and government output-cap rhetoric.

aCNCNNVFKM.meaning: Monthly total steel production (finished steel, including rolled products) at key CISA-tracked enterprises, distinct from aCNCNCOSM which measures crude steel at the liquid-steel stage. This series captures the downstream transformation step — rolling and forming — providing a picture of finished product supply entering the market.
aCNCNNVFKM.how_to_use: Compare against aCNCNCOSM to derive an implied crude-to-finished yield; when yields fall (more scrap, rejects), product mix is shifting toward lower-value flat/long products. A finished steel output surge without accompanying sales growth (aCNCNPBMZM) signals inventory accumulation at mills — a bearish signal for near-term prices, especially rebar and HRC.

aCNCNPHAM.description: Large-scale steel sales volume of key enterprises
aCNCNPHAM.subcategory: Large Section Steel Sales — Key Enterprises
aCNCNPHAM.meaning: Monthly sales volume of large-section steel products (heavy H-beams, large angle steel, channel sections) at key CISA enterprises. Large sections are primarily consumed in infrastructure — bridges, port cranes, industrial buildings — and in shipbuilding; demand is less sensitive to property cycles than rebar but highly correlated with fixed-asset investment in transport infrastructure.
aCNCNPHAM.how_to_use: When large-section sales outperform total steel sales (aCNCNPBMZM) growth by >3 ppts, it signals infrastructure-led demand is compensating for property weakness — a pattern seen post-2021 as Beijing pivoted to FAI stimulus. Compare with civil steel ship production (aCNCNZGMEM) as another large-section end-use. Monthly volumes above 2 Mt at CISA firms indicate a healthy order book.

aCNCNOGETM.description: Other steel sales volume of key enterprises
aCNCNOGETM.meaning: Monthly sales volume of the residual 'other steel' category at key CISA enterprises — encompassing semi-finished billets, ingots, specialty alloy bars, and niche grades not separately classified. This catch-all category is volatile month-to-month and can spike when mills sell semi-finished billets into the spot market rather than rolling them internally.
aCNCNOGETM.how_to_use: A sharp rise in 'other steel' relative to finished products often signals downstream rolling capacity constraints or downstream demand weakness forcing mills to liquidate semi-finished inventory externally. Cross with billet prices on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE): rising billet prices concurrent with high 'other' sales volumes indicates external rolling mills are absorbing supply at profitable spreads.

aCNCNHEXGM.description: Sales volume of medium & thick steel strips in key enterprises
aCNCNHEXGM.subcategory: Medium & Thick Steel Strip Sales — Key Enterprises
aCNCNHEXGM.meaning: Monthly sales volume of medium and thick steel strip (typically 3–20 mm gauge hot-rolled strip/coil) at key CISA enterprises. This product category feeds pipe mills (oil/gas line pipe, structural tubing), shipbuilding, and heavy machinery — end-markets with distinct cycles from property-driven rebar and wire rod.
aCNCNHEXGM.how_to_use: Track alongside China's shipbuilding order book (aCNCNZGMEM) and pipeline CAPEX cycles. When medium/thick strip sales grow faster than thin flat products, it indicates strength in industrial and energy-sector demand rather than consumer-linked sectors. Monthly run-rates above 3.5 Mt across CISA firms historically align with active shipbuilding seasons (March–October).

aCNCNEGRTM.description: Sales volume of small & medium-sized steel in key enterprises
aCNCNEGRTM.subcategory: Small & Medium Section Steel Sales — Key Enterprises
aCNCNEGRTM.meaning: Monthly sales of small and medium steel sections (rebar, angle iron, channel steel, I-beams in standard sizes) at key CISA enterprises. This is the most property-sensitive steel product category — rebar alone accounts for ~30% of China's finished steel demand, predominantly going into residential construction reinforcement.
aCNCNEGRTM.how_to_use: This series is the clearest steel-to-property linkage: when new home starts collapse (as during 2022–2024 deleveraging), small/medium section sales typically fall 10-20% YoY. A recovery above 0% YoY growth in this series is an early signal of property sector stabilisation. Compare monthly against aCNCNPBMZM to calculate mix share — small/medium sections below 35% of total sales confirms structural shift toward infrastructure/industrial flat products.

aCNCNAZHXM.description: Sales volume of tinplates (belts) of key enterprises
aCNCNAZHXM.meaning: Monthly sales volume of tinplate and tin-coated steel strip at key CISA enterprises. Tinplate is a premium flat-rolled product with a thin tin coating (1–12 g/m²), primarily used for food and beverage cans, aerosol containers, and battery casings. China's tinplate output (~4 Mt/year) is dominated by Baosteel and Shougang.
aCNCNAZHXM.how_to_use: Tinplate sales are driven by consumer packaged goods and beverage can demand — relatively defensive versus construction-linked steels. When tinplate sales hold up while rebar sales fall, it confirms the domestic consumer sector is decoupling from property weakness. Watch for shifts to aluminium can substitution, which has eroded tinplate share globally; a multi-month decline in this series warrants cross-checking aluminium can production data.

aCNCNZHMY.description: Accounts payable by industrial enterprises above designated size, foreign, Hong Kong, Macao & Taiwanese investment enterprises, manufacture of graphite & other non-metallic mineral products
aCNCNZHMY.meaning: Accounts payable balances of foreign, Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwanese-funded industrial enterprises above designated size in the manufacture of graphite and other non-metallic mineral products, sourced from the NBS annual industrial enterprise survey. Frequency is irregular/annual. Captures the credit posture of multinational-linked processors of industrial graphite, carbon electrodes, and specialty ceramics.
aCNCNZHMY.how_to_use: Rising payables without matching revenue growth signals working capital stress at FDI-linked graphite processors — relevant given China's dominance in battery-grade graphite (~80% of global supply) and the growing EV anode material supply chain. Cross with China's battery materials export data; tightening payables can precede procurement slowdowns by Japanese/Korean battery cell makers sourcing from China.
