aCNPDENH.description: Production, Electric power and heat power, Chg Y/Y
aCNPDENH.subcategory: Electric Power and Heat Power — YoY Output Growth
aCNPDENH.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of industrial output for electric power and heat power generation and supply. Published monthly by NBS, typically released ~15th of the following month. China's total electricity generation exceeds 8,000 TWh/year (world's largest), with thermal (coal), hydropower, wind, and solar as main sources. District heating is a significant northern China energy segment.
aCNPDENH.how_to_use: Electric power output growth is the most direct proxy for China's real economy activity — electricity consumption is harder to fake than GDP. Normal range: 4-8% YoY in steady growth; above 10% signals industrial/construction boom; negative growth (COVID-impacted months, policy-directed capacity controls) is a strong recession signal. Cross-check against aCNVAIPELR for series consistency. A 1 ppt change in power output growth historically correlates with roughly 0.3-0.4 ppt change in industrial value-added growth.

aCNPDENHC.description: Production, Electric power and heat power, Chg Y/Y
aCNPDENHC.subcategory: Electric Power and Heat Power — YoY Output Growth (Alt)
aCNPDENHC.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of industrial output for electric power and heat power — an alternative series to aCNPDENH, potentially reflecting NBS classification revision, seasonal adjustment methodology difference, or data vintage change. Published monthly by NBS, typically released ~15th of the following month.
aCNPDENHC.how_to_use: Compare with aCNPDENH to identify any methodological or scope differences. The two series should be nearly identical in most periods — sustained divergence above 0.5 ppts indicates classification changes. Use aCNVAIPELR (Chg Y/Y in electricity value-added) as a third independent check. For macro model purposes, the electricity output series is a key component of China's 'activity nowcast' — used by Li Keqiang's famous three-indicator index alongside rail freight and bank loans.

aCNPDEMEQC.description: Production, Electrical machinery & equipment, Chg Y/Y
aCNPDEMEQC.subcategory: Electrical Machinery & Equipment — YoY Output Growth
aCNPDEMEQC.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of industrial output for electrical machinery and equipment manufacturing. Published monthly by NBS, typically released ~15th of the following month. Covers motors, transformers, generators, switchgear, cables, batteries (including EV batteries — CATL, BYD), and solar inverters. China is the world's largest producer of electrical machinery, accounting for ~35% of global output.
aCNPDEMEQC.how_to_use: Electrical machinery output is the most direct gauge of China's energy transition manufacturing boom — EV battery production, solar inverters, wind generator manufacturing, and HV transformer output all feed into this series. YoY growth above 15% (as seen in 2021-23 when NEV battery output surged) signals strong clean energy capex. CATL's Ningde and Sichuan gigafactories alone contribute materially to monthly swings. Cross-reference with EV production data (CAAM) and solar installation data (NEA) for demand validation.

aCNPDEMEQ.description: Production, Electrical machinery and equipment, Chg Y/Y
aCNPDEMEQ.subcategory: Electrical Machinery and Equipment — YoY Output Growth (Alt)
aCNPDEMEQ.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of industrial output for electrical machinery and equipment — an alternative or earlier series to aCNPDEMEQC, potentially reflecting an NBS classification revision or data vintage difference. Published monthly by NBS, typically ~15th of the following month. The underlying sector encompasses motors, transformers, cables, batteries, and power conversion equipment.
aCNPDEMEQ.how_to_use: Cross-check aCNPDEMEQ against aCNPDEMEQC for consistency. Significant divergence (>2 ppts) suggests an NBS reclassification — most likely related to the 2017 revision when new energy vehicle batteries were reclassified under electrical machinery. For investment research, the current aCNPDEMEQC series is typically more representative given its more recent methodological base. Both series are essential context for Chinese electrical equipment exporters (cables, transformers, motors — major BRI export categories).

aCNVAIPELR.subcategory: Electricity Production — Industrial Value Added YoY Growth
aCNVAIPELR.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of industrial value added for electricity production. Published monthly by NBS as part of the Industrial Value Added by Sub-Sector release, typically ~15th of the following month. Industrial value added differs from physical output volume — it measures the net contribution of the electricity production sector to GDP after subtracting intermediate inputs.
aCNVAIPELR.how_to_use: Value-added based electricity sector growth is used in national accounts construction and cross-sector comparisons. Typically runs 1-2 ppts below or above physical output growth (aCNPDENH/aCNPDENHC) depending on fuel cost dynamics — when input fuel costs are high relative to tariffs, value-added growth lags physical output growth. The gap between value-added and physical output growth is a real-time profitability signal for the power sector. Critical component of China's secondary industry (工业) GDP calculation.

aCNVAMFMHR.description: Production, Ferrous Metals Mining and Dressing, Chg Y/Y
aCNVAMFMHR.subcategory: Ferrous Metals Mining Value-Added Growth (Series A)
aCNVAMFMHR.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in the ferrous metals mining and dressing sector (Series A), published by the NBS. Covers iron ore mining, dressing (beneficiation), and pelletising at above-designated-size domestic Chinese mining operations — the domestic supply side of China's iron feedstock story, competing with seaborne imports from Australia, Brazil, and South Africa.
aCNVAMFMHR.how_to_use: Sustained growth above +5% YoY in ferrous mining value-added signals domestic Chinese iron ore miners are ramping supply — typically a lagged response to high iron ore prices. China domestic ore (~200 Mt/year of useable iron equivalent) is high-cost (~$80-100/t production cost vs. Australian ~$18-22/t) but provides supply security. When this indicator rises while seaborne prices (Platts 62% Fe) fall, domestic mines are substituting for imports and compressing the price floor.

aCNVATMFMR.description: Production, Ferrous Metals Mining and Dressing, Chg Y/Y
aCNVATMFMR.subcategory: Ferrous Metals Mining Value-Added Growth (Series B)
aCNVATMFMR.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of ferrous metals mining and dressing value-added (Series B) — second NBS data series for the same sub-sector as aCNVAMFMHR, potentially using a different enterprise classification, base year, or cumulative methodology. Together, the two series bracket the NBS's official estimate of domestic iron ore mining sector growth.
aCNVATMFMR.how_to_use: Use with aCNVAMFMHR for data quality checks on domestic iron ore supply trends. When both series point to growth deceleration below 0% YoY, it signals China's domestic iron ore miners are under cost/price pressure — typically when seaborne iron ore prices fall below $90/t, undercutting domestic cost structures. Converging negative readings from both series is the most reliable signal of domestic iron supply contraction.

General purpose machinery covers compressors, pumps, valves, gears, rolling bearings, hoisting machinery, and general industrial equipment. Published by NBS; the blank frequency field suggests irregular or discontinued reporting.
aCNPDMACH.how_to_use: Given the blank frequency, treat this series as potentially discontinued — use aCNPDMACC as the primary general machinery production indicator. If historical data exists, aCNPDMACH may provide a longer back-run for trend analysis: general machinery output growth averages 8-12% in expansion phases, 0-3% in slowdowns, and turns negative in severe downturns (2015-16 machinery slump). Cross-reference with machinery sector PPI (aCNCNXIHMM) to distinguish volume vs. price effects on sector revenue.

aCNPDMACC.description: Production, General purpose machinery, Chg Y/Y
aCNPDMACC.subcategory: General Purpose Machinery — YoY Output Growth (Current Series)
aCNPDMACC.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of industrial output for general purpose machinery manufacturing — the active monthly series published by NBS, typically released ~15th of the following month. General purpose machinery encompasses a wide range of industrial capital goods: pumps (dominant in oil/gas, water treatment), compressors (petrochemical, refrigeration), and material handling equipment. China is the world's largest general machinery market and producer.
aCNPDMACC.how_to_use: General machinery output is a reliable mid-cycle indicator of industrial capex activity — growth of 8-12% YoY confirms healthy investment environment. The compressor and pump sub-segments lead the commodity and chemical capex cycles by 3-6 months. Watch for divergence from special purpose machinery (aCNVASPEOR/aCNVAFSPER) — when general machinery growth outpaces special machinery growth, it indicates broad-based manufacturing expansion rather than sector-specific capex. China's general machinery exports (~USD 50 billion/year) make this a global trade flow indicator.

aCNIACT/C.how_to_use: Use alongside headline industrial production for sector cycle analysis. China publishes detailed product-level output in monthly NBS Industrial Statistics. Above-designated-size threshold currently CNY 20 million annual revenue.

aCNPDFEOR.meaning: Monthly raw (run-of-mine) iron ore production in China, published by the NBS. China mines ~1 billion tonnes/year of raw ore, but at very low average iron grades (~25-32% Fe vs. Australian/Brazilian benchmarks at 57-65% Fe), yielding roughly 250 Mt/year of iron units after beneficiation. China's domestic iron ore is the critical swing supply source given the ~$70/t cost premium over seaborne imports.
aCNPDFEOR.how_to_use: Raw ore volumes alone are misleading without grade/yield adjustments — 1 Mt of Chinese raw ore contains roughly 0.28 Mt of iron equivalent vs. 0.62 Mt from Australian Pilbara ore. Use in combination with aCNPDFEORG (growth rate) and aCNVAMFMHR (value-added growth) for a triangulated domestic supply assessment. When raw ore production declines >10% YoY for two consecutive months, assume a ~30 Mt/year equivalent seaborne import replacement requirement — a meaningful demand uplift for Australian and Brazilian miners.

aCNPDFEORG.subcategory: Iron Ore Production — YoY Growth Rate
aCNPDFEORG.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of domestic iron ore (raw ore) production in China, published by the NBS as the companion growth series to aCNPDFEOR (volume). This series provides the rate-of-change signal without requiring base-year normalization, making it directly comparable across time periods and useful for momentum analysis.
aCNPDFEORG.how_to_use: A sustained deceleration to below -5% YoY growth in domestic iron ore production, when seaborne prices are simultaneously above $100/t, indicates Chinese domestic miners are facing structural (geological or environmental) constraints rather than price-driven curtailment — a bullish seaborne iron ore signal. Conversely, growth above +8% YoY with seaborne prices below $90/t signals Chinese miners are defending market share at marginal cost, capping the upside for Australian/Brazilian iron ore prices.

aCNVAAOFCR.description: Production, Manufacture of measuring instruments and machinery, Chg Y/Y
aCNVAAOFCR.subcategory: Measuring Instruments and Machinery — YoY Output Growth (Series A)
aCNVAAOFCR.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of industrial output for measuring instruments and machinery manufacturing. Published monthly by NBS, typically ~15th of the following month. Covers industrial measurement equipment: process instruments (pressure, temperature, flow sensors), laboratory instruments, surveying equipment, navigation instruments, and quality inspection machinery. This is a high-tech sub-sector closely linked to industrial automation and quality control investment.
aCNVAAOFCR.how_to_use: Measuring instruments output is a high-frequency indicator of industrial automation investment depth — sustained growth above 10% YoY reflects factory digitization and smart manufacturing capex. China's instrument sector has been strategically targeted under Made in China 2025, aiming to reduce imports of high-precision measurement equipment. Cross-reference with aCNVAOFCIR (the paired series) to confirm trend direction. Import substitution progress can be assessed by comparing domestic production growth with instrument import data (aCNCIMPB).

aCNVAOFCIR.description: Production, Manufacture of measuring instruments and machinery, Chg Y/Y
aCNVAOFCIR.subcategory: Measuring Instruments and Machinery — YoY Output Growth (Series B)
aCNVAOFCIR.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of industrial output for measuring instruments and machinery manufacturing — an alternative series to aCNVAAOFCR, likely reflecting an NBS classification revision or different aggregation method. Published monthly by NBS. Covers the same instruments sector (process control, precision measurement, lab instruments) with potentially different enterprise coverage or methodological vintage.
aCNVAOFCIR.how_to_use: Use in conjunction with aCNVAAOFCR — consistent readings confirm data robustness; persistent divergence reveals methodology differences worth investigating. The instruments sector is a proxy for high-tech industrial capex: China's 14th Five-Year Plan specifically targets 60% domestic self-sufficiency in core industrial measurement equipment by 2025. Strong output growth (15%+ YoY) here often precedes improvements in broader factory automation sector metrics. Semiconductor fabs, battery plants, and pharma manufacturers are the largest buyers.

aCNPDMNSST.meaning: Monthly production of medium and small section steel (rebar, small angles, small H-beams, channels in standard commodity sizes) in China, published by the NBS with irregular frequency. This product category is the most property-sensitive steel grade — rebar (threaded steel bar for concrete reinforcement) alone represents ~25-28% of China's finished steel consumption and is overwhelmingly used in residential construction.
aCNPDMNSST.how_to_use: The single most direct steel-to-property-market linkage in China's data. When this series falls >15% YoY, property new starts are almost certainly contracting sharply — use as an early read on residential fixed-asset investment before official FAI data. Compare with the CISA small/medium steel sales data (aCNCNEGRTM) to compute implied inventory: production minus sales indicates whether mills are building up stocks of these loss-making grades.

aCNVANMETR.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in the metal products manufacturing sector (Series A), published by the NBS. Metal products (NBS industry C33) includes metal structural components, metal containers, hardware, metal tools, and spring products — all downstream of steel and aluminum primary production, serving construction, auto, machinery, and consumer goods.
aCNVANMETR.how_to_use: Metal products value-added growth is a downstream steel demand quality indicator — it tells you not just whether steel production is rising but whether that steel is being transformed into value-added manufactured products. Growth above +6% YoY in this series alongside flat steel production implies downstream fabrication efficiency gains (yield improvements, product mix upgrading). Cross with aCNVAMETVR (Series B) for data reliability, and use the composite to assess whether China's manufacturing base is moving up the value chain.

aCNVAMETVR.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in metal products manufacturing (Series B) — second NBS series for the same sub-sector as aCNVANMETR. The two series may differ in enterprise classification scope (e.g., whether repair services are included), base-year deflation methodology, or data vintage.
aCNVAMETVR.how_to_use: Use in tandem with aCNVANMETR as a quality-control pair for the metal products sector. Consistent above-10% growth across both series indicates the downstream steel fabrication sector is in a strong expansion phase — supportive of sustained or growing flat-steel demand (HRC, CRC, coated grades) from structural steel fabricators, auto parts stampers, and equipment manufacturers. Persistent divergence between the two series warrants investigation of methodology changes before using in econometric models.

aCNCMCE.meaning: Monthly production of mobile communication equipment (primarily smartphones) by industrial enterprises above designated size in China. Published monthly by NBS, typically ~15th of the following month. China produces roughly 1.5-1.8 billion mobile phones per year — approximately 75% of global smartphone supply. Major production concentrated in Guangdong (Foxconn Shenzhen, OPPO, vivo), Chongqing (Foxconn), and Zhengzhou (Foxconn largest iPhone plant globally).
aCNCMCE.how_to_use: China smartphone production is a direct supply-chain indicator for Apple, Samsung (Korean components), and domestic brands (Xiaomi, OPPO, Huawei, vivo). Normal monthly output: 110-150 million units. A drop below 100 million/month signals either demand weakness or supply disruption (COVID factory lockdowns in Q4 2022 at Zhengzhou were among the most market-impactful disruptions in recent memory). Cross-reference Foxconn Taiwan revenue disclosures and iPhone upgrade cycle calendars for validation.

aCNVAMNFIR.description: Production, Non-Ferrous Metals Mining and Dressing, Chg Y/Y
aCNVAMNFIR.subcategory: Non-Ferrous Metals Mining Value-Added Growth (Series A)
aCNVAMNFIR.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in the non-ferrous metals mining and dressing sector (Series A), published by the NBS. Covers copper, aluminum (bauxite), lead, zinc, nickel, tin, molybdenum, and rare earth mining and beneficiation at above-designated-size Chinese mining operations — the upstream supply side of China's base metals complex.
aCNVAMNFIR.how_to_use: A reliable leading indicator for domestic non-ferrous metal supply: growth above +8% YoY implies Chinese miners are aggressively expanding upstream supply, which typically leads to smelter output growth (aCNVAPNMPR) by 3-6 months and ultimately base metal price pressure if not absorbed by demand. When this series contracts during periods of high LME prices, it signals genuine supply constraints at the mining/beneficiation stage — structurally bullish for copper and zinc.

aCNVAQMNFR.description: Production, Non-Ferrous Metals Mining and Dressing, Chg Y/Y
aCNVAQMNFR.subcategory: Non-Ferrous Metals Mining Value-Added Growth (Series B)
aCNVAQMNFR.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of non-ferrous metals mining and dressing value-added (Series B) — second NBS data series complementing aCNVAMNFIR. Covers the same upstream non-ferrous mining sector (copper, lead, zinc, bauxite, rare earths) and may reflect different enterprise coverage, statistical vintage, or cumulative vs. current-period methodology.
aCNVAQMNFR.how_to_use: Cross-validate with aCNVAMNFIR: if both series are below 0% YoY, the signal is unambiguous — China's upstream non-ferrous mine supply is contracting, providing support for LME base metals prices as concentrate availability tightens. When Series B is growing while Series A is flat or negative, check whether the divergence reflects enterprise scope differences (state-owned vs. all-ownership) before drawing macro conclusions.

aCNVAMMOBR.description: Production, Non-Metal Minerals Mining and Dressing, Chg Y/Y
aCNVAMMOBR.subcategory: Non-Metal Minerals Mining Value-Added Growth (Series A)
aCNVAMMOBR.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in non-metallic mineral mining and dressing (Series A), published by the NBS. This sector (NBS industry B10-B12) covers limestone, granite, sand/gravel, gypsum, kaolin, phosphate rock, and coal gangue mining — inputs to cement, glass, ceramics, fertiliser, and construction materials industries, all of which are intensive consumers of energy and logistics.
aCNVAMMOBR.how_to_use: Non-metal minerals mining growth is a leading indicator for cement and construction materials demand — when this series accelerates above +6% YoY, cement producers are drawing down limestone quarry inventories ahead of construction season (March–October). Compare with aCNVAJMMOR (Series B) for triangulation. The construction sector link makes this a secondary indicator for rebar and structural steel demand — expect a 4-8 week lead-lag between non-metal mining acceleration and rebar demand pickup.

aCNVAJMMOR.description: Production, Non-Metal Minerals Mining and Dressing, Chg Y/Y
aCNVAJMMOR.subcategory: Non-Metal Minerals Mining Value-Added Growth (Series B)
aCNVAJMMOR.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of non-metallic mineral mining and dressing value-added (Series B) — second NBS series for the same sector as aCNVAMMOBR. Both cover the quarrying and processing of industrial minerals used in construction (limestone, sand, gravel), chemicals (phosphate, sulfur), and advanced materials (graphite, industrial diamonds, high-purity quartz).
aCNVAJMMOR.how_to_use: Where aCNVAMMOBR and this series diverge significantly, investigate whether the difference reflects reclassification of enterprises between non-metal mining and non-metal products manufacturing. High-purity quartz and industrial graphite within the non-metal minerals sector are of increasing strategic interest (semiconductor supply chains); a spike in this series alongside rising electronics exports (aCNCEXBA) may reflect graphite electrode or synthetic quartz expansion beyond just construction aggregates.

aCNPMNMMPC.description: Production, Non-metal mineral products, Chg Y/Y
aCNPMNMMPC.subcategory: Non-Metal Mineral Products Value-Added Growth (Series A)
aCNPMNMMPC.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in the non-metallic mineral products manufacturing sector (Series A), published by the NBS. This sector (NBS industry C30) covers cement, flat glass, ceramics, refractory materials, stone processing, and mineral-wool insulation — all heavily property-construction and infrastructure-linked.
aCNPMNMMPC.how_to_use: Cement and glass production, which dominate this sector, are the most coincident indicators of China's construction activity. When aCNPMNMMPC falls below -5% YoY for two consecutive months, property new starts are almost certainly in severe contraction — a strong bearish signal for rebar and long steel. The glass component tracks property completion (windows/glazing are installed at near-completion stage) rather than starts, providing a different phase of the construction cycle signal.

aCNPDMNMMP.description: Production, Non-metal mineral products, Chg Y/Y
aCNPDMNMMP.subcategory: Non-Metal Mineral Products Value-Added Growth (Series B)
aCNPDMNMMP.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of non-metallic mineral products manufacturing value-added (Series B) — second NBS series for the same sector as aCNPMNMMPC. Both cover cement, glass, ceramics, and refractory products; methodological differences between the two series are typical of NBS dual-series reporting and may reflect revised industrial census base years.
aCNPDMNMMP.how_to_use: Use with aCNPMNMMPC as a dual-series cement/glass demand indicator; when both series converge below zero, the confidence level on construction sector contraction is high. The refractory materials sub-component within this sector is directly linked to steel furnace maintenance cycles — rising refractories output (when disaggregated) implies steel mills are rebuilding blast furnace linings, a signal of production restart or capacity expansion intent.

aCNVAMOOAR.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in other mining sectors (Series A), published by the NBS. 'Other mining' (NBS industry B09 or similar residual category) captures rare earth mining, potash mining, gemstone extraction, and specialty mineral extraction not classified under coal, ferrous, or non-ferrous mining — including China's critical minerals supply chains.
aCNVAMOOAR.how_to_use: This series is increasingly relevant as a rare earth and critical minerals proxy — China controls ~85% of global rare earth mining and processing, and NBS 'other mining' captures much of this activity. A sustained rise above +10% YoY in this series, concurrent with rare earth export quota announcements, signals China is expanding rare earth capacity ahead of anticipated export controls — the pattern seen in 2023-2024 before tungsten/germanium/gallium restrictions.

aCNVARMOOR.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of 'other mining' value-added (Series B) — second NBS series complementing aCNVAMOOAR for the residual mining categories beyond coal, ferrous, and non-ferrous metals. Includes rare earth, potash, and specialty mineral extraction; may also capture artisanal gold mining and salt production depending on NBS scope definitions.
aCNVARMOOR.how_to_use: Use alongside aCNVAMOOAR for signal reliability on China's critical minerals mining sector. When both 'other mining' series are rising strongly in a period when official export quotas for rare earths (REE) are being tightened, it suggests China is building domestic rare earth stockpiles before restricting exports — historically a precursor to price spikes in terbium, dysprosium, and neodymium markets used in EV motors and wind turbines.

The 'other' category has historically included significant seamless pipe volumes serving oil and gas OCTG markets.
aCNPDROLST.how_to_use: When 'other rolled steel' production surges, look for simultaneous strength in China's oil/gas OCTG orders — domestic CNPC/CNOOC exploration drilling programs are the primary driver. A 10% YoY rise in this series during periods of elevated Brent crude prices (above $80/bbl) is a reliable signal that China's energy sector is ramping drilling capex. Cross with aCNPDPLST (plated steel sheet) to distinguish energy-sector vs. consumer-sector flat products growth within the broader rolled steel complex.

aCNPDPIGI.meaning: Monthly national pig iron production in China, published by the NBS. Pig iron is the molten iron output from blast furnaces (BF), produced at a ~1.1:1 ratio from sinter/pellet iron ore and coke/coal; nearly all of China's ~850-870 Mt/year pig iron is immediately converted to crude steel in BOFs. This series is effectively a real-time blast furnace utilisation indicator.
aCNPDPIGI.how_to_use: Pig iron production tracks the BF operating rate (~3,000 blast furnaces in China). Monthly output above 75 Mt implies national BF capacity utilisation above 85% — near full utilisation. A drop of >5 Mt month-on-month typically signals deliberate production cuts (either environmental curtailment orders or mill-level margin-driven shutdowns) and has historically led iron ore futures (DCE i2509) to fall $5-10/t within 2 weeks. Ratio to crude steel (aCNPDCRDS): BF-BOF route should be ~0.83 pig iron/crude steel — divergence signals EAF share shift.

aCNPBIREMEP.description: Production, Printing and Record Medium Reproduction, Chg Y/Y
aCNPBIREMEP.subcategory: Printing & Recording Media Value-Added Growth (Series A)
aCNPBIREMEP.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in printing and recording media reproduction (Series A), published by the NBS. This sector (NBS industry C23) encompasses commercial printing, books/periodicals printing, and optical media reproduction — it consumes tinplate (ink cans), aluminium printing plates, and specialty paper. Included in the metals/mining batch as part of a broader NBS industrial dataset.
aCNPBIREMEP.how_to_use: Treat as a cross-sector demand indicator for metallic packaging materials — specifically tinplate (aCNCNAZHXM) and aluminum foil. When printing and media sector value-added decelerates sharply, it signals declining consumption of aluminium printing plates and tinplate ink cans. Use primarily as a benchmark for comparing sector-specific cost trends (aCNCNKYRFM, aCNCNPHJNM) rather than as a standalone metals demand driver.

aCNVAPRISR.description: Production, Printing and Record Medium Reproduction, Chg Y/Y
aCNVAPRISR.subcategory: Printing & Recording Media Value-Added Growth (Series B)
aCNVAPRISR.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of printing and recording media reproduction value-added (Series B) — second NBS data series complementing aCNPBIREMEP for the same sub-sector. As with other dual NBS series pairs, the two series may reflect different enterprise samples, deflation vintages, or cumulative vs. current-period calculation methodology.
aCNVAPRISR.how_to_use: Cross-validate with aCNPBIREMEP to confirm trend direction; both series declining simultaneously provides a cleaner read on consumer media/packaging sector softness. Of most relevance to metals analysts as a tinplate demand proxy: if printing value-added falls >8% YoY in both series, expect downstream aluminium plate and tinplate orders to weaken within 4-6 weeks, providing marginal downside for coated steel sheet (aCNPDCSTEEL) prices.

aCNPDTREQC.description: Production, Railway, shipping, aerospace & other transport equipments, Chg Y/Y
aCNPDTREQC.subcategory: Railway, Shipping, Aerospace & Other Transport Equipment — YoY Output Growth
aCNPDTREQC.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of industrial output for railway, shipping, aerospace and other transport equipment manufacturing. Published monthly by NBS, typically ~15th of the following month. Covers CRRC rail rolling stock (world's largest train manufacturer), Jiangnan/COSCO shipbuilding (world #1 shipbuilder), AVIC aircraft, and satellite/space equipment. Driven by domestic rail network expansion and BRI-linked exports.
aCNPDTREQC.how_to_use: Transport equipment output growth above 10% YoY signals an active infrastructure investment cycle — China's HSR network expansion (current ~43,000 km) and metro system build-outs drive CRRC order books. Shipbuilding surges (South Korea competition important context) reflect global trade recovery and naval vessel construction. Compare with aCNPDTRNEQ for series consistency. Rail and ship delivery lead times (18-36 months) mean this output series lags order data by 1.5-3 years — use new order data as a forward indicator.

aCNPDTRNEQ.description: Production, Railway, shipping, aerospace & other transport equipments, Chg Y/Y
aCNPDTRNEQ.subcategory: Railway, Shipping, Aerospace & Other Transport Equipment — YoY Output Growth (Alt)
aCNPDTRNEQ.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of industrial output for railway, shipping, aerospace and other transport equipment manufacturing — an alternative series to aCNPDTREQC, possibly reflecting an NBS classification or aggregation revision. Published monthly by NBS, typically ~15th of the following month.
aCNPDTRNEQ.how_to_use: Cross-check aCNPDTRNEQ against aCNPDTREQC for confirmation of trend direction. The two series should broadly align — notable divergence may indicate that one includes military/aerospace production classified separately in a revised industrial taxonomy. This sector is particularly relevant for tracking China's naval expansion (Type 075 amphibious assault ships, Type 055 destroyers) and space program (Long March rockets) — both are captured in 'other transport equipment' under NBS classification, adding a defense/space dimension often overlooked in purely commercial analysis.

aCNVALREPR.description: Production, Repair of metal products, machinery and equipment, Chg Y/Y
aCNVALREPR.subcategory: Metal Products & Machinery Repair Value-Added Growth (Series A)
aCNVALREPR.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in the repair of metal products, machinery, and equipment (Series A), published by the NBS. This sector captures maintenance, overhaul, and refurbishment services for industrial metal products and machinery — a counter-cyclical activity that tends to accelerate when new capex is constrained but operational equipment must be maintained.
aCNVALREPR.how_to_use: Repair sector growth above +10% YoY in a period of declining new-machinery production (aCNCNHAFYM, aCNCNPCIHM) suggests industrial enterprises are extending asset lives rather than investing in new equipment — a typical late-cycle or downturn indicator for metals demand. Conversely, when repair activity and new equipment production both rise simultaneously, it signals a full industrial upcycle where both maintenance backlogs and new capacity are being addressed.

aCNVAREPVR.description: Production, Repair of metal products, machinery and equipment, Chg Y/Y
aCNVAREPVR.subcategory: Metal Products & Machinery Repair Value-Added Growth (Series B)
aCNVAREPVR.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of metal products and machinery repair value-added (Series B) — second NBS series for the same sub-sector as aCNVALREPR. The repair/maintenance sector for metal equipment is strategically important in China as ageing capital stock in coal mines, steel mills, and metal processing plants requires increasing maintenance intensity.
aCNVAREPVR.how_to_use: Use in conjunction with aCNVALREPR for a complete picture of China's industrial maintenance cycle. When repair value-added growth accelerates in sectors like coal mining equipment (cross-check with aCNCNKWDNQ) or steel mill rolls and housings (cross-check with aCNCNPGIUM cast steel), it implies existing capacity is being sweated rather than replaced — supportive of specialty steel and cast steel demand for maintenance applications.

aCNPDSTPR.meaning: Monthly national rolled steel production in China, published by the NBS — the finished steel output indicator, downstream of crude steel (aCNPDCRDS) after hot-rolling, cold-rolling, and forming operations. China produces ~1,300-1,400 Mt/year of rolled products (more than crude steel output because rolling converts some imported semi-finished billets); major product categories include bar/rod, wire, structural sections, sheet/plate, and strip.
aCNPDSTPR.how_to_use: Rolled steel production exceeding crude steel (aCNPDCRDS) confirms China is importing semi-finished billets for rolling — check trade data for billet import volumes (HS 7207). The rolled-to-crude ratio persistently above 1.05 is unusual and signals domestic rolling capacity is being run on imported semis. Monthly rolled output above 120 Mt is the 'hot' threshold that typically triggers domestic steel price weakness as finished product supply overwhelms seasonal demand.

aCNPDPLST.description: Production, Rolled steel, plated steel sheet/strip
aCNPDPLST.meaning: Monthly production of rolled steel plated sheet and strip (hot-dip galvanised, electrogalvanised, and tin-plated flat products) in China, published by the NBS with irregular frequency. Plated steel is a premium flat product combining base steel's structural properties with corrosion or aesthetic coatings; consumed in automotive body panels (~30% of demand), white goods, construction roofing, and packaging.
aCNPDPLST.how_to_use: When plated sheet production rises while bare HRC or CRC output is flat, it signals mills are adding coating capacity to capture premium pricing — a margin-improvement strategy typical of steel pricing downturns. Track auto sector production schedules (CAAM monthly auto output data) as the primary demand driver for hot-dip galvanised grades. Plated steel production falling >8% YoY with auto production flat implies coating line maintenance or input (zinc) cost-driven curtailments.

aCNPSNPF.description: Production, Smelting & pressing of ferrous metals, Chg Y/Y
aCNPSNPF.subcategory: Ferrous Metals Smelting & Pressing Value-Added Growth (Series A)
aCNPSNPF.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in ferrous metals smelting and pressing (Series A), published by the NBS. This sector (NBS industry C31) covers the full steelmaking chain from liquid crude steel through rolling and finishing — the value-added spine of China's steel industry, from Baowu, HBIS, Shagang, Ansteel, and ~200 other significant producers.
aCNPSNPF.how_to_use: This is the most comprehensive value-added indicator for China's steel industry — it captures the entire BF-BOF-rolling chain rather than just crude steel volumes (aCNPDCRDS). When this growth rate exceeds crude steel volume growth, it signals product mix upgrading (more high-value specialty/flat products) or efficiency gains — both bullish for steel sector margins. Growth below -3% YoY while crude steel volumes are flat implies pricing/margin collapse — typical of 2015-2016 style overcapacity crises.

aCNPSNPFC.description: Production, Smelting & pressing of ferrous metals, Chg Y/Y
aCNPSNPFC.subcategory: Ferrous Metals Smelting & Pressing Value-Added Growth (Series B)
aCNPSNPFC.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of ferrous metals smelting and pressing value-added (Series B) — second NBS series for the same steelmaking sector as aCNPSNPF. As with other dual NBS series, differences may arise from enterprise classification scope, base-year methodology, or cumulative vs. current-period calculation approaches in the NBS's industrial census and annual survey reconciliation process.
aCNPSNPFC.how_to_use: Cross-validate with aCNPSNPF: when both series are below -5% YoY, the ferrous metals value chain is clearly under severe margin pressure — a systemic signal rather than measurement noise. The dual-series approach is especially important during NBS rebasing years (2015, 2019) when methodological changes can temporarily create large apparent divergences. Strong convergence between Series A and B above +5% YoY is the most reliable green light for overweight Chinese steel sector positions.

aCNVAPNMPR.description: Production, Smelting and Pressing of Non-Ferrous Metals, Chg Y/Y
aCNVAPNMPR.subcategory: Non-Ferrous Metals Smelting & Pressing Value-Added Growth (Series A)
aCNVAPNMPR.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in non-ferrous metals smelting and pressing (Series A), published by the NBS. This sector (NBS industry C32) covers the smelting and refining of copper, aluminum, lead, zinc, nickel, tin, and precious metals, plus the downstream rolling and forming of these metals into sheets, rods, wires, and profiles. China dominates this sector globally (~55% of world non-ferrous smelting capacity).
aCNVAPNMPR.how_to_use: This is THE top-level value-added indicator for China's non-ferrous sector — a primary input for global base metals demand models. Growth above +6% YoY signals China's non-ferrous supply chain is expanding production faster than domestic demand, typically an LME price headwind. Cross-check with LME inventory builds: rising aCNVAPNMPR + rising LME stocks is the most bearish combination for base metals. Cross with aCNCNDQMEM (copper) and aCNCNKRWSM (alumina) to decompose by metal.

aCNVACPNMR.description: Production, Smelting and Pressing of Non-Ferrous Metals, Chg Y/Y
aCNVACPNMR.subcategory: Non-Ferrous Metals Smelting & Pressing Value-Added Growth (Series B)
aCNVACPNMR.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of non-ferrous metals smelting and pressing value-added (Series B) — second NBS series complementing aCNVAPNMPR for the same sector. This series may use different enterprise classification, an alternative price deflator, or a different statistical base year compared to Series A, producing the characteristic NBS dual-series divergence pattern.
aCNVACPNMR.how_to_use: Use alongside aCNVAPNMPR as a signal quality checker for China's non-ferrous metals sector. Persistent divergence between the two series typically indicates an NBS rebasing event — the NBS revises its industrial census base approximately every 5 years (2015, 2020), creating temporary measurement inconsistencies. Both series contracting below -4% YoY simultaneously is the cleanest signal of a genuine Chinese non-ferrous metals industry downturn — relevant for global copper, aluminum, and zinc price outlooks.

aCNVASPEOR.description: Production, Special Purpose Equipment Manufacturing, Chg Y/Y
aCNVASPEOR.subcategory: Special Purpose Equipment Manufacturing — YoY Output Growth
aCNVASPEOR.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of industrial output for special purpose equipment manufacturing. Published monthly by NBS, typically ~15th of the following month. Special purpose equipment includes mining machinery, metallurgical equipment, construction machinery (XCMG, Sany, Zoomlion, LGMG), agricultural machinery (LOVOL, YANMAR China), and environmental protection/pollution control equipment. China leads globally in construction machinery production.
aCNVASPEOR.how_to_use: Special equipment output is the most direct proxy for China's infrastructure investment cycle. Growth above 12% YoY typically coincides with FAI in infrastructure above 5% YoY; contraction below -5% signals capex slump. Excavator monthly sales (CCMA, typically 15,000-25,000 units in upcycle, 8,000-12,000 in downcycle) correlate closely. Environmental equipment sub-segment (wastewater treatment, air pollution control) shows secular growth regardless of the broader construction cycle — driven by $400B+ environmental compliance spending since 2013.

aCNVAFSPER.description: Production, Special purpose machinery, Chg Y/Y
aCNVAFSPER.subcategory: Special Purpose Machinery — YoY Output Growth
aCNVAFSPER.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of industrial output for special purpose machinery — an alternative or related series to aCNVASPEOR, potentially reflecting a different aggregation scope or classification vintage. Published monthly by NBS. May distinguish 'special purpose machinery' (专用设备) from the broader 'special purpose equipment manufacturing' (专用设备制造业) at different levels of the NBS industry taxonomy.
aCNVAFSPER.how_to_use: Cross-reference aCNVAFSPER against aCNVASPEOR to identify any scope difference. In NBS taxonomy, 专用设备 is used at different hierarchy levels; the series capturing the more granular sub-category (e.g., excluding environmental machinery) may show different cyclical behavior. When aCNVAFSPER consistently outpaces aCNVASPEOR, it suggests that a specific high-growth sub-segment (e.g., semiconductor equipment, medical devices, or agricultural machinery) is driving the aggregate, while environmental equipment may be relatively weaker.

aCNVALSUMR.description: Production, Support activities of mining, Chg Y/Y
aCNVALSUMR.subcategory: Mining Support Activities Value-Added Growth (Series A)
aCNVALSUMR.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in support activities for mining (Series A), published by the NBS. Mining support services (NBS industry B11 or equivalent) include mine drilling, blasting, mine shaft sinking, mine dewatering, and mining equipment rental — services intensive in specialty steel (drill pipe, casing, drill bits), explosives, and advanced machinery.
aCNVALSUMR.how_to_use: Mining support services act as a leading indicator for future mining production volume: when support activity accelerates 3-6 months ahead of actual output data, it confirms new mine capacity is being prepared for commissioning. Growth above +15% YoY in this series alongside strong non-ferrous mining confidence (aCNCNADZYQ) signals a significant capacity expansion cycle is underway — typically translates into supply pressure for target metals 12-18 months later.

aCNVASUMTR.description: Production, Support activities of mining, Chg Y/Y
aCNVASUMTR.subcategory: Mining Support Activities Value-Added Growth (Series B)
aCNVASUMTR.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of mining support activities value-added (Series B) — second NBS series for the same sector as aCNVALSUMR. Both series track the service sector surrounding China's mining industry: drilling contractors, blasting specialists, mine ventilation engineers, and mining software providers — all of which respond to upstream mining capex cycles.
aCNVASUMTR.how_to_use: Cross-validate with aCNVALSUMR: dual-series confirmation of above-10% YoY growth in mining support activities indicates the mining industry is at the peak of a capital deployment cycle. When both support series contract simultaneously with raw material prices (aCNCNNFMEM, aCNPPIAR) still elevated, it signals mine operators are cutting capex while hoping to hold output — a recipe for future supply shortfall and price recovery 12-24 months ahead.

aCNPDTHSTP.meaning: Monthly production of thick steel plate (heavy plate, typically >8 mm gauge hot-rolled flat steel) in China, published by the NBS with irregular frequency. Thick plate is a capital-intensive specialty flat product consumed in shipbuilding (~35% of demand), bridges and large steel structures, pressure vessels (boilers, chemical reactors), offshore platforms, and heavy machinery. China is the world's largest thick plate producer (~25 Mt/year).
aCNPDTHSTP.how_to_use: Thick plate production is the primary shipbuilding and heavy engineering cycle indicator in China's steel data. When production rises >10% YoY alongside strong civil steel ship output (aCNCNZGMEM), it confirms a genuine shipbuilding super-cycle rather than a temporary scheduling effect. Korean and Japanese shipyards also consume Chinese thick plate — monitor export steel flows alongside domestic production for the split between domestic and export-driven demand.
