aCNCNDWGHM.meaning: Monthly production of automotive equipment (manufacturing machinery and tooling for vehicle production lines) by industrial enterprises above designated size. Published monthly by NBS, typically released ~15th of the following month. Covers stamping presses, welding robots, painting equipment, assembly-line conveyor systems, and body-in-white production equipment used in auto assembly plants.
aCNCNDWGHM.how_to_use: Automotive equipment production is a capital expenditure indicator for China's car manufacturing industry — an active production line retooling wave for EV platforms generates significant equipment orders. Typically, automotive equipment output spikes 18-24 months ahead of new model launch cycles. Chinese EV brands (BYD, NIO, Li Auto, AITO) all completed major plant expansions in 2022-24, driving a multi-year equipment investment cycle. Compare with aCNPDAUMOT for the paired automotive equipment series and cross-reference with CAAM vehicle production data.

aCNCNUQBGM.description: Production, cement special equipment, Anhui Province
aCNCNUQBGM.subcategory: Cement Special Equipment Output — Anhui Province
aCNCNUQBGM.meaning: Monthly production of cement special equipment (kilns, mills, separators, conveyor systems for cement plants) by enterprises above designated size in Anhui Province. Published by NBS Anhui Bureau monthly, typically in the second or third week of the following month. Anhui hosts major cement equipment manufacturers, connected to the province's large cement and construction materials industry (Conch Cement, China's largest cement producer, is Anhui-headquartered).
aCNCNUQBGM.how_to_use: Cement equipment output from Anhui is directly linked to Conch Cement's domestic capacity expansion and BRI-linked cement plant exports. China has exported cement plant turnkey projects to Africa, Southeast Asia, and South Asia — Anhui manufacturers are major suppliers. Growth of 15%+ YoY in cement equipment typically precedes global cement production capacity additions by 12-18 months. Decline in output signals either domestic overcapacity rationalization or BRI project pipeline slowdown.

aCNCNZGMEM.units: DWT (deadweight tonnes) or Number of vessels
aCNCNZGMEM.meaning: Monthly production of civil steel ships in China, published by the NBS. China has been the world's largest shipbuilder since 2010 (~50% global market share in DWT, ~60% in orders in 2023-2024); major yards include CSSC (China State Shipbuilding Corp), CSIC, Yangzijiang Shipbuilding, and Cosco Shipping Heavy Industry. A civil steel ship is one of the most steel-intensive manufactured goods (~15-20 kt of steel per Capesize bulk carrier).
aCNCNZGMEM.how_to_use: Ship production is the anchor demand driver for thick plate (aCNPDTHSTP) and medium/heavy structural steel. The current 2023-2025 shipbuilding boom (driven by LNG vessel orders, container replacement, and green-shipping regulations) is a multi-year thick plate demand uplift — sustaining high production figures here for 3+ consecutive years is a structural bullish signal for shipbuilding steel grades. Cross with order book data (Clarksons Research): a ratio of order book/deliveries above 3 years confirms sustained forward demand.

aCNCNDXHEM.description: Production, concrete machinery, Industrial Production & Utilization, Monthly, National Bureau of Statistics of China
aCNCNDXHEM.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of concrete machinery production (concrete mixers, pump trucks, batching plants, and transit mixers) by industrial enterprises above designated size. Published monthly by NBS, typically released ~15th of the following month. China's concrete machinery sector is led by SANY, Zoomlion, and XCMG — globally dominant producers that export to over 100 countries.
aCNCNDXHEM.how_to_use: Concrete machinery output growth is one of the most reliable leading indicators for China's fixed asset investment in construction. Growth above 15% YoY typically precedes a construction boom by 3-6 months; decline below -10% signals cement demand contraction 2-3 months ahead. SANY's monthly mixer truck sales data (reported independently) provides weekly cross-check. The 2021 construction machinery super-cycle saw growth peak above 50% YoY; the 2022-23 downturn saw -30% prints — an extreme range that mirrors real estate sector volatility directly.

aCNCNBNRQM.description: Production, concrete machinery, Volume, Industrial Production & Utilization, Monthly, National Bureau of Statistics of China
aCNCNBNRQM.meaning: Monthly production volume (absolute level) of concrete machinery (concrete mixers, pump trucks, batching plants) by industrial enterprises above designated size. Published monthly by NBS. This is the levels companion to aCNCNDXHEM (which shows the YoY growth rate), allowing calculation of absolute production scale rather than just the rate of change.
aCNCNBNRQM.how_to_use: Use the absolute production level to construct longer-run trend analysis and identify where the current cycle sits relative to peak production. Peak monthly concrete machinery output reached ~25,000-30,000 units in the 2020-21 super-cycle; a structural level of 15,000-20,000 units represents the 'new normal' given property sector deleveraging. The level series also enables comparison of China's production share of global concrete equipment — China typically accounts for 40-50% of global concrete mixer output. Combine with aCNCNDXHEM for a complete picture.

aCNCNBOLRM.meaning: Monthly production of cotton processing machinery (ginning machines, carding machines, spinning frames, weaving looms for cotton textile processing) by industrial enterprises above designated size. Published monthly by NBS, typically released ~15th of the following month. China's cotton textile machinery sector is concentrated in Jiangsu (Jintan, Wuxi machinery clusters), Henan, and Xinjiang — the latter as China's largest cotton-growing region.
aCNCNBOLRM.how_to_use: Cotton processing machinery output correlates with textile industry capex cycles and reflects cotton production volumes (Xinjiang accounts for ~85% of Chinese cotton). Equipment output surges often accompany new Xinjiang cotton processing capacity additions — geopolitically sensitive given international scrutiny. Cross-reference with Xinjiang cotton planting area (NBS agricultural data) and global cotton prices (ICE). A secondary market is the aftermarket replacement cycle for older machinery, driven by productivity upgrade pressure from rising labor costs.

aCNCNLYRYM.description: Production, crane, Industrial Production & Utilization, Monthly, National Bureau of Statistics of China
aCNCNLYRYM.meaning: Industrial Production: crane, Industrial Production & Utilization, Monthly, National Bureau of Statistics of China. Sub-sector or product-level output series from NBS Industrial Statistics (above-designated-size firms).
aCNCNLYRYM.how_to_use: Use alongside headline industrial production for sector cycle analysis. China publishes detailed product-level output in monthly NBS Industrial Statistics. Above-designated-size threshold currently CNY 20 million annual revenue.

aCNCNEUQWM.description: Production, crane, Volume, Industrial Production & Utilization, Monthly, National Bureau of Statistics of China
aCNCNEUQWM.meaning: Industrial Production: crane, Volume, Industrial Production & Utilization, Monthly, National Bureau of Statistics of China. Sub-sector or product-level output series from NBS Industrial Statistics (above-designated-size firms).
aCNCNEUQWM.how_to_use: Use alongside headline industrial production for sector cycle analysis. China publishes detailed product-level output in monthly NBS Industrial Statistics. Above-designated-size threshold currently CNY 20 million annual revenue.

aCNCNBQZM.description: Production, crane, Volume, Industrial Production & Utilization, Monthly, National Bureau of Statistics of China
aCNCNBQZM.meaning: Industrial Production: crane, Volume, Industrial Production & Utilization, Monthly, National Bureau of Statistics of China. Sub-sector or product-level output series from NBS Industrial Statistics (above-designated-size firms).
aCNCNBQZM.how_to_use: Use alongside headline industrial production for sector cycle analysis. China publishes detailed product-level output in monthly NBS Industrial Statistics. Above-designated-size threshold currently CNY 20 million annual revenue.

aCNCNZZDAM.description: Production, electric hand tool, Zhejiang Province
aCNCNZZDAM.subcategory: Electric Hand Tool Production — Zhejiang Province
aCNCNZZDAM.meaning: Monthly production of electric hand tools (drills, grinders, saws, sanders, and jigsaws) by enterprises above designated size in Zhejiang Province. Published by NBS Zhejiang Bureau monthly, typically in the second or third week of the following month. Zhejiang dominates China's electric hand tool industry — the Jinhua/Yongkang cluster is known as 'China's hardware city,' housing thousands of electric tool manufacturers, many of which export under Western OEM brands (Black & Decker, Bosch have supply chains here).
aCNCNZZDAM.how_to_use: Zhejiang electric hand tool output is a direct proxy for global DIY and professional tool demand — typically 80%+ of output is for export, making this series highly correlated with Western consumer home improvement cycles. The 2020-21 pandemic-era home improvement surge drove Zhejiang tool output to record highs (+30-40% YoY). Monitor alongside USD/CNY exchange rates and Western retail construction indicators (US housing starts, Europe DIY retail sales) for export order context. Cross-reference with Zhejiang electrical equipment output (aCNCNZWAVM).

aCNCNWGBGM.meaning: Monthly production of electrical equipment by enterprises above designated size in Hunan Province. Published by NBS Hunan Bureau monthly, typically in the second or third week of the following month. Hunan's electrical equipment sector includes transmission and distribution equipment (Xuji Electric, Changsha Electric), plus industrial motors and control systems serving the province's diversified manufacturing base (construction machinery, non-ferrous metals, rail equipment).
aCNCNWGBGM.how_to_use: Hunan electrical equipment output is a regional indicator for central China's electricity infrastructure investment — T&D equipment production typically tracks State Grid/China Southern Grid capex with a 6-12 month lead. The province's special position as home to CRRC's train manufacturing and Sany's construction machinery means electrical equipment demand spans traction motors, inverters, and grid-scale storage equipment. YoY growth above 12% signals active power grid upgrading cycles. Cross-reference with aCNCNZWAVM (Zhejiang) for coastal-inland electrical equipment comparison.

aCNCNZWAVM.meaning: Monthly production of electrical equipment by enterprises above designated size in Zhejiang Province. Published by NBS Zhejiang Bureau monthly, typically in the second or third week of the following month. Zhejiang is China's third-largest electrical equipment production base after Guangdong and Jiangsu — the Wenzhou and Hangzhou clusters produce low-voltage switchgear, connectors, circuit breakers, and power tools, with a very high export orientation.
aCNCNZWAVM.how_to_use: Zhejiang electrical equipment output is a high-frequency proxy for global electrical infrastructure demand — Zhejiang manufacturers supply OEM components to Schneider, ABB, Siemens distribution-level equipment. Growth above 15% YoY typically coincides with global grid investment upcycles (the 2021-24 energy transition investment wave drove exceptional Zhejiang output expansion). Cross-reference with Hunan (aCNCNWGBGM) to compare export-oriented Zhejiang vs. domestically-oriented Hunan. Closely linked to electrical export revenue (aCNCEXBA).

aCNCNJGVKM.meaning: Industrial Production: insulation. Sub-sector or product-level output series from NBS Industrial Statistics (above-designated-size firms).
aCNCNJGVKM.how_to_use: Use alongside headline industrial production for sector cycle analysis. China publishes detailed product-level output in monthly NBS Industrial Statistics. Above-designated-size threshold currently CNY 20 million annual revenue.

aCNCNOSHVM.description: Production, machine paper & paperboard (except base paper processing)
aCNCNOSHVM.meaning: Monthly production of machine-made paper and paperboard (excluding base paper processing/converting) by industrial enterprises above designated size nationally. Published monthly by NBS, typically released ~15th of the following month. China is the world's largest paper and paperboard producer (~120 million tonnes/year), with packaging paper (9 Dragon Paper, Lee & Man Paper) dominating output, followed by cultural paper and newsprint.
aCNCNOSHVM.how_to_use: Machine-made paper output is a leading indicator for packaging and consumer goods activity — China's packaging paper demand closely tracks e-commerce (Alibaba, JD.com) box shipments and industrial goods export packaging. Production surges above 8% YoY typically accompany e-commerce seasonal peaks (Singles' Day in November). Domestic wastepaper recycled fiber costs (after China's 2017-2018 waste paper import ban) make domestic production economics unique — cross-reference with domestic recovered fiber prices for margin context.

aCNCNFALFM.description: Production, machine paper & paperboard (except base paper processing), Henan Province
aCNCNFALFM.subcategory: Machine-Made Paper & Paperboard Production — Henan Province
aCNCNFALFM.meaning: Monthly production of machine-made paper and paperboard (excluding base paper processing) by enterprises above designated size in Henan Province. Published by NBS Henan Bureau monthly, typically in the second or third week of the following month. Henan has developed a significant paper production capacity oriented toward packaging paper and cultural paper for central China's market, utilizing both recycled and virgin fiber inputs.
aCNCNFALFM.how_to_use: Henan paper output reflects inland China packaging demand and construction-related paper (cement bags, gypsum board facing) activity — both linked to central China's real estate and logistics sectors. Deceleration below -5% YoY in Henan paper production often coincides with regional real estate or industrial slowdowns. Compare with national series (aCNCNOSHVM) to assess Henan's market share trends — Henan has been expanding paper capacity at the expense of coastal provinces where environmental compliance costs are higher.

aCNCNMRCUM.meaning: Monthly production of powder metallurgy (PM) parts in China, published by the NBS. PM parts (produced by compacting and sintering metal powders — iron, copper, aluminum, tungsten, stainless) are precision components used in auto transmissions, electric motors, VVT systems, and electronics; China is the world's fastest-growing PM market, consuming ~150,000 tonnes/year of PM iron powders.
aCNCNMRCUM.how_to_use: PM parts production is an advanced manufacturing metals indicator — rising output signals strength in high-value-added auto components and precision engineering, which consume specialty iron powders, copper powders, and tungsten carbide. The EV transition is a structural tailwind (EV motors use more PM sintered components than ICE transmissions). Cross with aCNCNHAFYM (casting machinery) to assess whether PM is gaining share vs. traditional casting in auto components — a technology shift indicator.

aCNCNJEPZM.meaning: Industrial Production: power cable. Sub-sector or product-level output series from NBS Industrial Statistics (above-designated-size firms).
aCNCNJEPZM.how_to_use: Use alongside headline industrial production for sector cycle analysis. China publishes detailed product-level output in monthly NBS Industrial Statistics. Above-designated-size threshold currently CNY 20 million annual revenue.

aCNCNOJFMM.units: tonnes of steam per hour (t/h) capacity (monthly)
aCNCNOJFMM.meaning: Monthly production of power station boilers (utility-scale steam generators for coal/gas/biomass power plants) by industrial enterprises above designated size in China. Published monthly by NBS, typically ~15th of the following month. China's dominant power station boiler manufacturers are Dongfang Boiler (Dongfang Electric Group), Shanghai Boiler Works (Shanghai Electric), and Harbin Boiler Company (Harbin Electric International), which together supply nearly all of China's new coal and biomass power plant boilers and export to BRI countries.
aCNCNOJFMM.how_to_use: Power station boiler production is the single best indicator of Chinese thermal power capacity pipeline. Monthly production of 100,000+ t/h capacity signals an active coal plant construction wave; sub-60,000 t/h reflects the phase-down of coal capacity addition. However, biomass and gas boiler orders are partially offsetting coal decline — examine the fuel-type breakdown where available. Lead time for delivery is 12-18 months after order; compare with NEA thermal power capacity additions ~18 months later. Critical for China coal demand 2-3 year outlook.

aCNCNMEYSM.meaning: Industrial Production: smartphone. Sub-sector or product-level output series from NBS Industrial Statistics (above-designated-size firms).
aCNCNMEYSM.how_to_use: Use alongside headline industrial production for sector cycle analysis. China publishes detailed product-level output in monthly NBS Industrial Statistics. Above-designated-size threshold currently CNY 20 million annual revenue.

aCNCNGWHM.meaning: Industrial Production: soft drink, Hubei Province. Sub-sector or product-level output series from NBS Industrial Statistics (above-designated-size firms).
aCNCNGWHM.how_to_use: Use alongside headline industrial production for sector cycle analysis. China publishes detailed product-level output in monthly NBS Industrial Statistics. Above-designated-size threshold currently CNY 20 million annual revenue.

aCNCNETIHM.description: Production, steam turbine for power stations
aCNCNETIHM.meaning: Industrial Production: steam turbine for power stations. Sub-sector or product-level output series from NBS Industrial Statistics (above-designated-size firms).
aCNCNETIHM.how_to_use: Use alongside headline industrial production for sector cycle analysis. China publishes detailed product-level output in monthly NBS Industrial Statistics. Above-designated-size threshold currently CNY 20 million annual revenue.

aCNCNFTLPM.meaning: Monthly production of turbine generators (steam turbine generators for coal/gas/nuclear power plants and wind turbine generators) by industrial enterprises above designated size. Published monthly by NBS, typically ~15th of the following month. China's turbine generator manufacturers — Dongfang Turbine, Shanghai Turbine (Shanghai Electric), and Harbin Turbine (Harbin Electric) — are among the world's largest, supplying both domestic power plants and exporting under BRI infrastructure contracts.
aCNCNFTLPM.how_to_use: Turbine generator production above 15 million kW/month signals robust power capacity build-out pipeline — the 2023-24 period saw exceptionally high output as China added ~220 GW of new power capacity per year. The shift from coal to wind turbine generators within this series is a key structural trend — wind generator capacity growth of 30%+ YoY reflects China's target of 1,200 GW wind+solar by 2030. Cross-reference with power station boiler output (aCNCNOJFMM) — both should track each other in coal plant cycles; divergence indicates rapid growth in non-thermal generation.

aCNCNPLHJM.meaning: Monthly production of welding machines (arc welding, MIG/MAG welding, laser welding, and spot welding equipment) by industrial enterprises above designated size. Published monthly by NBS, typically ~15th of the following month. China is the world's largest producer and consumer of welding equipment, with production concentrated in Shanghai, Tianjin, Chengdu, and Guangzhou. Key manufacturers include Lincoln Electric China, Miller China, and domestic brands like Riland, Jasic Technology.
aCNCNPLHJM.how_to_use: Welding machine production is a broad manufacturing capex indicator — nearly every metal fabrication, shipbuilding, automotive, and construction steel industry requires welding equipment. YoY growth above 10% signals healthy manufacturing investment; decline below -10% reflects capex contraction. The shift from traditional arc welders to robotic laser welding systems (a high-value segment) is a structural upgrade trend — monitor alongside industrial robot installations (CRIA data, ~270k units/year) for the automation investment context. Exports are significant (~30-40% of production).

aCNCNPEIA.description: Profit, industrial companies above designated size, entertainment boat & sport boat manufacturing
aCNCNPEIA.meaning: Industrial: Profit, industrial companies above designated size, entertainment boat & sport boat manufacturing. Profit statistics for above-designated-size industrial firms — released monthly by NBS.
aCNCNPEIA.how_to_use: Industrial profits are the corporate-earnings cycle proxy for China. PPI deflation 2023-24 has compressed industrial-sector margins; profit YoY growth often negative. Watch alongside SOE vs private firm profit splits.

aCNCNAZMB.description: Profit, industrial companies above designated size, non-ferrous metal casting
aCNCNAZMB.meaning: Profit of industrial companies above designated size in non-ferrous metal casting, published by the NBS with irregular frequency. Non-ferrous casting (aluminum die-casting, copper casting, zinc die-casting) is a downstream processing sector bridging primary metals and component manufacturing; major customers are auto OEMs, electronics assemblers, and construction hardware manufacturers.
aCNCNAZMB.how_to_use: Irregular frequency limits time-series analysis — treat as periodic profitability snapshots. When non-ferrous casting profits are strong alongside rising aluminum production (aCNCNDRRM1, aCNCNTPTOM), it confirms healthy downstream margins in the aluminum-to-casting value chain — a positive for aluminum smelter demand. Profit margin compression in casting (cross with aCNCNLOFHM) typically precedes destocking of aluminum ingot by die-casters and a weakening in premium aluminum alloy prices.

aCNCNKMHRM.meaning: Monthly raw coal (run-of-mine coal) production in China, published by the NBS — China's headline coal output indicator. China produces ~4.5 billion tonnes/year (~53% of global coal output), making it by far the world's largest coal producer; major provinces are Inner Mongolia (~1.1 Bt), Shanxi (~1.3 Bt), and Shaanxi (~700 Mt). Released monthly around the 15th of the following month.
aCNCNKMHRM.how_to_use: Monthly output above 400 Mt signals China is running at near-maximum mine capacity — typically reached during winter heating demand peaks (Nov–Feb) or government energy security campaigns. A sustained drop below 360 Mt/month is structurally bearish for thermal coal seaborne prices (Newcastle API4) as it implies Chinese domestic supply is constraining and import demand rises. Cross with aCNVAUMWSR (coal value-added growth) and aCNCNKWDNQ (capacity utilisation) for a triangulated coal supply health check.

aCNCNBFOF.description: Sales cost, industrial companies above designated size, medical diagnostic, monitoring & treatment equipment manufacturing
aCNCNBFOF.subcategory: Medical Diagnostic, Monitoring & Treatment Equipment — Sales Cost
aCNCNBFOF.meaning: Sales cost (cost of goods sold relating to sales revenue) for industrial companies above designated size in the medical diagnostic, monitoring and treatment equipment manufacturing sub-sector. Published by NBS as part of Industrial Enterprise Financial Statistics; frequency is irregular given the blank field. Covers makers of CT scanners, MRI systems, ultrasound devices, patient monitors, and radiotherapy equipment — a sector dominated by Mindray, United Imaging, and joint-venture multinationals.
aCNCNBFOF.how_to_use: Medical equipment sales cost evolution reveals margin dynamics — sustained cost growth outpacing revenue growth implies margin compression, often driven by component inflation (semiconductors, rare earth magnets in MRI machines) or competitive pricing pressure. China's medical equipment sector has seen rapid domestic brand market share gains (Mindray winning domestic hospital tenders previously dominated by GE, Philips, Siemens). Compare with equipment export data (aCNCEXBA) to assess whether domestic cost efficiency translates into export competitiveness gains.

aCNCNBCCK.description: Sales cost, state-owned industrial companies above designated size, electricity supply
aCNCNBCCK.subcategory: State-Owned Industrial Firms — Electricity Supply Sales Cost
aCNCNBCCK.meaning: Sales cost for state-owned industrial companies above designated size in the electricity supply (distribution and retail) sector. Published by NBS as part of Industrial Enterprise Financial Statistics; frequency is irregular given the blank field. Captures the cost structure of State Grid Corporation of China (SGCC) and China Southern Power Grid (CSG) — the world's two largest electricity distributors — plus provincial grid companies.
aCNCNBCCK.how_to_use: State-owned electricity supply sales costs are dominated by purchased electricity costs (from generators) and transmission/distribution infrastructure expenses. This series is critical for analyzing China's electricity sector value chain — when generator tariffs rise faster than retail tariffs (regulated), state grid distribution costs compress margins. Cross-reference with aCNCNFBSKM (utility profit margins) and aCNCNFYFH (state-owned generation sales value) to construct a full power sector P&L picture. Policy implications: persistent cost increases here drive annual tariff review cycles at NDRC.

aCNCNPMTYM.meaning: Monthly steel production in Fujian Province, published by the NBS Fujian Bureau with irregular frequency (marked [e] — estimated/unofficial). Fujian (~10 Mt/year steel capacity) hosts Sanming Iron and Steel and several smaller mills; the province's steel sector serves local construction and the growing semiconductor/electronics manufacturing base around Fuzhou and Quanzhou.
aCNCNPMTYM.how_to_use: The [e] flag means use as a directional indicator only — data is less reliable than core provincial series. Fujian steel is increasingly significant as a stainless and specialty steel province (serving semiconductor fab equipment and precision manufacturing). Cross with aCNCNIYVNM (Fujian aluminum) to assess whether the province's industrial metals complex is uniformly expanding or experiencing sector-specific patterns. Irregular frequency means quarterly interpolation may be needed for consistent time-series modeling.

aCNCNHBRFM.description: Steel production, Gansu Province, Current Period
aCNCNHBRFM.meaning: Monthly current-period steel production in Gansu Province, published by the NBS Gansu Bureau. Gansu (~5 Mt/year steel capacity) is a northwest China steel producer, anchored by Jiuquan Iron and Steel (JISCO) — one of China's oldest integrated steel enterprises (est. 1958) located near Jiayuguan in the Hexi Corridor. JISCO specialises in plates and structural sections for northwest infrastructure.
aCNCNHBRFM.how_to_use: Gansu steel is primarily a northwest infrastructure demand indicator and JISCO operational health proxy. JISCO has historically been a financially stressed SOE (requiring restructuring in 2016), so output fluctuations here often reflect balance sheet constraints rather than pure demand signals. When Gansu steel production recovers following a multi-month decline, check whether it coincides with debt restructuring announcements or government capital injections into JISCO.

aCNCNJASM.meaning: Monthly steel (all grades, total finished steel) production in Guangdong Province, as distinct from aCNCNLEGIM which specifically measures crude steel. This series captures the downstream rolled and finished steel picture in Guangdong, including a significant contribution from Zhanjiang's Baowu stainless/silicon steel complex and numerous coastal rolling mills that process semi-finished billets imported from third provinces or overseas.
aCNCNJASM.how_to_use: Compare with aCNCNLEGIM (Guangdong crude steel) to derive Guangdong's implied rolling conversion ratio — when total steel grows faster than crude steel, the province is importing and processing semi-finished billets. A persistent rolling/crude ratio above 1.15 in Guangdong signals strong coastal trading-mill activity — these mills are price-sensitive and will cut when HRC-billet spreads compress below ~CNY 100/t.

aCNCNLQBDM.meaning: Monthly current-period steel production in Hebei Province — China's largest steel-producing province (~240 Mt/year, ~24% of national output) published by the NBS Hebei Bureau. Hebei's steel belt (Tangshan, Handan, Shijiazhuang) is home to HBIS Group (Hesteel), Tangshan Guofeng, Delong Steel, Jingye Group, and hundreds of smaller mills. Tangshan alone produces ~85-90 Mt/year.
aCNCNLQBDM.how_to_use: This is the single most important provincial steel series in China — Hebei's output alone exceeds the entire production of the US, EU, or Japan. A Hebei 'blast furnace halt' notice from local government (triggered by air quality alerts — common in autumn/winter) cuts Chinese steel production by ~3-5 Mt/week and is the most frequent short-term steel supply shock. Tangshan pollution curtailment orders (Orange/Red alerts) typically follow within 5 days of this series printing above 20 Mt/month.

aCNCNDNCXM.description: Steel production, Heilongjiang Province, Industrial Production & Utilization, Monthly, National Bureau of Statistics of China
aCNCNDNCXM.meaning: Monthly steel production in Heilongjiang Province (Series A), published by the NBS Heilongjiang Bureau. This series (alongside aCNCNASSOM) represents Heilongjiang's total steel output including finished rolled products, as opposed to aCNCNIAVM which specifically tracks crude steel. The northeast's steel sector has been in structural decline since the early 2010s, with capacity rationalization ongoing.
aCNCNDNCXM.how_to_use: Use as a northeast China industrial recovery tracker — when this series stabilises or recovers after multi-year decline, cross-check with NBS northeast revitalisation policy announcements and Heilongjiang SOE credit conditions. Compare the ratio of this series (total steel) to aCNCNIAVM (crude steel) to derive rolling mill efficiency: a rising ratio indicates improving downstream processing activity even as crude steel flatlines, suggesting recovery is starting in fabrication before reaching primary steelmaking.

aCNCNASSOM.description: Steel production, Heilongjiang Province, Volume, Industrial Production & Utilization, Monthly, National Bureau of Statistics of China
aCNCNASSOM.subcategory: Steel Production — Heilongjiang Province (Series B, Volume)
aCNCNASSOM.meaning: Monthly steel production in Heilongjiang Province (Series B — Volume series), published by the NBS Heilongjiang Bureau alongside aCNCNDNCXM. The 'Volume' designation distinguishes this series from potential value-based or index-form presentations of the same underlying data. Together, the two Heilongjiang steel series provide cross-validation for the province's industrial output reporting.
aCNCNASSOM.how_to_use: Where aCNCNDNCXM and aCNCNASSOM diverge by >5%, investigate whether the difference reflects different product scope (crude vs. rolled, or all-steel vs. specific grades) rather than measurement error. Both series declining below -10% YoY simultaneously confirms Heilongjiang's steel sector is in genuine contraction — at this point, the macro story is about SOE credit risk (Heilongjiang province debt) rather than physical steel supply, and the policy response typically involves Northeastern Revitalisation Fund disbursements.

aCNCNPDBNM.meaning: Monthly steel (total rolled/finished) production in Henan Province, published by the NBS Henan Bureau, as distinct from aCNCNBYBM (Henan crude steel). Henan's steel sector produces both long products (rebar, wire rod) for the province's massive construction market and flat products for its growing auto manufacturing cluster around Zhengzhou (BYD new plant, Foxconn iPad plant nearby).
aCNCNPDBNM.how_to_use: Compare with aCNCNBYBM (Henan crude steel) to compute the crude-to-finished ratio: a rising ratio above 1.05 indicates Henan mills are processing imported semi-finished billets. Henan's rebar demand is a direct proxy for central China property construction health — when Henan rebar-type output falls >12% YoY, it implies property new starts in this 100M-population province are severely depressed, confirming national housing market stress beyond coastal markets.

aCNCNCSCM1.description: Steel production, Jiangsu Province, Current Period
aCNCNCSCM1.meaning: Monthly current-period steel production in Jiangsu Province, published by the NBS Jiangsu Bureau. Jiangsu (~140 Mt/year steel capacity) is China's second-largest steel-producing province after Hebei, anchored by Shagang Group (the world's largest private steel company, ~45 Mt/year), Nanjing Iron and Steel (Baowu subsidiary), and Xingcheng Special Steel. Jiangsu is China's leading specialty steel and flat products hub.
aCNCNCSCM1.how_to_use: Jiangsu steel is the private-sector-led, export-oriented contrast to state-dominated Hebei: Shagang produces primarily HRC, wire rod, and semi-finished billets for both domestic and export markets. When Jiangsu output rises faster than Hebei (aCNCNLQBDM), it typically signals export-driven demand growth for flat products rather than domestic property-led rebar demand. Monthly output above 12 Mt from Jiangsu indicates Shagang and peers are running at near-full capacity.

aCNCNOTAM.meaning: Monthly total steel production in Liaoning Province, published by the NBS Liaoning Bureau, complementing aCNCNBUCLM (Liaoning crude steel). Liaoning's total steel production (including finished rolling) exceeds crude steel volumes when the province's numerous downstream pipe mills, tube mills, and section mills are running at capacity. Key producers: Ansteel, Benxi Steel, Fushun Special Steel, Dalian Steel.
aCNCNOTAM.how_to_use: Compare with aCNCNBUCLM (Liaoning crude steel) to assess rolling mill utilisation — total steel consistently above crude steel by >8% indicates active downstream processing and likely billet imports into Liaoning's coastal mills. Liaoning's Dalian port is China's primary seamless pipe export hub — when Liaoning total steel rises faster than crude steel, it often signals strong energy-sector tubular demand (CNPC, Sinopec drilling programmes) feeding through the Dalian pipe cluster.

aCNCNFHNM1.description: Steel production, Shandong Province, Current Period
aCNCNFHNM1.meaning: Monthly current-period steel production in Shandong Province, published by the NBS Shandong Bureau. Shandong (~80 Mt/year steel capacity) is China's fourth-largest steel-producing province, with a diverse mix of producers including Shandong Iron and Steel Group (Laiwu + Jinan mills), Rizhao Steel (world's largest single-site steel complex), and numerous coastal rolling mills. Shandong steel feeds the province's giant construction, machinery, and marine equipment sectors.
aCNCNFHNM1.how_to_use: Shandong's Rizhao mill is one of the world's most efficient integrated steel plants (~25 Mt/year) and a benchmark for coastal seaborne-ore procurement — when Rizhao is running hot (inferred from this series strength), it competes aggressively for Brazilian and Australian iron ore cargoes at Rizhao port. Monthly output above 6.5 Mt for Shandong indicates the province's mills are at or above designed capacity; output above 7 Mt is the historical ceiling before government output restriction commentary emerges.

aCNCNJEWFM.meaning: Monthly current-period steel production in Shanghai Municipality, published by the NBS Shanghai Bureau. Shanghai (~20 Mt/year steel capacity) is anchored entirely by Baowu's Baoshan complex — the world's first purpose-built coastal integrated steel mill (opened 1985), now one of the world's most advanced steel plants, producing high-end automotive steel, electrical steel, and shipbuilding plate. Shanghai is a benchmark for China's premium steel quality capabilities.
aCNCNJEWFM.how_to_use: Shanghai/Baoshan is China's premium flat steel indicator — when this series rises, it signals healthy demand in auto (SAIC, local JV production), shipbuilding (Jiangnan Shipyard), and appliance sectors that consume Baoshan's high-value grades (dual-phase, ultra-high-strength, grain-oriented electrical steel). A divergence where Shanghai flat steel output rises while small/medium section production (aCNPDMNSST) falls confirms the steel sector is operating on an industrial/consumer rather than property demand cycle.

aCNCNBKDBM.meaning: China industrial output: Steel production, Shanxi Province. Industrial-sector production data for specific products or sub-sectors.
aCNCNBKDBM.how_to_use: Track for sector-cycle dynamics. China is the world's largest producer of steel, cement, copper, aluminum, and many other industrial commodities. Sustained production declines signal industrial-sector deceleration; sustained increases reflect capacity expansion or commodity-cycle peaks.

aCNCNEHQKM.description: Steel production, Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region,Current Period
aCNCNEHQKM.meaning: China industrial output: Steel production, Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region,Current Period. Industrial-sector production data for specific products or sub-sectors.
aCNCNEHQKM.how_to_use: Track for sector-cycle dynamics. China is the world's largest producer of steel, cement, copper, aluminum, and many other industrial commodities. Sustained production declines signal industrial-sector deceleration; sustained increases reflect capacity expansion or commodity-cycle peaks.

aCNCNLIHXM.meaning: China industrial output: Steel production, Zhejiang Province. Industrial-sector production data for specific products or sub-sectors.
aCNCNLIHXM.how_to_use: Track for sector-cycle dynamics. China is the world's largest producer of steel, cement, copper, aluminum, and many other industrial commodities. Sustained production declines signal industrial-sector deceleration; sustained increases reflect capacity expansion or commodity-cycle peaks.

aCNCNHFZU.description: Stock, industrial companies above designated size, vegetable oil processing
aCNCNHFZU.meaning: China commodity inventory/stock: Stock, industrial companies above designated size, vegetable oil processing. Inventory data tracking stockpiles of industrial commodities, raw materials, or finished goods.
aCNCNHFZU.how_to_use: Inventory cycles drive industrial-sector demand patterns. Rising stocks alongside falling production signal weakening demand; falling stocks with stable production signal supply tightening. Major stockpiles tracked: steel, copper, cement, coal — these are commodity-cycle indicators globally.

aCNCNYUFM1.meaning: Import value via processing trade centers (bonded zones/processing centers). Monthly series from GACC (General Administration of Customs). Tracks imports channeled through China's processing trade regime.
aCNCNYUFM1.how_to_use: Processing trade imports (materials imported for assembly/re-export) are a key structural component of China's trade. Their share of total imports has declined as China moves up the value chain (from ~50% in the 1990s to ~20% now). Falling processing trade imports signal structural transformation — fewer low-value assembly operations. Rising processing trade can indicate export order recovery. Cross-reference with total exports and manufacturing PMI new export orders.

aCNCNOZFOM.description: Foreign insurance property insurance company's original insurance premium income, French Union
aCNCNOZFOM.meaning: Foreign property insurance company original insurance premium income — French Union Insurance. Monthly series from CBIRC (China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission). Tracks premium revenue of a foreign-invested property insurer.
aCNCNOZFOM.how_to_use: Premium income from foreign insurers in China tracks the penetration and growth of foreign financial services in a highly regulated, gradually liberalizing market. China's property insurance market is dominated by PICC, Ping An, and China Life P&C; foreign players have <5% market share. French Union premium trends reflect appetite for specialty risks (marine, aviation, trade credit) where foreign expertise has a competitive edge.

aCNCNURXM1.description: Foreign insurance property insurance company's original insurance premium income, Fubon property
aCNCNURXM1.meaning: Foreign property insurance company original premium income — Fubon Property Insurance (Taiwan-invested insurer in mainland China). Monthly series from CBIRC.
aCNCNURXM1.how_to_use: Fubon Property's premium income in mainland China tracks cross-strait financial services integration. Taiwan-invested insurers serve both the Taiwanese corporate community in China (manufacturing supply chains) and domestic Chinese clients. Fubon's growth reflects the Taiwan investment presence in China and cross-strait economic linkages — sensitive to bilateral political developments.

aCNCNTOJUM.description: Foreign insurance property insurance company's original insurance premium income, History property
aCNCNTOJUM.meaning: Foreign property insurance company original premium income — History Property Insurance. Monthly series from CBIRC.
aCNCNTOJUM.how_to_use: A smaller foreign-invested property insurer's premium income. Use in aggregate with other foreign insurer series (aCNCNOZFOM, aCNCNRBUM) to construct a composite foreign property insurance market share indicator. The aggregate trend of foreign insurer premiums captures the pace of financial market opening under CBIRC's licensing regime and reflects foreign corporate demand for non-life insurance coverage in China.

aCNCNOOTHM.description: Foreign insurance property insurance company's original insurance premium income, Meiya
aCNCNOOTHM.meaning: Foreign property insurance company original premium income — Meiya Insurance. Monthly series from CBIRC.
aCNCNOOTHM.how_to_use: Meiya Insurance (美亚财险 AIG-affiliated) is one of the largest foreign property insurers in China. Its premium income is a bellwether for foreign insurer performance. AIG has a long history in China (pre-1949 roots); Meiya's growth tracks the expansion of international trade, expatriate services, and liability insurance in China. Declining premiums may signal foreign corporate retreat or market competition from domestic players.

aCNCNRBUM.description: Foreign insurance property insurance company's original insurance premium income, Sumitomo Mitsui Marine Fire Insurance
aCNCNRBUM.meaning: Foreign property insurance company original premium income — Sumitomo Mitsui Marine Fire Insurance (Japan). Monthly series from CBIRC.
aCNCNRBUM.how_to_use: Japan is China's largest foreign investor by historical stock. Sumitomo Mitsui Marine's China premium income tracks Japanese corporate presence and risk appetite in China — including manufacturing supply-chain insurance. Sharp declines could signal Japanese corporate withdrawal from China (de-risking). Use alongside Japan FDI into China data and bilateral trade volumes.

aCNCNCKYLQ.description: Insurance companies, enterprise annuity investment management business contribution amount, Safe Pension
aCNCNCKYLQ.meaning: Insurance companies — enterprise annuity investment management business contribution amount, Safe Pension (太平养老). Quarterly series from CBIRC / Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (MoHRSS). Measures employer contributions managed by Safe Pension.
aCNCNCKYLQ.how_to_use: Enterprise annuities (second-pillar pensions) are underdeveloped in China — covering only ~30M workers vs the ~700M+ formal-sector workforce. Contribution volumes track the growth of supplementary pension savings, critical given China's aging demographic and the first-pillar public pension's fiscal pressures (projected deficit by 2035). Rising contributions signal corporate willingness to invest in employee retention and pension security.

aCNCNNMMPQ.description: Insurance companies, enterprise annuity investment management business contribution amount, Yangtze River Pension
aCNCNNMMPQ.meaning: Insurance companies — enterprise annuity investment management business contribution amount, Yangtze River Pension (长江养老). Quarterly series from CBIRC / MoHRSS.
aCNCNNMMPQ.how_to_use: Yangtze River Pension is a major enterprise annuity manager. Contribution growth here tracks pension savings accumulation in the Yangtze River Economic Belt — China's most populous economic corridor. Aggregate enterprise annuity contributions (aCNCNCKYLQ + aCNCNNMMPQ + aCNCNRZXGQ) give a read on China's pension savings adequacy vs the looming elderly care funding gap.

aCNCNDQNI.meaning: Insurance companies — total liabilities, Anbang Assets Management. Frequency not specified (likely annual). From CBIRC. Measures the liability side of Anbang's insurance/asset management balance sheet.
aCNCNDQNI.how_to_use: Anbang Insurance was seized by the government in 2018 following its aggressive global acquisition spree and domestic mis-selling of high-yield wealth management products. Its liability data tracks the resolution of one of China's most prominent insurance sector bailouts. Rising liabilities post-seizure would signal ongoing policy cost; declining liabilities reflect successful wind-down. Relevant for assessing systemic risk management in China's insurance sector.

aCNCNRZXGQ.description: Insurance companies, pension security & other entrusted management assets balance, National Life Pension
aCNCNRZXGQ.meaning: Insurance companies — pension security and other entrusted management assets balance, National Life Pension (国寿养老). Quarterly series from CBIRC / MoHRSS. Measures AUM of China Life's pension management arm.
aCNCNRZXGQ.how_to_use: National Life Pension (China Life subsidiary) is the largest enterprise annuity manager. Its AUM balance tracks the accumulation of second-pillar pension assets — a critical buffer for China's aging demographics. Rising AUM is positive for institutional equity and bond market demand (pension managers are long-term investors). China's pension fund AUM is still small relative to GDP vs developed markets — significant growth runway.

aCNCNPDZM.description: Insurance net profit, Junkang Life Insurance Co., Ltd.
aCNCNPDZM.meaning: Insurance net profit — Junkang Life Insurance Co., Ltd. Annual series from CBIRC. Measures bottom-line profitability of Junkang Life.
aCNCNPDZM.how_to_use: Insurance sector profitability is a financial cycle indicator. China's life insurers face dual pressures: low interest rates compress investment returns on policy reserves, while claim costs rise with aging. Junkang Life (a smaller insurer) net profit tracks whether sector-wide margin pressures are affecting smaller players disproportionately. Sector-wide insurance profits also track investment portfolio returns (equities, bonds, real estate).

aCNCNKJBP.description: Insurance net profit, Sunshine Property Insurance Co.
aCNCNKJBP.meaning: Insurance net profit — Sunshine Property Insurance Co. Annual series from CBIRC. Measures net profit of a mid-sized domestic property-casualty insurer.
aCNCNKJBP.how_to_use: Sunshine P&C profit is a corporate earnings proxy for China's non-life insurance cycle. P&C profitability depends on: combined ratios (claims + expenses vs premiums), catastrophe losses (floods, typhoons — rising with climate change), and investment returns. Use with premium income data and catastrophe loss statistics to construct a full-cycle insurance sector picture.

aCNCNKPYC.description: Peronal insurance companies, original insurance premium income, China Merchants Cigna Life Insurance Co., Ltd.
aCNCNKPYC.meaning: Personal insurance companies — original insurance premium income, China Merchants Cigna Life Insurance Co., Ltd. Annual series from CBIRC.
aCNCNKPYC.how_to_use: China Merchants Cigna is a sino-foreign JV life insurer (China Merchants Bank + Cigna). Its premium income tracks: (1) bancassurance channel productivity (CMBCM branch network), (2) demand for health and life insurance in an aging society, (3) foreign insurer strategy success in China. China's health insurance market is the fastest-growing globally; Cigna's China JV premium growth is a bellwether for foreign health insurer opportunity.

aCNCNQBHHM.meaning: Basic medical insurance participation (人数). Monthly series from NHC / NBS. Measures total enrollment in China's basic medical insurance schemes (urban employee BMI + urban-rural resident BMI).
aCNCNQBHHM.how_to_use: Basic medical insurance enrollment is the coverage indicator for China's universal healthcare system. China achieved near-universal coverage (~1.36B enrollees) by 2015 through the urban-rural resident scheme expansion. Monthly changes reflect: demographic shifts (population decline reduces absolute enrollment), migrant worker enrollment improvements (hukou reform), and administrative consolidation. Coverage quality (not just quantity) is the policy frontier; pair with per-capita reimbursement rate data.

aCNSTLAR.how_to_use: Cross-check against related series in the same category for context. China macro data is published by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS, real-economy + prices), People's Bank of China (PBoC, monetary), State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE, BoP/FX), and Ministry of Finance (fiscal).

aCNPFYAR.meaning: Industrial total profits, cumulative year-to-date, year-over-year change (%). Monthly series from NBS. Cumulative growth rate of industrial profits.
aCNPFYAR.how_to_use: The cumulative YoY growth rate of industrial profits smooths base-effect volatility in the monthly series. It is the key input for full-year corporate earnings forecasting. A cumulative rate recovering from deep negatives (as in 2023) signals the beginning of an earnings cycle upturn. The PPI deflation context is crucial: nominal profit growth understates real profit recovery if prices are falling. Decompose into revenue growth vs margin recovery.

aCNINVPNG.description: Inventories, Finished Goods, Petroleum & natural gas extraction
aCNINVPNG.meaning: Inventories, finished goods — petroleum and natural gas extraction sector. Monthly series from NBS industrial enterprise survey.
aCNINVPNG.how_to_use: Oil and gas sector finished goods inventories track the supply-demand balance in China's upstream energy industry. Rising inventories signal production outpacing refinery offtake (potential crude price pressure domestically) or export restrictions. Declining inventories indicate strong refinery throughput. Pair with crude oil import data and refinery utilization rates for a full picture of China's oil supply chain.

aCNINVPNF.description: Inventories, Finished Goods, Petroleum processing, coking & nuclear fuels processing
aCNINVPNF.meaning: Inventories, finished goods — petroleum processing, coking, and nuclear fuels processing sector. Monthly series from NBS industrial enterprise survey.
aCNINVPNF.how_to_use: Refined petroleum product inventories (gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, coke) are critical demand-supply indicators. High coke inventories signal steel sector slowdown (property crisis impact); high diesel inventories signal logistics and construction weakness. Gasoline inventory swings reflect passenger vehicle demand and EV substitution (rising EV penetration structurally reduces gasoline demand). Use with aCNCNLZVJ (transport diesel) for cross-sector verification.

aCNCNROGS.meaning: Online retail trade, total transaction value. Annual series from NBS / MOFCOM (Ministry of Commerce). Measures total e-commerce retail sales value.
aCNCNROGS.how_to_use: China has the world's largest e-commerce market (~$2T+ annually) with online retail penetration ~28% of total retail — the highest globally. Online retail growth has been the key driver of total retail resilience even as offline retail stagnates. The annual series captures full-year platform sales (Alibaba, JD, PDD, TikTok Shop). Structural drivers: mobile commerce, livestreaming shopping, rural e-commerce expansion. Cross-reference with aCNWRTCOS (cosmetics sub-category) and aCNCNZHYBM (auto retail).

aCNCNGWFJ.description: Property insurance companies, original premium income, special risk insurance
aCNCNGWFJ.meaning: Property insurance companies — original premium income, special risk insurance. Annual series from CBIRC. Covers specialty lines including nuclear, aviation, satellite, and other non-standard risks.
aCNCNGWFJ.how_to_use: Special risk (特殊风险) insurance premium growth tracks China's development of advanced industrial risks — nuclear power expansion (China has the world's largest nuclear build program), commercial aerospace (Long March rockets, Shenzhou spacecraft), and offshore energy. Rising premiums signal China's ascent in advanced technology with associated insurance needs. Use with nuclear power generation capacity data and aerospace program budgets.

aCNWRTCOS.meaning: Retail sales, cosmetics, total value. Monthly series from NBS. Measures consumer spending on cosmetics through enterprises above designated size (annual revenue >CNY 5M).
aCNWRTCOS.how_to_use: Cosmetics retail is a premium consumption indicator — sensitive to consumer confidence and income growth. China is the world's second-largest cosmetics market. The rise of domestic brands ('guochao' — national trend) has challenged L'Oreal, Estee Lauder, and LVMH in China. Rapid growth in cosmetics retail signals premiumization of consumption; contraction (as in 2022-23) reflects the 'consumption downgrade' narrative. Pair with aCNWRTCOSGR (YoY growth) for trend monitoring.

aCNWRTCOSGR.meaning: Retail sales, cosmetics, year-over-year change (%). Monthly series from NBS. Growth rate of cosmetics consumer spending.
aCNWRTCOSGR.how_to_use: The cosmetics YoY growth rate is a high-frequency consumer sentiment gauge. It leads broader retail sales recovery/deterioration by 1-2 months (cosmetics are discretionary but low-ticket vs durables). Deep negative readings in 2022 (lockdowns) reversed to strong positive in 2023 (revenge spending), then moderated into 2024 (consumer caution). Use as a leading indicator for consumer confidence and luxury/beauty sector equity positioning.

aCNCNZHYBM.description: Retail sales of enterprises above designated size, car
aCNCNZHYBM.meaning: Retail sales of enterprises above designated size — passenger cars. Monthly series from NBS / CAAM (China Association of Automobile Manufacturers). Measures auto retail sales value.
aCNCNZHYBM.how_to_use: Auto retail is the single largest category of China's consumer goods retail and the bellwether of the consumption cycle. China is the world's largest auto market (~25M passenger cars/year). EV penetration has surged to ~35% of new car sales (2024). Monitor for: (1) NEV vs ICE split (structural shift), (2) price war impact on revenue growth vs unit sales growth, (3) export boom (China became world's #1 auto exporter in 2023). Use with aCNCNROGS and aCNWRTCOSGR for consumption cycle context.

aCNT2SPSRCW.description: Sales Revenue, Coal mining, washing & dressing
aCNT2SPSRCW.meaning: Sales revenue — coal mining, washing, and dressing sector. Monthly series from NBS industrial enterprise survey. Measures total revenue of the coal mining sub-sector.
aCNT2SPSRCW.how_to_use: Coal mining revenue tracks both coal price and volume — the two determinants of China's most critical energy sector's financial health. Post-2021 coal price spike massively boosted mining revenues; subsequent normalization has pressured profitability. Shanxi and Inner Mongolia government fiscal revenues are directly tied to coal-sector revenues via royalties and taxes. Declining revenue signals fiscal stress in coal-dependent provinces and potential LGFV stress.

aCNT2SPSRFM.description: Sales Revenue, Ferrous metals mining & dressing
aCNT2SPSRFM.meaning: Sales revenue — ferrous metals mining and dressing sector. Monthly series from NBS industrial enterprise survey. Measures total revenue of iron ore and ferrous metals mining.
aCNT2SPSRFM.how_to_use: Ferrous metals (iron ore, steel) revenue is one of the most direct proxies for China's construction and manufacturing cycle. The property sector crisis (2021-) has been devastating for ferrous metals demand — steel demand for real estate dropped ~40% from peak. Revenue here tracks the magnitude of the industrial steel-demand contraction. Export of cheap Chinese steel to global markets is creating trade tensions. Pair with aCNINVPNF for full metals sector picture.

aCNT2SPSRNF.description: Sales Revenue, Non-ferrous metals mining & dressing
aCNT2SPSRNF.meaning: Sales revenue — non-ferrous metals mining and dressing sector. Monthly series from NBS industrial enterprise survey. Covers copper, aluminium, lead, zinc, nickel, lithium, rare earths, and other non-ferrous metal mining.
aCNT2SPSRNF.how_to_use: Non-ferrous metals revenue is the critical clean-energy transition indicator: copper (power cables, EVs), lithium (batteries), cobalt (batteries), rare earths (magnets for EVs and wind turbines). China dominates global production and refining of most critical minerals. Lithium mining revenue boom (2022-23) followed by bust (2024) directly impacted this series. Rising non-ferrous revenue driven by lithium/copper tracks the green transition supply chain.

aCNCNRLVKQ.meaning: Urban Registered Unemployment Rate — legacy unemployment measure tracking only people who registered for unemployment benefits at local labor bureaus. Pre-2018 official headline; less meaningful now (people often don't bother registering).
aCNCNRLVKQ.how_to_use: Use the survey rate (aCNCNUERLM) instead. Urban-registered rate runs much lower (~3-4%) than the broader survey rate (5-6%) because registration is incomplete.

aCNCNUERLM.meaning: Urban Survey Unemployment Rate — the official monthly headline unemployment rate, based on the urban-area labor-force survey. Replaced the old urban-registered unemployment rate as the headline gauge in 2018.
aCNCNUERLM.how_to_use: THE China unemployment headline. Pre-COVID ~5%; spiked to 6.2% in 2020 and 2022 (lockdowns). Released monthly.
