aCNIFATSPG.how_to_use: FAI is China's headline investment gauge — released monthly by NBS as part of the activity bundle. Decompose into infrastructure (state-led, counter-cyclical), manufacturing (private sector), real estate (now contracting). Each component tells a different story.

aCNIFATOT.meaning: China Fixed Asset Investment: Investment in Fixed Assets, Urban. Captures capital expenditure across infrastructure, real estate, manufacturing, and other sectors.
aCNIFATOT.how_to_use: FAI is China's headline investment gauge — released monthly by NBS as part of the activity bundle. Decompose into infrastructure (state-led, counter-cyclical), manufacturing (private sector), real estate (now contracting). Each component tells a different story.

aCNIFATOTCG.description: Investment in Fixed Assets, Urban, growth rate, Chg Y/Y
aCNIFATOTCG.meaning: China Fixed Asset Investment: Investment in Fixed Assets, Urban, growth rate, Chg Y/Y. Captures capital expenditure across infrastructure, real estate, manufacturing, and other sectors.
aCNIFATOTCG.how_to_use: FAI is China's headline investment gauge — released monthly by NBS as part of the activity bundle. Decompose into infrastructure (state-led, counter-cyclical), manufacturing (private sector), real estate (now contracting). Each component tells a different story.

aCNIFAWCEG.description: Investment in Fixed Assets, Water conservancy, environment & public utilities management, growth rate, Chg Y/Y
aCNIFAWCEG.meaning: China Fixed Asset Investment: Investment in Fixed Assets, Water conservancy, environment & public utilities management, growth rate, Chg Y/Y. Captures capital expenditure across infrastructure, real estate, manufacturing, and other sectors.
aCNIFAWCEG.how_to_use: FAI is China's headline investment gauge — released monthly by NBS as part of the activity bundle. Decompose into infrastructure (state-led, counter-cyclical), manufacturing (private sector), real estate (now contracting). Each component tells a different story.

aCNIFAWNRTG.description: Investment in Fixed Assets, Wholesale & retail trade, growth rate, Chg Y/Y
aCNIFAWNRTG.meaning: China Fixed Asset Investment: Investment in Fixed Assets, Wholesale & retail trade, growth rate, Chg Y/Y. Captures capital expenditure across infrastructure, real estate, manufacturing, and other sectors.
aCNIFAWNRTG.how_to_use: FAI is China's headline investment gauge — released monthly by NBS as part of the activity bundle. Decompose into infrastructure (state-led, counter-cyclical), manufacturing (private sector), real estate (now contracting). Each component tells a different story.

aCNPITOTR.description: Private Fixed Investment, Total, growth rate
aCNPITOTR.meaning: China macro reference series: Private Fixed Investment, Total, growth rate. Refer to the description and source for analytical context.
aCNPITOTR.how_to_use: Cross-check against related series in the same category for context. China macro data is published by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS, real-economy + prices), People's Bank of China (PBoC, monetary), State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE, BoP/FX), and Ministry of Finance (fiscal).

aCNUFAIAR.meaning: China macro reference series: Urban, Chg Y/Y. Refer to the description and source for analytical context.
aCNUFAIAR.how_to_use: Cross-check against related series in the same category for context. China macro data is published by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS, real-economy + prices), People's Bank of China (PBoC, monetary), State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE, BoP/FX), and Ministry of Finance (fiscal).

aCNCNOULM.description: Average domestic market price of oil & chemical products, sodium cyanide (import)
aCNCNOULM.meaning: Average domestic market price of oil and chemical products including sodium cyanide (import), compiled monthly. Tracks upstream chemical input costs that feed through to manufacturing CPI and PPI.
aCNCNOULM.how_to_use: Monitor for cost-push pressure on PPI non-metal chemicals; divergence from global crude benchmarks signals domestic supply-demand imbalance or FX pass-through.

aCNCNZZTS.meaning: Average import price for liquefied natural gas (LNG) into China, reflecting spot and term contract settlement values. China is the world's largest LNG importer; import price feeds domestic gas utility tariffs and industrial energy costs.
aCNCNZZTS.how_to_use: Rising LNG import prices compress margins for gas-intensive industries and push up utility CPI sub-components; compare against JKM spot prices for arbitrage signals.

aCNCNUSGC.meaning: Average import price for palm oil arriving in China, a key cooking-oil input covering roughly 20% of edible-oil consumption. Palm oil prices from Malaysia and Indonesia pass through directly to CPI food sub-component edible oils.
aCNCNUSGC.how_to_use: Watch for seasonal peaks (Ramadan demand, La Nina crop impact) feeding into China edible-oil retail CPI with a 1-2 month lag; also a proxy for food-import inflation pressure on trade balance.

aCNCNVRGRM.meaning: China steel price index for rebar (construction-grade reinforcement bar), the most widely traded steel contract on Shanghai Futures Exchange. Rebar prices are a leading indicator of construction activity and housing investment.
aCNCNVRGRM.how_to_use: Rebar price trends lead NBS land price indices by 1-3 months; sharp drops signal property sector stress feeding deflationary pressure; also watch vs SHFE DCE futures spread.

aCNCNCLPXQ.meaning: National aggregate land price level index compiled by the China Land Price Information Service Platform (CLPIS), covering residential, commercial, and industrial use parcels transacted at government auctions. Land prices are the key input cost for property developers.
aCNCNCLPXQ.how_to_use: Declining land prices signal developer funding stress and reduced local government revenue; sustained fall below 2020 levels reinforces PBoC easing thesis and dampens housing CPI.

aCNCNDAXFQ.description: Land price level, Bohai Economic Zone
aCNCNDAXFQ.meaning: Land price level index for the Bohai Economic Zone (Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region plus Liaoning/Shandong coasts), a major industrial and logistics corridor. Regional land price reflects demand from manufacturing investment and tier-1 city spillover.
aCNCNDAXFQ.how_to_use: Bohai land prices move with northern China industrial cycles; use alongside national index to assess regional divergence and targeted policy easing in the BTH integration zone.

aCNCNDBDIQ.meaning: Land price level for China's Central South region (Hunan, Hubei, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan), encompassing Pearl River Delta adjacents and interior provincial cities. Captures rapid urbanization-driven land demand in a high-growth belt.
aCNCNDBDIQ.how_to_use: Divergence between Central South and East/Bohai indices flags regional property policy effectiveness; Guangdong urban-rural land reform can cause step changes.

aCNCNGZKN/A.meaning: Land price level for the East area (Yangtze River Delta: Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Anhui, Fujian), China's most economically dense coastal region. East area land prices command the highest national premiums and are most sensitive to property policy tightening.
aCNCNGZKN/A.how_to_use: East area land price is a bellwether for national trend; YRD city-cluster policy relaxation or tightening shows up here first, with CPI housing sub-component following 2-4 quarters later.

aCNCNXZFYQ.description: Land price level, Fushun city, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNXZFYQ.meaning: Land price level index for Fushun city (Liaoning province, Northeast China), a former heavy-industry base undergoing economic restructuring. Reflects micro-level land-market conditions in a tier-3 rust-belt city.
aCNCNXZFYQ.how_to_use: Fushun's persistently weak land prices illustrate population-outflow deflation dynamics typical of Northeast cities; contrast against Bohai zone aggregate to gauge regional divergence.

aCNCNQDTQ.description: Land price level, Fushun city, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNQDTQ.meaning: Fushun city land price level at current (nominal) prices, as reported by the China Land Price Information Service Platform. The current-price series captures nominal transaction values without deflation, useful for developer cost accounting.
aCNCNQDTQ.how_to_use: Pair with the constant-price Fushun series (aCNCNXZFYQ) to derive implicit land price deflator for the city; large gap signals elevated local inflation even as real land demand is flat.

aCNCNQKJUQ.description: Land price level, Fuxin city, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNQKJUQ.meaning: Land price level for Fuxin city (Liaoning province), another Northeast coal-dependent city with long-term structural decline. Tracks land demand from limited industrial redevelopment and government-led urban renewal.
aCNCNQKJUQ.how_to_use: Fuxin's land prices typically lag national upturns by 6-12 months; use as a lagging indicator of whether central government stimulus is reaching distressed smaller cities.

aCNCNFWBRQ.description: Land price level, Fuxin city, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNFWBRQ.meaning: Fuxin city land prices at current nominal values from CLPIS quarterly surveys. Nominal series includes local price-level changes relevant for municipal finance and land revenue forecasting.
aCNCNFWBRQ.how_to_use: Compare nominal vs. real series to assess how much of Fuxin land revenue growth is price vs. volume; key for gauging local government fiscal stress in Northeast China.

aCNCNWKYAQ.description: Land price level, Handan city, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNWKYAQ.meaning: Land price level for Handan city (Hebei province, BTH region), a major steel-producing city whose land market is closely tied to steelmaker consolidation and environmental policy. Tracks real land demand in a transition-economy tier-3 city.
aCNCNWKYAQ.how_to_use: Handan land prices react to steel-capacity cuts and BTH integration policy; rising prices alongside rebar index (aCNCNVRGRM) confirm industrial-zone land demand is re-emerging.

aCNCNFLNKQ.description: Land price level, Handan city, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNFLNKQ.meaning: Handan city land prices at current (nominal) prices, capturing actual transaction values in CNY. Allows direct comparison with developer land bank costs and local government land revenue in nominal terms.
aCNCNFLNKQ.how_to_use: Use alongside constant-price Handan series for real price deflation estimates; gap between nominal and real signals whether local CPI is elevated relative to land market fundamentals.

aCNCNGAQLQ.description: Land price level, Hegang city, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNGAQLQ.meaning: Land price level for Hegang city (Heilongjiang province), which made headlines in 2021 for house prices as low as CNY 10,000-20,000 per unit — among the cheapest in China. Captures extreme deflation in a shrinking coal-mining city.
aCNCNGAQLQ.how_to_use: Hegang is a tail-risk reference for what population-outflow deflation looks like at its extreme; useful for scenario analysis of rust-belt city property risk in Northeast portfolio exposure.

aCNCNTOPBQ.description: Land price level, Hegang city, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNTOPBQ.meaning: Hegang city land prices at current nominal values, representing minimum land-market activity in one of China's most distressed urban economies. Nominal values may remain near zero or show very small absolute changes.
aCNCNTOPBQ.how_to_use: Pair with aCNCNGAQLQ to monitor whether government-directed redevelopment programmes are translating into real or merely nominal land price recovery in Hegang.

aCNCNKUWMQ.description: Land price level, Hengyang city, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNKUWMQ.meaning: Land price level for Hengyang city (Hunan province, Central South), a mid-size inland city with growing manufacturing investment from coastal industry relocation. Land prices reflect urbanisation-driven demand from migrant workers and industrial parks.
aCNCNKUWMQ.how_to_use: Rising Hengyang land prices alongside Central South regional index signal successful inland industry relocation absorbing coastal deflation; watch for acceleration post-stimulus rounds.

aCNCNZGYQ.description: Land price level, Hengyang city, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNZGYQ.meaning: Hengyang city land prices at current nominal prices from CLPIS, capturing developer acquisition costs and local fiscal land revenue in CNY terms. Nominal series is used in local government budget and land auction reporting.
aCNCNZGYQ.how_to_use: Compare to constant-price series (aCNCNKUWMQ) to assess local price inflation; Hengyang nominal land prices rising faster than real suggest cost-push pressures on new housing supply.

aCNCNKTFDQ.meaning: Land price level for the Huadong (East China) region from CLPIS — broadly covering Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian. As China's wealthiest coastal cluster, Huadong land prices are the highest nationally and the most policy-sensitive.
aCNCNKTFDQ.how_to_use: Huadong land prices are a primary input for developer margin models; a 10% quarterly fall signals material developer distress in the Yangtze Delta cluster, directly impacting housing CPI rents.

aCNCNFZZHQ.description: Land price level, Huaibei City, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNFZZHQ.meaning: Land price level for Huaibei city (Anhui province), a coal-mining city transitioning to manufacturing and logistics. Located in the Yangtze River Delta extended hinterland, its land market is supported by YRD integration policy.
aCNCNFZZHQ.how_to_use: Track alongside Huaibei current-price series for real demand signals; YRD integration upgrades and high-speed rail connectivity announcements tend to produce step-changes in Huaibei land prices.

aCNCNLQAZQ.description: Land price level, Huaibei City, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNLQAZQ.meaning: Huaibei city land prices at current nominal prices, reporting actual auction transaction values used for local government fiscal planning. Nominal values reflect both real demand shifts and general price-level changes in Anhui.
aCNCNLQAZQ.how_to_use: Paired with constant-price aCNCNFZZHQ, the nominal-real gap offers an implicit local land price deflator; useful for granular Anhui property market analysis.

aCNCNIDZRQ.description: Land price level, Huainan City, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNIDZRQ.meaning: Land price level for Huainan city (Anhui province), historically a major coal-production centre now diversifying into data centres and clean energy. Real land price tracks structural economic transition in a mid-Yangtze city.
aCNCNIDZRQ.how_to_use: Rising real land prices in Huainan amid coal industry decline signal successful diversification; compare with Huaibei for Anhui intra-province land market dynamics.

aCNCNFKSCQ.description: Land price level, Huainan City, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNFKSCQ.meaning: Huainan city land prices at current (nominal) values from CLPIS quarterly survey. Captures nominal transaction-price trends relevant for local developer cost and government revenue accounting in Anhui.
aCNCNFKSCQ.how_to_use: Use alongside aCNCNIDZRQ to compute Huainan land price inflation rate; sustained nominal-real convergence confirms deflationary pressure from coal-sector demand retreat.

aCNCNYTAGQ.description: Land price level, Jixi city, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNYTAGQ.meaning: Land price level for Jixi city (Heilongjiang province, Northeast China), a coal and graphite mining hub facing long-term population outflow. Tracks land demand conditions in one of China's most economically challenged rust-belt cities.
aCNCNYTAGQ.how_to_use: Jixi land prices, like Hegang, serve as a stress-test benchmark for Northeast deflation; persistent declines confirm structural headwinds that require central transfer payments to sustain local fiscal health.

aCNCNQAUZQ.description: Land price level, Jixi city, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNQAUZQ.meaning: Jixi city land prices at current nominal values, from CLPIS quarterly reports. Given Jixi's weak real demand, nominal series may show near-zero or declining trends reflecting both real and price deflation.
aCNCNQAUZQ.how_to_use: Cross-reference with real-price Jixi series (aCNCNYTAGQ) to isolate price inflation from volume; compare across Heilongjiang cities to assess province-wide property market stress.

aCNCNDELJQ.meaning: Land price level for North China (Beijing, Tianjin, Hebei, Shanxi, Inner Mongolia), a region combining the nation's political capital premium with heavy industrial cities. Captures differentiated demand across tier-1 (Beijing) and industrial cities.
aCNCNDELJQ.how_to_use: North China land price is heavily distorted by Beijing's administrative land-supply restrictions; strip out Beijing effects to assess Hebei/Inner Mongolia industrial land dynamics relative to national cycle.

aCNCNDIDQ.meaning: Land price level for Northeast China (Liaoning, Jilin, Heilongjiang), the historic rust-belt region with chronic population outflow and weak demand. Northeast aggregate land prices have trended down since 2014 in real terms.
aCNCNDIDQ.how_to_use: Northeast land prices are a leading indicator of regional property developer distress; sustained drops signal deeper fiscal stress for Liaoning/Jilin/Heilongjiang local governments reliant on land-sale revenue.

aCNCNQHMPQ.meaning: Land price level for Northwest China (Shaanxi, Gansu, Qinghai, Ningxia, Xinjiang), a resource-rich but sparsely populated region whose land market is driven by energy and Belt-and-Road infrastructure investment.
aCNCNQHMPQ.how_to_use: Northwest land prices respond to energy commodity cycles and central policy for western development (Xi Bu Da Kai Fa); lag coastal regions by 2-4 quarters in policy transmission.

aCNCNSBYJQ.description: Land price level, Pearl River Delta Economic Zone, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNSBYJQ.subcategory: Land Prices — Pearl River Delta Economic Zone
aCNCNSBYJQ.meaning: Land price level for the Pearl River Delta (PRD) Economic Zone (Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Dongguan, Foshan, etc.), China's export manufacturing and tech hub. PRD land prices reflect global supply-chain dynamics and tech-sector real-estate demand.
aCNCNSBYJQ.how_to_use: PRD land prices lead South China housing CPI; Shenzhen policy experiments (property tax pilots, land reform) often precede national rollout — monitor for early signals of structural property policy change.

aCNCNMYWKQ.description: Land price level, Pearl River Delta Economic Zone, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNMYWKQ.subcategory: Land Prices — Pearl River Delta (Current Prices)
aCNCNMYWKQ.meaning: Pearl River Delta land prices at current (nominal) prices, capturing actual developer acquisition costs and government land-sale revenues in Guangdong's core economic zone at prevailing nominal values.
aCNCNMYWKQ.how_to_use: PRD nominal land prices are directly visible in Guangdong local government fiscal data; divergence from real price series signals price inflation or deflation within the zone's property cycle.

aCNCNSCXIQ.description: Land price level, Qiqihar city, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNSCXIQ.meaning: Land price level for Qiqihar city (Heilongjiang province), a heavy-machinery and agricultural processing centre in China's grain belt. Land prices reflect both industrial demand and agricultural land-use conversion dynamics.
aCNCNSCXIQ.how_to_use: Monitor Qiqihar land prices alongside Northeast regional aggregate; agricultural policy allowing rural collective land transfer can produce step-changes in peri-urban land prices here.

aCNCNUEXUQ.description: Land price level, Qiqihar city, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNUEXUQ.meaning: Qiqihar city land prices at current nominal prices from CLPIS. Reflects actual CNY transaction values in the city's land auction market, used for local revenue and developer cost accounting.
aCNCNUEXUQ.how_to_use: Pair with aCNCNSCXIQ real-price series; if nominal prices rise faster than real, it suggests local price inflation rather than genuine demand recovery in Qiqihar.

aCNCNMSQPQ.meaning: Land price level for Shunde District (Foshan city, Guangdong), one of China's wealthiest county-level economies and home to major appliance manufacturers (Midea, Galanz). Shunde land prices reflect premium demand from high-value manufacturing.
aCNCNMSQPQ.how_to_use: Shunde is a bellwether for Pearl River Delta industrial land demand; rising prices here alongside PRD aggregate confirm manufacturing investment cycle in South China, influencing CPI through import-competing goods.

aCNCNFVIQ.meaning: Land price level for Southwest China (Sichuan, Yunnan, Guizhou, Chongqing, Tibet), a region experiencing rapid urbanisation around Chengdu-Chongqing economic circle. Land prices here outperformed national average in 2020-22 on strong infrastructure spending.
aCNCNFVIQ.how_to_use: Southwest land prices are a proxy for Chengdu-Chongqing dual-city circle success; rising prices confirm policy-directed urban expansion absorbing coastal industrial relocation.

aCNCNLRKNQ.meaning: Broad Western China land price level index, encompassing both Southwest and Northwest sub-regions. Captures the aggregate effect of western development (XiBuDaKaiFa) policies and Belt-and-Road corridor investment on land values.
aCNCNLRKNQ.how_to_use: Compare Western vs Eastern land price spread to assess policy-driven convergence; narrowing gap indicates successful fiscal transfer and investment stimulus reaching interior provinces.

aCNCNSWSFQ.description: Land price level, Xinxiang city, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNSWSFQ.meaning: Land price level for Xinxiang city (Henan province, Central Plains), an industrial city in the Zhengzhou metropolitan area corridor. Land prices track Zhengzhou spillover demand and Central Plains manufacturing investment.
aCNCNSWSFQ.how_to_use: Rising Xinxiang land prices signal successful Zhengzhou metropolitan expansion; monitor against provincial aggregate for Central Plains development policy effectiveness.

aCNCNEAEX/A.description: Land price level, Xinxiang city, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNEAEX/A.meaning: Xinxiang city land prices at current nominal values, reporting actual CNY transaction prices from government land auctions in this Henan city. Nominal series reflects prevailing price levels for developer budget and municipal revenue purposes.
aCNCNEAEX/A.how_to_use: Pair with aCNCNSWSFQ constant-price series; widening nominal-real gap in Xinxiang indicates local price inflation driven by construction cost increases in Central China.

aCNCNDZQFQ.description: Land price level, Yangtze River Delta Economic Zone
aCNCNDZQFQ.subcategory: Land Prices — Yangtze River Delta Economic Zone
aCNCNDZQFQ.meaning: Land price level for the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) Economic Zone (Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Anhui), China's most integrated regional economy. YRD land prices command a structural premium over national average due to supply constraints and high productivity.
aCNCNDZQFQ.how_to_use: YRD land prices feed directly into Shanghai housing cost and consumer rents in the CPI basket; a 5%+ quarterly decline is a strong signal of developer deleveraging affecting East China housing CPI.

aCNCNRQZQ.description: Land price level, Yichun city, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNRQZQ.meaning: Land price level for Yichun city (Heilongjiang province), a forestry and tourism city in Northeast China with severely limited industrial base. One of the lower land price markets in China reflecting population decline and limited urban demand.
aCNCNRQZQ.how_to_use: Yichun prices provide the low-end anchor for Northeast China land market analysis; sustained near-zero values confirm that fiscal-transfer-dependent cities cannot generate organic property price recovery.

aCNCNLRTQ.description: Land price level, Yichun city, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNLRTQ.meaning: Yichun city land prices at current nominal prices from CLPIS quarterly survey. Given the city's structurally weak demand, nominal and real price series tend to move in close parallel, with little inflation wedge.
aCNCNLRTQ.how_to_use: Track for any nominal price recovery driven by central/provincial subsidies to Yichun redevelopment; positive nominal-real gap would signal externally injected price support rather than organic demand.

aCNCNBTFFQ.description: Land use price level, Bohai Economic Zone
aCNCNBTFFQ.subcategory: Land Use Prices — Bohai Economic Zone
aCNCNBTFFQ.meaning: Land use right price level for the Bohai Economic Zone from CLPIS — distinct from land transaction prices, this measures the cost of land-use right leases and renewals in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei corridor. Reflects ongoing occupancy cost for industrial and commercial users.
aCNCNBTFFQ.how_to_use: Rising land use prices in Bohai indicate tightening supply of industrial land in the BTH integration zone; feeds into manufacturing cost-push CPI pressure in North China.

aCNCNNIPWQ.description: Land use price level, Central Region
aCNCNNIPWQ.meaning: Land use right price level for Central China (Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Shanxi, Anhui) from CLPIS. Central region land use costs reflect the pivot of China's manufacturing base inland and demand from logistics hubs.
aCNCNNIPWQ.how_to_use: Central China land use prices rising faster than transaction prices suggests incumbent occupier demand outpacing new auction supply; positive for local government fiscal but negative for manufacturing cost inflation.

aCNCNQRGHQ.description: Land use price level, Central South
aCNCNQRGHQ.meaning: Land use right price level for Central South China, covering Hunan, Hubei, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan from CLPIS. Reflects land occupancy costs across a diverse region ranging from PRD tech clusters to interior agricultural land.
aCNCNQRGHQ.how_to_use: PRD industrial land use price premium vs. Central South regional average signals Guangdong's supply-constrained tech cluster; use to assess cost competitiveness for manufacturing relocation decisions.

aCNCNDBEQ.description: Land use price level, East area
aCNCNDBEQ.meaning: Land use right price level for East China (YRD and Fujian) from CLPIS, measuring the cost of leasing or renewing land-use rights in China's highest-value coastal cluster. East area land use prices are the national benchmark for commercial and industrial occupancy costs.
aCNCNDBEQ.how_to_use: Elevated East area land use prices relative to other regions drive manufacturing migration inland; monitor trend for evidence of Shanghai-Jiangsu cost-push transmission into services CPI.

aCNCNDGDQQ.description: Land use price level, Fushun city, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNDGDQQ.meaning: Land use right price level for Fushun city (Liaoning) from CLPIS quarterly survey. Measures ongoing occupancy costs for industrial and commercial tenants in a Northeast transitional economy city.
aCNCNDGDQQ.how_to_use: Fushun land use prices persistently below national average confirm limited investor confidence; use alongside land transaction price for city-level real estate stress assessment.

aCNCNOZBPQ.description: Land use price level, Fushun city, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNOZBPQ.subcategory: Land Use Prices — Fushun City (Current Prices)
aCNCNOZBPQ.meaning: Fushun city land use right prices at current nominal values from CLPIS. Nominal series captures actual CNY lease-cost levels prevailing in Fushun's commercial and industrial property market.
aCNCNOZBPQ.how_to_use: Compare with constant-price Fushun land use series (aCNCNDGDQQ) to assess real occupancy-cost trends; persistent nominal decline confirms structural demand destruction in Fushun.

aCNCNLGNIQ.description: Land use price level, Fuxin city, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNLGNIQ.meaning: Land use right price level for Fuxin city (Liaoning) from CLPIS, reflecting industrial and commercial occupancy costs in a coal-transition city. Land use prices in Fuxin are among the lowest in Liaoning province.
aCNCNLGNIQ.how_to_use: Monitor alongside land transaction prices in Fuxin; divergence between use-right cost and transaction price signals whether demand is from new development or existing occupiers renewing leases.

aCNCNHMJM/A.description: Land use price level, Fuxin city, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNHMJM/A.subcategory: Land Use Prices — Fuxin City (Current Prices)
aCNCNHMJM/A.meaning: Fuxin city land use right prices at current nominal values, published by CLPIS. Captures nominal lease-cost trends in one of Liaoning's most economically challenged cities for property market stress monitoring.
aCNCNHMJM/A.how_to_use: Pair with aCNCNLGNIQ for real vs. nominal comparison; very low absolute values confirm Fuxin's land market is not self-sustaining without central fiscal support.

aCNCNMQQFQ.description: Land use price level, Handan city, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNMQQFQ.meaning: Land use right price level for Handan city (Hebei) from CLPIS, capturing occupancy costs for steel-industry and logistics tenants in this Bohai-adjacent industrial hub. Land use prices reflect post-capacity-cut industrial restructuring.
aCNCNMQQFQ.how_to_use: Rising Handan land use prices alongside rebar index recovery (aCNCNVRGRM) confirm steel-sector consolidation is supporting industrial property demand in Hebei.

aCNCNACMUQ.description: Land use price level, Handan city, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNACMUQ.subcategory: Land Use Prices — Handan City (Current Prices)
aCNCNACMUQ.meaning: Handan city land use right prices at current nominal values, reflecting actual CNY occupancy costs for industrial tenants in a post-restructuring Hebei city. Used for local government land-lease revenue accounting.
aCNCNACMUQ.how_to_use: Nominal-real spread for Handan land use prices provides a local inflation indicator for Hebei industrial belt; use alongside BTH regional aggregate for Hebei-specific analysis.

aCNCNEBXQ.description: Land use price level, Hegang city, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNEBXQ.meaning: Land use right price level for Hegang city (Heilongjiang) from CLPIS. In a city where residential transaction prices collapsed to near CNY 10,000/unit, commercial land use right costs are similarly depressed, reflecting near-zero investor demand.
aCNCNEBXQ.how_to_use: Hegang land use prices are a stress-test floor reference for Northeast China commercial real estate; sustained very-low readings confirm the city is in structural property deflation with no near-term recovery catalyst.

aCNCNUPGIQ.description: Land use price level, Hegang city, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNUPGIQ.subcategory: Land Use Prices — Hegang City (Current Prices)
aCNCNUPGIQ.meaning: Hegang city land use right prices at current nominal values from CLPIS. Nominal and real series in Hegang tend to converge at near-zero levels, confirming both real deflation and near-zero nominal price change.
aCNCNUPGIQ.how_to_use: Use in stress-test scenario analysis for Northeast China property debt exposure; any nominal pickup above near-zero would be notable news for Heilongjiang province recovery.

aCNCNSHOIQ.description: Land use price level, Hengyang city, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNSHOIQ.meaning: Land use right price level for Hengyang city (Hunan) from CLPIS, measuring commercial and industrial occupancy costs in a Central South city benefiting from coastal industry relocation. Use-right prices reflect steady mid-tier urban growth.
aCNCNSHOIQ.how_to_use: Rising Hengyang land use prices alongside Central South aggregate signal successful industry absorption in interior Hunan; compare with transaction price (aCNCNKUWMQ) to assess new vs. renewal demand balance.

aCNCNEAUTQ.description: Land use price level, Hengyang city, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNEAUTQ.subcategory: Land Use Prices — Hengyang City (Current Prices)
aCNCNEAUTQ.meaning: Hengyang city land use right prices at current nominal values from CLPIS. Reflects actual CNY lease costs for commercial and industrial occupants in Hunan's second-largest city, used for local revenue and developer cost modelling.
aCNCNEAUTQ.how_to_use: Compare to aCNCNSHOIQ real-price series; a widening nominal-real gap confirms local service-sector inflation contributing to consumer cost pressures in Hengyang.

aCNCNHTKXQ.description: Land use price level, Huadong Region
aCNCNHTKXQ.meaning: Land use right price level for the Huadong (East China) region from CLPIS, covering YRD and Fujian. The highest regional land use price in China, reflecting intense competition for commercial and industrial space in the Yangtze Delta.
aCNCNHTKXQ.how_to_use: Huadong land use prices feed directly into East China logistics, retail, and industrial cost structures, contributing to services CPI in Shanghai and surrounding cities; 5%+ quarterly moves are market-moving for commercial REITs.

aCNCNJDURQ.description: Land use price level, Huaibei City, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNJDURQ.meaning: Land use right price level for Huaibei city (Anhui) from CLPIS, tracking commercial and industrial occupancy costs in a Yangtze Delta hinterland coal city undergoing transition. YRD integration drives external demand for Huaibei industrial parks.
aCNCNJDURQ.how_to_use: Monitor for rising use-right prices signalling successful YRD supply-chain relocation to Huaibei's lower-cost industrial parks; compare to YRD regional use-price for cost-differential analysis.

aCNCNHCSUQ.description: Land use price level, Huaibei City, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNHCSUQ.subcategory: Land Use Prices — Huaibei City (Current Prices)
aCNCNHCSUQ.meaning: Huaibei city land use right prices at current nominal values from CLPIS quarterly survey. Captures actual CNY lease-cost levels for Huaibei's transitioning coal and logistics industries.
aCNCNHCSUQ.how_to_use: Pair with aCNCNJDURQ real series to compute local land-use inflation in Anhui; nominal-real divergence signals whether restructuring is producing genuine real occupancy-cost improvement.

aCNCNPZFQ.description: Land use price level, Huainan City, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNPZFQ.meaning: Land use right price level for Huainan city (Anhui) from CLPIS, measuring occupancy costs as the city transitions from coal to data centres and green energy. Structural industry change creates demand for new types of industrial land use.
aCNCNPZFQ.how_to_use: Rising land use prices for non-coal industrial categories in Huainan signal successful diversification; compare to transaction price (aCNCNIDZRQ) to assess whether new tenants are buying or leasing.

aCNCNUABRQ.description: Land use price level, Huainan City, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNUABRQ.subcategory: Land Use Prices — Huainan City (Current Prices)
aCNCNUABRQ.meaning: Huainan city land use right prices at current nominal values from CLPIS. Reflects CNY occupancy-cost trends in Anhui's largest coal-transition city, used for local government lease-revenue and corporate real-estate cost budgeting.
aCNCNUABRQ.how_to_use: Nominal-real gap comparison with aCNCNPZFQ reveals local service-sector inflation; use alongside Huainan current-price transaction series for a complete cost picture of the city's property market.

aCNCNZACEQ.description: Land use price level, Jixi city, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNZACEQ.meaning: Land use right price level for Jixi city (Heilongjiang) from CLPIS, tracking commercial and industrial occupancy costs in this graphite-mining and coal city facing population decline. Land use prices are structurally depressed.
aCNCNZACEQ.how_to_use: Jixi land use prices reinforce the Northeast deflation narrative alongside transaction prices; graphite-industry demand (EV battery supply chain) could be a nascent recovery driver to watch.

aCNCNYBWQ/A.description: Land use price level, Jixi city, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNYBWQ/A.subcategory: Land Use Prices — Jixi City (Current Prices)
aCNCNYBWQ/A.meaning: Jixi city land use right prices at current nominal values from CLPIS. Given Jixi's very weak demand, both nominal and real land use prices tend toward the national floor, with any uplift likely policy-driven.
aCNCNYBWQ/A.how_to_use: Use as a tracking series for EV-supply-chain investment (graphite anode demand) lifting Jixi's property market; any sustained nominal-real convergence above historic lows would be a positive development signal.

aCNCNDQSVQ.description: Land use price level, North China
aCNCNDQSVQ.meaning: Land use right price level for North China (Beijing, Tianjin, Hebei, Shanxi, Inner Mongolia) from CLPIS, measuring commercial and industrial occupancy costs across the region. Beijing's premium elevates the regional average significantly above the national median.
aCNCNDQSVQ.how_to_use: Monitor for divergence between Beijing-driven premium and Hebei/Inner Mongolia industrial use-right prices; BTH integration policy narrowing this gap would signal successful regional development and industrial cost redistribution.

aCNCNFSFQQ.description: Land use price level, North-west region
aCNCNFSFQQ.meaning: Quarterly land-use price level for China's Northwest region (Shaanxi, Gansu, Qinghai, Ningxia, Xinjiang), sourced from the China Land Price Information Service Platform. Captures urban land transaction costs that feed into housing and construction cost components of CPI.
aCNCNFSFQQ.how_to_use: Compare with east-coast equivalents (Yangtze Delta, Pearl River Delta) to gauge regional divergence; sustained weakness signals subdued local property markets and limited pass-through to rent CPI.

aCNCNNTAQ.description: Land use price level, Pearl River Delta Economic Zone, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNNTAQ.subcategory: Land Use Price — Pearl River Delta
aCNCNNTAQ.meaning: Land-use price level for the Pearl River Delta Economic Zone (Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Dongguan cluster), published quarterly by the China Land Price Information Service Platform. Reflects commercial and residential land demand in China's premier manufacturing export corridor.
aCNCNNTAQ.how_to_use: Track alongside Guangdong provincial CPI for rent pass-through signals; a sustained drop in Pearl River Delta land prices typically leads residential rent softness by 2-4 quarters.

aCNCNBQDUQ.description: Land use price level, Pearl River Delta Economic Zone, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNBQDUQ.subcategory: Land Use Price — Pearl River Delta (Current Prices)
aCNCNBQDUQ.meaning: Pearl River Delta land-use price in current (nominal) CNY per square metre, from the China Land Price Information Service Platform. Nominal series without index adjustment, useful for absolute price-level comparisons across economic zones.
aCNCNBQDUQ.how_to_use: Use alongside the index-based PRD series (aCNCNNTAQ) to decompose real vs. nominal land cost trends; divergence may indicate price deflation pressures feeding into the housing CPI sub-component.

aCNCNUBICQ.description: Land use price level, Qiqihar city, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNUBICQ.meaning: Quarterly land-use price index for Qiqihar, a heavy-industry city in Heilongjiang province, sourced from the China Land Price Information Service Platform. Reflects conditions in northeast China's rust-belt urban land market.
aCNCNUBICQ.how_to_use: Use as a proxy for tier-3/4 city land market stress in the northeast; sustained index decline correlates with local government fiscal pressure and weak developer activity, which can dampen local services CPI.

aCNCNNVRQ.description: Land use price level, Qiqihar city, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNNVRQ.subcategory: Land Use Price — Qiqihar City (Current Prices)
aCNCNNVRQ.meaning: Nominal current-price land transaction value for Qiqihar city (Heilongjiang), from the China Land Price Information Service Platform. Provides an undeflated measure of local land market activity and developer appetite.
aCNCNNVRQ.how_to_use: Compare with the Qiqihar index series (aCNCNUBICQ) to isolate nominal vs. real land price trends; sharp nominal declines indicate distressed local government land auctions, a leading indicator of fiscal strain.

aCNCNIKBPQ.description: Land use price level, Shunde District
aCNCNIKBPQ.meaning: Quarterly land-use price index for Shunde District (Foshan, Guangdong), a major appliance and furniture manufacturing hub, from the China Land Price Information Service Platform. Reflects industrial and commercial land costs in the Pearl River Delta hinterland.
aCNCNIKBPQ.how_to_use: Monitor for signals on Guangdong manufacturing-zone land cost inflation, which can lead changes in durable-goods CPI components via input costs; compare with broader PRD series to gauge sub-regional divergence.

aCNCNGJSIQ.description: Land use price level, Southwest Region
aCNCNGJSIQ.meaning: Quarterly land-use price level for China's Southwest region (Sichuan, Chongqing, Yunnan, Guizhou, Tibet), from the China Land Price Information Service Platform. Tracks the urbanisation-driven land market in China's fastest-developing interior zone.
aCNCNGJSIQ.how_to_use: Chengdu-Chongqing corridor land momentum often leads southwest regional CPI rent components by 2-3 quarters; sustained rises signal durable domestic demand expansion in the interior.

aCNCNIIMOQ.description: Land use price level, Western Region
aCNCNIIMOQ.meaning: Quarterly land-use price level for China's broader Western region (includes Northwest + Southwest, i.e. 12 provinces/municipalities), published by the China Land Price Information Service Platform. Serves as the composite western interior benchmark.
aCNCNIIMOQ.how_to_use: Use as a macro-level view of interior China land market conditions; compare East-West spreads to assess policy-driven regional investment flows (e.g., Belt and Road domestic extension, westward industrial relocation).

aCNCNDSKXQ.description: Land use price level, Xinxiang city, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNDSKXQ.meaning: Quarterly land-use price index for Xinxiang city (Henan province), a mid-size central China industrial and agricultural hub, from the China Land Price Information Service Platform.
aCNCNDSKXQ.how_to_use: Track alongside Henan provincial CPI; Xinxiang's land market reflects central China's agricultural-industrial economy — softness may precede downward pressure on local housing CPI.

aCNCNDMMXQ.description: Land use price level, Xinxiang city, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNDMMXQ.subcategory: Land Use Price — Xinxiang City (Current Prices)
aCNCNDMMXQ.meaning: Nominal current-price land value for Xinxiang city (Henan), from the China Land Price Information Service Platform. Provides an absolute price benchmark for central China tier-3 land market transactions.
aCNCNDMMXQ.how_to_use: Pair with the index series (aCNCNDSKXQ) to distinguish inflation from real demand; Henan land prices often track migration-driven urbanisation — divergence with index signals deflation in the local market.

aCNCNFCAVQ.description: Land use price level, Yangtze River Delta Economic Zone
aCNCNFCAVQ.subcategory: Land Use Price — Yangtze River Delta
aCNCNFCAVQ.meaning: Quarterly land-use price level for the Yangtze River Delta Economic Zone (Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Anhui), from the China Land Price Information Service Platform. Tracks the most commercially intense land market outside Tier-1 cities.
aCNCNFCAVQ.how_to_use: The YRD land price index leads eastern China housing rent CPI by roughly 2-4 quarters; compare with Pearl River Delta (aCNCNNTAQ) to assess relative property cycle positioning across China's two major megacity clusters.

aCNCNYXLFQ.description: Land use price level, Yichun city, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNYXLFQ.meaning: Quarterly land-use price index for Yichun city (Heilongjiang), a forestry-based declining industrial city in northeast China, from the China Land Price Information Service Platform.
aCNCNYXLFQ.how_to_use: Yichun is among China's most economically distressed tier-4 cities; near-zero or negative land price readings indicate severe population outflow and suppressed local demand — relevant to northeast China regional CPI divergence analysis.

aCNCNMUFYQ.description: Land use price level, Yichun city, Current Prices, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Quarterly, China Land Price Information Service Platform
aCNCNMUFYQ.subcategory: Land Use Price — Yichun City (Current Prices)
aCNCNMUFYQ.meaning: Nominal current-price land transaction value for Yichun city (Heilongjiang), from the China Land Price Information Service Platform. Absolute price benchmark for one of northeast China's most depressed land markets.
aCNCNMUFYQ.how_to_use: Monitor for evidence of policy-induced stabilisation (e.g., northeast revitalisation subsidies); persistent near-zero values confirm structural deflationary pressure in the local economy with no near-term CPI upside.

aCNCNZFQQM.description: Average domestic market price of oil & chemical products, coke (secondary metallurgical coke)
aCNCNZFQQM.meaning: Average domestic market price of secondary metallurgical coke, a key steelmaking input, from China's oil and chemical product price monitoring. Tracks midstream industrial commodity costs with pass-through to steel and construction prices.
aCNCNZFQQM.how_to_use: Coke price moves lead steel CPI components by 1-2 months; sustained softness points to weak construction/infrastructure demand, feeding into PPI deflation and downstream consumer durables price declines.

aCNCNOOUEM.description: Average domestic market price of oil & chemical products, epdm (4045#)
aCNCNOOUEM.meaning: Average domestic market price of EPDM (Ethylene Propylene Diene Monomer) rubber grade 4045#, a synthetic rubber used in automotive seals, roofing, and consumer goods, from China's oil and chemical product price series.
aCNCNOOUEM.how_to_use: EPDM tracks crude oil and ethylene feedstock cycles; rising prices signal upstream petrochemical cost push into consumer durables and auto parts, though direct CPI pass-through is diffuse and lagged.

aCNCNMIGBM.description: Average domestic market price of oil & chemical products, formaldehyde (primary, clean water)
aCNCNMIGBM.meaning: Average domestic market price of primary-grade formaldehyde (clean water solution), a key input to resins, adhesives, and furniture manufacturing, from China's oil and chemical price monitoring.
aCNCNMIGBM.how_to_use: Formaldehyde prices track methanol and natural gas feedstock cycles; sustained declines indicate weak real-estate-related demand (furniture, construction materials), consistent with property sector deflation in housing CPI.

aCNCCPIPE/A.description: CPI, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
aCNCCPIPE/A.meaning: CPI Month-over-Month — high-frequency inflation pulse. Volatile (food + holiday seasonality dominates).
aCNCCPIPE/A.how_to_use: Smooth with 3-month average. Lunar New Year timing (January or February) drives Q1 distortions. Markets watch annualized 3-month MoM as a smoothed momentum gauge.

aCNCCPIPF.description: CPI, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
aCNCCPIPF.meaning: CPI MoM — alternative release. Same conceptual measure as aCNCCPIPE/A.
aCNCCPIPF.how_to_use: Cross-check against the primary release. Use whichever has fresher data; methodology and timing differences across releases are typically minor and resolved on revision.

aCNCCPIYE/A.description: CPI, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aCNCCPIYE/A.meaning: Headline Consumer Price Index, year-over-year change — the headline China inflation print. Released monthly by NBS ~10th of each month with 1-month lag.
aCNCCPIYE/A.how_to_use: THE most-watched China inflation gauge. Pre-2018 ranged 1-3%; turned negative 2023-24 (-0.5% to +0.5%) — China's first deflation in decades. PBoC's implicit comfort zone is 1-3%. Surprise vs Reuters consensus moves CNY and CGB yields. Pork prices (~3% of basket) drive much of the cyclical noise.

aCNCCPIYF.description: CPI, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aCNCCPIYF.meaning: CPI YoY — alternative release. Same conceptual measure as aCNCCPIYE/A.
aCNCCPIYF.how_to_use: Cross-check against the primary release. Use whichever has fresher data; methodology and timing differences across releases are typically minor and resolved on revision.

aCNCCPIF/C.how_to_use: Cross-check against the primary release. Use whichever has fresher data; methodology and timing differences across releases are typically minor and resolved on revision.

aCNCCPIE/CA.meaning: CPI level — index measure of consumer prices. NBS uses chain-weighted methodology with rolling base updates.
aCNCCPIE/CA.how_to_use: Use YoY (aCNCCPIYE/A) for trend; level for analytical baseline. China deflation 2023-24 visible as negative YoY moves in this series.

aCNCNULLRQ.description: Star hotel room average room rate, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region
aCNCNULLRQ.meaning: Average star-hotel room rate in Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, published quarterly. Tracks travel-services inflation in a resource-rich border region with significant business and tourist flows.
aCNCNULLRQ.how_to_use: Hotel rates are a real-time services-CPI proxy; Inner Mongolia's rates are sensitive to coal/mining business cycles and seasonal tourism — compare with national hotel price indices to assess regional divergence in services inflation.

aCNCNWEDXQ.description: Star hotel room average room rate, Jiangsu Province
aCNCNWEDXQ.meaning: Average star-hotel room rate across Jiangsu province (Nanjing, Suzhou, Wuxi), published quarterly. Jiangsu is China's second-largest provincial economy; hotel rates here are a bellwether for YRD business travel and convention activity.
aCNCNWEDXQ.how_to_use: Track alongside Jiangsu services CPI; elevated Jiangsu rates vs. national average signal strong corporate travel demand and domestic consumption recovery — relevant to the recreation and travel sub-component of CPI.

aCNCNEDONQ.description: Star hotel room average room rate, Jiangxi Province
aCNCNEDONQ.meaning: Average star-hotel room rate across Jiangxi province, a central China province with significant tourism (Lushan, Jingdezhen) and manufacturing activity, published quarterly.
aCNCNEDONQ.how_to_use: Jiangxi hotel rates capture mid-tier domestic tourism and manufacturing business travel; compare with coastal provinces (aCNCNWEDXQ) to gauge inland-coastal services-price convergence or divergence.

aCNCNMBKQQ.description: Star hotel room average room rate, one-star, Jiangxi Province
aCNCNMBKQQ.meaning: Average one-star hotel room rate in Jiangxi province, published quarterly. One-star rates capture the budget end of the accommodation market, more reflective of domestic migrant-worker and low-income travel costs.
aCNCNMBKQQ.how_to_use: One-star rates are a proxy for lower-income consumer services inflation; compare with all-star average (aCNCNEDONQ) to identify polarisation — widening spreads may signal K-shaped services price recovery.

aCNCNIDRFQ.description: Star hotel room average room rate, one-star, Jilin Province
aCNCNIDRFQ.meaning: Average one-star hotel room rate in Jilin province (northeast China), published quarterly. Reflects budget accommodation pricing in a slow-growth northeastern province with significant out-migration.
aCNCNIDRFQ.how_to_use: Jilin's one-star hotel rates benchmark the northeast's low-end services economy; persistent deflation vs. national average confirms structural demand weakness and contracting local services CPI.

aCNPFAPA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Apples (Fuji apple)
aCNPFAPA.meaning: Average retail price of Fuji apples across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM). Fuji apples are China's dominant variety and a standard fruit-price benchmark in the food CPI basket.
aCNPFAPA.how_to_use: Apple prices exhibit pronounced seasonal cycles (lowest post-harvest Oct-Dec, highest May-Jul); use YoY change to control for seasonality. Sustained price declines indicate oversupply or weak consumer demand in the fresh-fruit CPI sub-component.

aCNPFBAA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Bananas (domestic products)
aCNPFBAA.meaning: Average retail price of domestic bananas across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Domestic banana supply is concentrated in Yunnan, Guangdong and Guangxi; prices are sensitive to typhoon damage and import competition.
aCNPFBAA.how_to_use: Banana prices are a leading indicator of tropical fruit CPI volatility; spikes following Hainan or Yunnan weather disruptions typically reverse within 1-2 months. Compare with apple prices to assess broad fresh-fruit basket direction.

aCNPFBEA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Beef(leg)
aCNPFBEA.meaning: Average retail price of beef (leg cut) across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Beef consumption has grown rapidly with rising incomes; prices reflect both domestic cattle supply and import volumes.
aCNPFBEA.how_to_use: Beef prices tend to trend structurally higher as dietary upgrading continues; watch for import policy changes (Brazil/Australia quotas) as drivers of sudden deflation. Compare with pork (aCNPFPBA) to assess meat-basket substitution dynamics.

aCNPFCEA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Celeries
aCNPFCEA.meaning: Average retail price of celery across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Celery is a staple Chinese vegetable with high-frequency price swings driven by planting cycles, weather and transport costs.
aCNPFCEA.how_to_use: Celery price volatility is a proxy for the 'vegetable shock' component of food CPI; extreme moves (common in winter months) are largely supply-driven and typically mean-revert within 4-8 weeks.

aCNPFCBA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Chickens(breast)
aCNPFCBA.meaning: Average retail price of chicken breast across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Chicken breast is a premium cut whose pricing reflects rising protein demand and poultry industry consolidation.
aCNPFCBA.how_to_use: Chicken breast price divergence from whole-chicken prices (aCNPFCCA) signals premiumisation trends in the poultry market; track alongside feed cost proxies (corn, soybean) for margin pressure signals.

aCNPFCCA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Chickens(frozen fresh chicken)
aCNPFCCA.meaning: Average retail price of frozen/fresh whole chicken across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Serves as the benchmark poultry price in the food CPI basket and tracks the full supply chain from farm to retail.
aCNPFCCA.how_to_use: Whole chicken prices are sensitive to AI (avian influenza) outbreaks and seasonal demand spikes (Chinese New Year); compare with chicken breast (aCNPFCBA) spread to identify supply-chain margins and processing-industry health.

aCNPFCHA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Chinese cabbages
aCNPFCHA.meaning: Average retail price of Chinese cabbage (bai cai) across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Chinese cabbage is the highest-volume vegetable in Chinese diets and a key weight in the food CPI vegetable sub-basket.
aCNPFCHA.how_to_use: Chinese cabbage prices have extreme seasonal and weather sensitivity; the 'cabbage effect' can swing food CPI by 0.1-0.3 ppt in a single month. Use to flag weather-driven food CPI noise vs. structural demand shifts.

aCNPFCUA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Cucumbers
aCNPFCUA.meaning: Average retail price of cucumbers across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Cucumbers are a year-round greenhouse vegetable with relatively stable but seasonally varying prices.
aCNPFCUA.how_to_use: Cucumber prices are useful for tracking greenhouse vegetable inflation, which responds to energy costs (heating) and planting decisions; winter spikes signal input-cost pass-through rather than demand-pull.

aCNPFDUA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Ducks(frozen fresh duck)
aCNPFDUA.meaning: Average retail price of frozen/fresh whole duck across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Duck consumption is concentrated in southern China and is culturally important in festival-driven demand spikes.
aCNPFDUA.how_to_use: Duck prices peak around Mid-Autumn and Chinese New Year festivals; monitor year-round baseline to distinguish seasonal from structural inflation in the poultry CPI component.

aCNPFEGA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Eggs(fresh eggs in bulk)
aCNPFEGA.meaning: Average retail price of fresh bulk eggs across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Eggs are a daily staple with tight supply-demand dynamics; price is a key food CPI input and a social stability concern for policymakers.
aCNPFEGA.how_to_use: Egg prices follow a distinct seasonality (high in winter, low in autumn) and are highly sensitive to feed costs (corn/soybean); sustained moves above CNY 10/kg historically prompt market interventions to stabilise food CPI.

aCNPFFWA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Flour(standard wheat)
aCNPFFWA.meaning: Average retail price of standard wheat flour across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Standard flour is a staple grain product; its price reflects both domestic wheat harvest outcomes and government grain reserve policies.
aCNPFFWA.how_to_use: Flour prices are policy-managed (minimum purchase prices, state reserve releases) so tend to be stable; deviations from trend signal crop failures or international wheat price pass-through. Compare with strong flour (aCNPFFFA) for product-tier divergence.

aCNPFFFA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Flour(strong flour)
aCNPFFFA.meaning: Average retail price of strong (high-gluten, bread-type) wheat flour across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Strong flour commands a premium over standard flour and tracks demand from bakery and processed-food sectors.
aCNPFFFA.how_to_use: The spread between strong and standard flour prices reflects premiumisation of processed food demand; widening spread indicates rising middle-class food consumption upgrading, relevant to food services CPI.

aCNPFHTA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Hair tails
aCNPFHTA.meaning: Average retail price of hairtail (beltfish) across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Hairtail is one of China's most consumed marine fish; prices reflect East China Sea catch volumes and seasonal fishing bans.
aCNPFHTA.how_to_use: Prices spike during the May-September East China Sea fishing moratorium and moderate post-ban; structural trends are driven by overfishing and aquaculture investment. Use as a proxy for marine protein CPI sub-component direction.

aCNPFKBA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Kidney beans
aCNPFKBA.meaning: Average retail price of kidney beans across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Kidney beans are a dry legume staple; prices are influenced by domestic harvest (Yunnan, Heilongjiang) and import availability.
aCNPFKBA.how_to_use: Kidney bean prices are less volatile than fresh vegetables but track legume supply cycles; compare with soy products (aCNPFSPA) for broader protein-vegetable CPI basket assessment.

aCNPFLCA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Live carps
aCNPFLCA.meaning: Average retail price of live carp across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Live carp is the most widely consumed freshwater fish in China and a critical component of the food CPI aquatic products sub-basket.
aCNPFLCA.how_to_use: Live carp prices are sensitive to summer flood disruptions to Yangtze/Pearl River aquaculture and to Spring Festival demand surges; sustained price weakness reflects excess aquaculture supply and soft consumer demand.

aCNPFLGA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Live grass carp
aCNPFLGA.meaning: Average retail price of live grass carp across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Grass carp is a key pond-farming species and a lower-cost complement to common carp in China's freshwater aquaculture basket.
aCNPFLGA.how_to_use: Track alongside live carp (aCNPFLCA) for cross-species price dynamics; divergence may reflect species-specific disease outbreaks or feed-cost differentials. Both series are key for modelling aquatic products CPI.

aCNPFMUA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Mutton(leg)
aCNPFMUA.meaning: Average retail price of mutton leg across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Mutton is a high-value meat concentrated in northern/northwestern China (Inner Mongolia, Xinjiang); demand spikes in winter months.
aCNPFMUA.how_to_use: Mutton prices trend structurally higher due to slow herd expansion cycles (3+ year); winter demand seasonality is pronounced. Compare with beef (aCNPFBEA) for red-meat basket dynamics relevant to food CPI.

aCNPFPOA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Peanut oil(pressing)
aCNPFPOA.meaning: Average retail price of pressing-grade peanut oil across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Peanut oil is the premium cooking oil in southern and central China; prices track peanut crop harvests and consumer preferences.
aCNPFPOA.how_to_use: Peanut oil prices have lower sensitivity to global commodity cycles than soy/rapeseed oils; sharp divergence from soybean oil (aCNPFSBA) indicates domestic harvest disruption or shifting consumer demand in the edible oils CPI sub-basket.

aCNPFPBA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Pork(belly meat)
aCNPFPBA.meaning: Average retail price of pork belly across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Pork belly is the most popular pork cut in China and a bellwether for the 'pig cycle', the dominant driver of China's food CPI volatility.
aCNPFPBA.how_to_use: Monitor alongside pork rump (aCNPFPRA) for full-carcass price dynamics. The pig cycle (18-24 month herd rebuild after ASF or profit-squeeze culling) can move headline CPI by 0.5-1.0 ppt; below CNY 20/kg signals herd oversupply.

aCNPFPRA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Pork(rump)
aCNPFPRA.meaning: Average retail price of pork rump (lean cut) across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Pork rump prices move closely with belly prices but reflect lean-meat demand, which tracks rising health-consciousness among urban consumers.
aCNPFPRA.how_to_use: Track alongside belly (aCNPFPBA) to compute the lean/fatty spread — a widening premium for lean meat signals dietary upgrading. Both series together provide a robust pig-cycle inflation signal for food CPI modelling.

aCNPFPTA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Potatoes
aCNPFPTA.meaning: Average retail price of potatoes across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Potatoes are a major staple crop in northern and southwestern China; prices reflect both domestic production (Gansu, Inner Mongolia, Yunnan) and seasonal storage dynamics.
aCNPFPTA.how_to_use: Potato prices follow a clear seasonal cycle (low post-autumn harvest, high in spring/early summer); use YoY data to isolate structural supply trends. Elevated prices in winter signal cold-storage shortages or crop failure.

aCNPFRSA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Rape seed oil(grade 1 in bulk)
aCNPFRSA.meaning: Average retail price of Grade 1 bulk rapeseed oil across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Rapeseed oil is the dominant cooking oil in central and southwestern China; prices link domestic canola harvests to global oilseed markets.
aCNPFRSA.how_to_use: Rapeseed oil prices are more globally linked than peanut oil — track with international canola futures and Canadian crop reports. Divergence from soybean oil (aCNPFSBA) signals domestic supply disruption vs. global feedstock shifts.

aCNPFRAA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Rapes
aCNPFRAA.meaning: Average retail price of rapeseed (whole seed/crushable rapes) across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Farm-gate rapeseed prices are a direct agricultural input cost feeding into cooking oil production.
aCNPFRAA.how_to_use: Use rapeseed prices as a leading indicator for rapeseed oil inflation (aCNPFRSA) with a ~1-month processing lag; sustained below-minimum-purchase-price readings signal policy intervention risk or structural supply surplus.

aCNPFRCA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Rice(japonica rice)
aCNPFRCA.meaning: Average retail price of japonica (short-grain) rice across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Japonica rice is the premium rice variety consumed in northern and northeastern China; prices reflect Heilongjiang/Jilin harvests.
aCNPFRCA.how_to_use: Japonica prices are sticky due to government minimum purchase prices and state reserve buffer stocks; sharp moves indicate harvest shortfalls or reserve policy changes. Compare with flour (aCNPFFWA) for grain staple inflation breadth.

aCNPFSPA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Soy products(bean curd)
aCNPFSPA.meaning: Average retail price of tofu (bean curd) across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Tofu is a daily protein staple; its price tracks soybean input costs and local manufacturing competition in the soy products CPI sub-basket.
aCNPFSPA.how_to_use: Tofu prices lag soybean prices by ~1-2 months via processing; compare with soybean oil (aCNPFSBA) to assess how soybean crush economics pass through to consumer soy products inflation.

aCNPFSBA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Soya bean oil(5 lin barrel bulk)
aCNPFSBA.meaning: Average retail price of soybean oil (5-litre barrel) across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Soybean oil is the highest-volume cooking oil in China; prices are tightly linked to US/Brazilian soybean crop forecasts and crush margins.
aCNPFSBA.how_to_use: Use alongside Chicago soybean futures as a global-to-domestic price transmission monitor; a narrowing spread between soybean oil and rapeseed oil prices (aCNPFRSA) signals convergence of domestic oilseed supply conditions.

aCNPFTMA.description: Average food price in 50 cities, Tomatoes
aCNPFTMA.meaning: Average retail price of tomatoes across 50 monitored cities, published monthly by MOFCOM. Tomatoes are a staple cooking vegetable; prices exhibit strong seasonality driven by outdoor vs. greenhouse production cycles.
aCNPFTMA.how_to_use: Tomato prices are a high-frequency CPI signal for vegetable inflation: winter peaks reflect greenhouse heating costs, summer lows reflect outdoor harvest gluts. Sharp winter spikes can add 0.05-0.1 ppt to monthly food CPI.

aCNCONPRSF.meaning: China's headline Consumer Price Index level, published monthly by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS). The broadest measure of retail consumer price changes covering the full basket of goods and services across urban and rural areas.
aCNCONPRSF.how_to_use: Use as the primary inflation reference for China; compare with PPI (aCNCPPIYE/A) to assess deflation transmission risk. Sub-0 YoY readings since late 2023 confirm deflationary pressure requiring PBoC easing.

aCNCPI.meaning: China CPI average index (period average level), published monthly by NBS. Represents the average price level across the survey period rather than a point-in-time reading, smoothing intra-period volatility.
aCNCPI.how_to_use: Use the average index for contract deflation, wage escalation clauses, and annual inflation comparisons; the point-in-time index (aCNCONPRSF) is preferable for real-time policy and market analysis.

aCNCPIYY.description: CPI, Average, Chg Y/Y, Price Index, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Monthly, National Bureau of Statistics of China
aCNCPIYY.meaning: China's headline CPI year-on-year percentage change (price index form), published monthly by NBS. The primary market-moving inflation indicator tracked by PBoC, markets and international institutions.
aCNCPIYY.how_to_use: Key threshold: below 0% triggers deflation-concern narrative; the PBoC's informal comfort zone is 1-3%. Sustained sub-1% prints since 2023 reflect post-COVID demand gap and property sector deflation — watch for inflection above 1% as recovery signal.

aCNCPIAR.description: CPI, Average, Chg Y/Y, Consumer Prices / Inflation, Monthly, National Bureau of Statistics of China
aCNCPIAR.meaning: China CPI year-on-year change calculated on the average index basis, published by NBS. Provides a smoother YoY inflation reading than the point-in-time series by averaging prices across the period.
aCNCPIAR.how_to_use: Use for annual budget planning and policy analysis requiring smoothed inflation estimates; for monthly market positioning or PBoC reaction-function analysis, prefer the point-in-time YoY series (aCNCPIYY).

aCNCPIMAR.meaning: China's headline CPI month-on-month (period-on-period) percentage change, published monthly by NBS. Provides the highest-frequency read on short-term price momentum before seasonal adjustment.
aCNCPIMAR.how_to_use: MoM CPI has strong seasonal patterns (January/February typically +0.5-1.0% for CNY, October-November typically negative); use seasonally adjusted estimates or SAAR transformations for underlying momentum analysis. Watch for 3+ consecutive negative MoM prints as a deflation acceleration signal.

aCNCPICPIP.meaning: Alternative monthly period-on-period CPI change series for China, published by NBS. This series may cover a different sub-population, vintage, or calculation methodology vs. aCNCPIMAR — verify source documentation for exact scope.
aCNCPICPIP.how_to_use: Cross-check against aCNCPIMAR to validate MoM CPI readings; persistent divergence between the two series may indicate vintage revision effects or sub-index vs. headline composition differences.

aCNCPIC.meaning: China CPI for the Clothing sub-category (average index), published monthly by NBS. Tracks retail price changes for garments, footwear and related accessories — one of the eight major CPI sub-categories.
aCNCPIC.how_to_use: Clothing CPI is structurally disinflationary in China due to domestic overcapacity and e-commerce competition; sustained deflation here is normal. Cyclical spikes typically reflect raw material (cotton, polyester) cost shocks with 2-3 month lag.

aCNCPDURAF/C.meaning: China CPI for consumer (durable) goods as a broad category, published by NBS. Aggregates price changes across tangible goods purchased by households, excluding services — an important split in China's bifurcated goods-deflation/services-inflation environment.
aCNCPDURAF/C.how_to_use: Consumer goods CPI has been in persistent deflation since 2022, driven by e-commerce price competition, weak property demand, and EV/appliance price wars; compare with services CPI to quantify the goods-services inflation split central to PBoC analysis.

aCNCPIF.meaning: China CPI for the Food sub-category (average index), published monthly by NBS. At ~21% of the CPI basket, food is the largest single sub-component and the primary driver of China's headline CPI volatility through pig cycle and vegetable price swings.
aCNCPIF.how_to_use: Food CPI is the most watched NBS CPI sub-component; a swing of 1% in food CPI moves headline CPI by ~0.21 ppt. Monitor pork (aCNPFPBA) and vegetable prices as the two highest-volatility food sub-inputs.

aCNCPIFYY.meaning: China's food CPI year-on-year percentage change, published monthly by NBS. The single most important sub-component YoY series for explaining monthly headline CPI surprises — food accounts for ~21% of the basket.
aCNCPIFYY.how_to_use: Food CPI YoY swings of ±3% are common and are the primary source of headline CPI beats/misses vs. consensus. Decompose into pork (aCNPFPBA/aCNPFPRA), fresh vegetables (aCNPFCHA) and grains to attribute the move.

aCNCPIM.description: CPI, Health care and medical services
aCNCPIM.meaning: China CPI for the Health Care and Medical Services sub-category, published monthly by NBS. This component (~8% weight) tracks hospital fees, drug prices and outpatient service costs — one of China's stickiest CPI components.
aCNCPIM.how_to_use: Medical services CPI is among the most structurally elevated CPI sub-categories in China due to ageing demographics and healthcare reform; it rarely deflates even in broader deflationary environments, supporting core CPI floors.

aCNCPNDURF/C.meaning: China CPI for home appliances (household durable goods such as white goods, electronics), published by NBS. Tracks retail price trends for major consumer electronics and appliances — a sub-component facing structural price war deflation.
aCNCPNDURF/C.how_to_use: Home appliance CPI is persistently deflationary in China (-1% to -3% YoY typical) due to manufacturing overcapacity, online price competition and subsidy-driven upgrade cycles; deep deflation here is a drag on headline CPI and corporate margins.

aCNCPIH.description: CPI, Household facilities, articles and services
aCNCPIH.meaning: China CPI for Household Facilities, Articles and Services (furniture, furnishings, household maintenance services), published monthly by NBS. Tracks price changes in goods and services related to home setup and maintenance.
aCNCPIH.how_to_use: This sub-component is closely linked to property sector activity; sustained deflation here since 2022 reflects the housing downturn reducing furniture and renovation demand. Recovery signals from this series often lag property transaction data by 2-3 months.

aCNCPNOSSF/C.meaning: China CPI for Household Services (domestic helpers, cleaning, repair, and maintenance services), published by NBS. This is a labour-intensive services sub-category, making it a useful proxy for wage-driven services inflation in China.
aCNCPNOSSF/C.how_to_use: Household services CPI tends to be one of the more resilient inflation components given labour cost stickiness; compare trend with healthcare services (aCNCPIM) and education to assess whether China's services CPI can sustain a floor even amid broader deflation.

aCNCPNMDTF/C.meaning: China CPI for Medical Services specifically (physician consultations, hospital procedures, nursing care), distinct from the broader healthcare sub-index (aCNCPIM). Published by NBS, this series isolates the services component of healthcare inflation.
aCNCPNMDTF/C.how_to_use: Medical services CPI is structurally sticky upward due to state-directed pricing reform and ageing demographics; it serves as an anchor for core services inflation even when goods deflation deepens. Use alongside household services to assess labour-market pass-through in services pricing.

aCNCPINAXFE/C.description: CPI, National average except food & energy
aCNCPINAXFE/C.meaning: China CPI: CPI, National average except food & energy. Sub-component of the Consumer Price Index basket.
aCNCPINAXFE/C.how_to_use: China CPI in deflation 2023-24 (-0.5% to +0.5% YoY). Decompose by sub-category for cyclical-noise vs structural signal: pork (~3% of basket) drives short-term volatility; services-CPI (sticky core component) is most policy-relevant.
