aCNCCORE/CA.meaning: Core CPI level — All items excluding food and energy.
aCNCCORE/CA.how_to_use: Use YoY (aCNCCORYE/A) for trend signal. Core CPI excludes volatile food and energy.

aCNCCORF/C.how_to_use: Cross-check against the primary release. Use whichever has fresher data; methodology and timing differences across releases are typically minor and resolved on revision.

aCNCCORPE/A.meaning: Core CPI MoM — sequential core-inflation pulse.
aCNCCORPE/A.how_to_use: Smooth with 3-month average. Cleaner sequential signal than headline (no food/energy noise).

aCNCCORPF.how_to_use: Cross-check against the primary release. Use whichever has fresher data; methodology and timing differences across releases are typically minor and resolved on revision.

aCNCCORYF.how_to_use: Cross-check against the primary release. Use whichever has fresher data; methodology and timing differences across releases are typically minor and resolved on revision.

aCNCCORYE/A.meaning: Core CPI, year-over-year — All items excluding food and energy. The cleanest read on underlying inflation, removing volatile pork/vegetable prices.
aCNCCORYE/A.how_to_use: PBoC's preferred underlying-inflation gauge. Has trended at 0.5-1.0% post-2020 — well below pre-2018 norm of ~2%. Sustained sub-1% core signals weak demand and persistent disinflation. Watch services component for sticky-inflation signals.

aCNCNFLMPM.description: Weighted average price-earnings ratio, A shares, Shanghai Stock Exchange
aCNCNFLMPM.meaning: China Stock Exchange: Weighted average price-earnings ratio, A shares, Shanghai Stock Exchange. Trading and listing data for Shanghai (SSE) or Shenzhen (SZSE) Stock Exchanges.
aCNCNFLMPM.how_to_use: China's two major stock exchanges. Major indices: SSE Composite (Shanghai), SZSE Composite (Shenzhen), CSI 300 (cap-weighted top 300), STAR 50 (SSE STAR Market — tech), ChiNext (SZSE growth board). Foreign access via Stock Connect.

aCNCPTARF.description: CPI, Inflation target rate, Chg Y/Y
aCNCPTARF.meaning: China CPI: CPI, Inflation target rate, Chg Y/Y. Sub-component of the Consumer Price Index basket.
aCNCPTARF.how_to_use: China CPI in deflation 2023-24 (-0.5% to +0.5% YoY). Decompose by sub-category for cyclical-noise vs structural signal: pork (~3% of basket) drives short-term volatility; services-CPI (sticky core component) is most policy-relevant.

aCNCNAQZDQ.description: 城镇储户未来物价预期指数_当期_全国

aCNHPATOTA.description: CIA 100 Cities House Price Index, House price by cities, average price in the sample, Total
aCNHPATOTA.meaning: China Index Academy (CIA) 100-city average new residential price — a high-frequency composite averaging asking/transaction prices across 100 surveyed cities, released monthly. Broader geographic coverage than the NBS 70-city index.
aCNHPATOTA.how_to_use: Use as a real-time national price benchmark; compare trend with NBS 70-city data for consistency checks — divergences often reflect tier-3/4 city dynamics not captured by NBS.

aCNHRABT.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Area, Baotou
aCNHRABT.meaning: CIA monthly residential transaction area for Baotou (Inner Mongolia) — a third-tier resource-economy city whose housing market is closely tied to coal and steel sector cycles.
aCNHRABT.how_to_use: Monitor for divergence from national trends; commodity-sector weakness tends to hit Baotou transactions harder than coastal cities, signaling demand fragility in tier-3 industrial cities.

aCNHRACQ.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Area, Chongqing
aCNHRACQ.meaning: CIA monthly residential transaction area for Chongqing — China's largest municipality by population and a key tier-1 equivalent market in the southwest with distinct policy levers including a local property tax pilot.
aCNHRACQ.how_to_use: Chongqing's large affordable housing stock and unique tax environment make it a policy bellwether; compare with aCNHRASH and aCNHRASZ to gauge southwest vs. coastal divergence.

aCNHRADG.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Area, Dongguan
aCNHRADG.meaning: CIA monthly residential transaction area for Dongguan — a tier-2 manufacturing hub in the Pearl River Delta whose housing demand is driven by migrant workers and Hong Kong/Shenzhen spillover demand.
aCNHRADG.how_to_use: Use alongside aCNHRAGZ and aCNHRASZ to construct a Pearl River Delta cluster view; weakness here often leads Guangdong-wide softening given its migrant-worker demand base.

aCNHRAGZ.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Area, Guangzhou
aCNHRAGZ.meaning: CIA monthly residential transaction area for Guangzhou — one of China's four tier-1 cities and the capital of Guangdong, with a large secondary market and relatively faster purchase restriction relaxation since 2023.
aCNHRAGZ.how_to_use: Compare with aCNHRASH and aCNHRASZ to assess tier-1 cross-city trends; Guangzhou's earlier easing of hukou and purchase restrictions makes it a leading indicator for tier-1 policy diffusion.

aCNHRANB.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Area, Ningbo
aCNHRANB.meaning: CIA monthly residential transaction area for Ningbo — a strong tier-2 port city in Zhejiang with high per-capita income and an active private enterprise base supporting housing demand.
aCNHRANB.how_to_use: Ningbo tracks closely with Zhejiang provincial trends; use with aCNHRASX (Shaoxing) to build a Yangtze Delta secondary-city composite distinct from Shanghai's premium market.

aCNHRASH.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Area, Shanghai
aCNHRASH.meaning: CIA monthly residential transaction area for Shanghai — China's largest tier-1 property market and the highest-value residential market globally by total transaction value.
aCNHRASH.how_to_use: Shanghai transactions are a confidence barometer for national housing sentiment; sustained monthly recovery here typically precedes broader tier-2 city upturn by one to two quarters.

aCNHRAST.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Area, Shantou
aCNHRAST.meaning: CIA monthly residential transaction area for Shantou — a third-tier coastal city in eastern Guangdong historically associated with the Chaoshan business community, with overseas Chinese investment influencing demand.
aCNHRAST.how_to_use: Use as a proxy for smaller coastal Guangdong city demand; compare against aCNHRADG and aCNHRAGZ to see whether Pearl River Delta dynamism is spreading to third-tier coastal cities.

aCNHRASY.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Area, Shenyang
aCNHRASY.meaning: CIA monthly residential transaction area for Shenyang — capital of Liaoning province and the largest city in Northeast China, a region suffering population outflow and persistent housing oversupply.
aCNHRASY.how_to_use: Northeast China cities like Shenyang are structural outliers — use to benchmark weak-end scenarios; sustained weakness here reflects demographic and fiscal headwinds beyond cyclical policy levers.

aCNHRASZ.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Area, Shenzhen
aCNHRASZ.meaning: CIA monthly residential transaction area for Shenzhen — the most expensive tier-1 city by price-to-income ratio, driven by tech sector demand and proximity to Hong Kong capital flows.
aCNHRASZ.how_to_use: Shenzhen leads national price cycles — a sustained transaction uptick here typically signals the leading edge of a tier-1 recovery and precedes mortgage-rate-cut transmission effects.

aCNHRATJ.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Area, Tianjin
aCNHRATJ.meaning: CIA monthly residential transaction area for Tianjin — a large tier-1 adjacent municipality near Beijing with significant industrial employment and a housing market that mirrors but lags Beijing's cycle.
aCNHRATJ.how_to_use: Tianjin historically trades at a discount to Beijing; compare with national trends to gauge whether Bohai Rim recovery is broadening beyond Beijing's core, a sign of genuine cycle turn.

aCNHRPBT.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Average price, Baotou
aCNHRPBT.meaning: CIA monthly average residential transaction price for Baotou — a commodity-linked, third-tier city in Inner Mongolia where prices reflect coal-industry income cycles.
aCNHRPBT.how_to_use: Plot against commodity price indices (coal, steel) to quantify the resource-sector price transmission into lower-tier residential markets.

aCNHRPCQ.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Average price, Chongqing
aCNHRPCQ.meaning: CIA monthly average residential transaction price for Chongqing — one of the most affordable large Chinese cities given its large affordable housing supply and property tax pilot that suppresses speculative premium.
aCNHRPCQ.how_to_use: Chongqing's affordability ratio is a natural reference for housing policy success; track against income growth to assess real purchasing power trends in inland tier-1 equivalent markets.

aCNHRPDG.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Average price, Dongguan
aCNHRPDG.meaning: CIA monthly average residential transaction price for Dongguan — a Pearl River Delta manufacturing hub where prices reflect export-sector incomes and commuter demand from Shenzhen.
aCNHRPDG.how_to_use: Compare with aCNHRPGZ and aCNHRPSZ to map the Shenzhen price spillover gradient; Dongguan's premium over Guangzhou can widen as Shenzhen buyers seek affordability.

aCNHRPGZ.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Average price, Guangzhou
aCNHRPGZ.meaning: CIA monthly average residential transaction price for Guangzhou — the most affordable of China's four tier-1 cities, benefiting from broader land supply and a less restrictive purchase environment post-2023.
aCNHRPGZ.how_to_use: Guangzhou's relative affordability makes it more sensitive to mortgage rate cuts; use as a leading signal for volume recovery ahead of more expensive tier-1 peers.

aCNHRPNB.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Average price, Ningbo
aCNHRPNB.meaning: CIA monthly average residential transaction price for Ningbo — a prosperous Zhejiang port city with private economy driven house prices typically tracking the Yangtze Delta premium tier.
aCNHRPNB.how_to_use: Ningbo prices reflect Zhejiang entrepreneur wealth effects; compare with aCNHRPSX and aCNHRPSH to gauge how regional private-sector confidence translates into local housing demand.

aCNHRPSA.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Average price, Sanya
aCNHRPSA.meaning: CIA monthly average residential transaction price for Sanya — Hainan's premier resort city where prices are driven by holiday home demand, high-income migration, and Hainan Free Trade Port incentives.
aCNHRPSA.how_to_use: Sanya is a speculative premium market; use as a sentiment indicator for wealthy household confidence — sharp corrections here signal risk-off among high-net-worth domestic buyers.

aCNHRPSH.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Average price, Shanghai
aCNHRPSH.meaning: CIA monthly average residential transaction price for Shanghai — the highest-value primary residential market in China, closely watched as the national price ceiling benchmark.
aCNHRPSH.how_to_use: Sustained price stabilization in Shanghai (the market most correlated with global financial conditions) is a prerequisite for declaring the national price downcycle has bottomed.

aCNHRPST.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Average price, Shantou
aCNHRPST.meaning: CIA monthly average residential transaction price for Shantou — an eastern Guangdong third-tier city with historically elevated prices relative to income due to overseas Chinese demand.
aCNHRPST.how_to_use: Track alongside aCNHRPSG (Shaoguan) to construct a Guangdong tier-3 average; compare with aCNHRPGZ to measure the tier-1 to tier-3 price spread within Guangdong.

aCNHRPSG.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Average price, Shaoguan
aCNHRPSG.meaning: CIA monthly average residential transaction price for Shaoguan — an inland Guangdong tier-3 city with lower price levels reflecting limited economic diversification and weak in-migration.
aCNHRPSG.how_to_use: Use as lower-bound reference for Guangdong's price distribution; gap versus aCNHRPGZ indicates affordability headroom and rural-urban convergence pace in the province.

aCNHRPSX.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Average price, Shaoxing
aCNHRPSX.meaning: CIA monthly average residential transaction price for Shaoxing — a tier-2 Zhejiang city with strong private textile and chemical industries underpinning residential demand.
aCNHRPSX.how_to_use: Compare with aCNHRPNB (Ningbo) to track intra-Zhejiang price dynamics; Shaoxing's industry-based demand is more sensitive to export-sector performance than Shanghai spillover.

aCNHRPSY.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Average price, Shenyang
aCNHRPSY.meaning: CIA monthly average residential transaction price for Shenyang — the Northeast China price bellwether reflecting demographic headwinds, population outflow, and a structurally oversupplied housing stock.
aCNHRPSY.how_to_use: Shenyang's persistent price weakness serves as a lower-bound scenario for cities facing demographic decline; useful for stress-testing policy effectiveness in structurally challenged markets.

aCNHRPSZ.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Average price, Shenzhen
aCNHRPSZ.meaning: CIA monthly average residential transaction price for Shenzhen — China's most expensive housing market by price-to-income ratio, driven by tech-sector wealth, limited land supply, and cross-border Hong Kong flows.
aCNHRPSZ.how_to_use: Shenzhen prices are the leading indicator for tier-1 national trends; recovery here, alongside Guangzhou purchase restriction removal, signals the start of a sustainable tier-1 price floor.

aCNHRPTJ.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Average price, Tianjin
aCNHRPTJ.meaning: CIA monthly average residential transaction price for Tianjin — a tier-1 adjacent municipality whose prices track Beijing with a significant discount, reflecting heavier industrial exposure and slower job growth.
aCNHRPTJ.how_to_use: Track the Beijing–Tianjin price spread as a measure of Bohai Rim housing premium concentration; narrowing spread signals improving Tianjin attractiveness relative to Beijing.

aCNHRPXA.description: CIA Real Estate Transaction Data, Average price, Xi'an
aCNHRPXA.meaning: CIA monthly average residential transaction price for Xi'an — the largest city in Northwest China, elevated by tech manufacturing investment and university-city demand since 2017–2020 boom years.
aCNHRPXA.how_to_use: Xi'an's rapid price ascent in 2017–2020 and subsequent correction make it a useful case study in policy-induced demand volatility; compare with aCNHRPCQ to assess inland tier-2 pricing dynamics.

aCNCNHTCDM.description: Power infrastructure investment completion, Current Prices, Housing & Real Estate Prices, Monthly, NEA - National Energy Administration, China
aCNCNHTCDM.meaning: Power infrastructure investment completion at current prices — National Energy Administration (NEA) monthly series tracking actual spending on completed power grid and generation projects.
aCNCNHTCDM.how_to_use: Use as a proxy for grid-infrastructure build-out intensity; compare with real estate investment to assess whether fixed-asset investment is rotating from property into energy infrastructure as government stimulus shifts.

aCNCNDLKPM.description: Power infrastructure investment completion, Housing & Real Estate Prices, Monthly, NEA - National Energy Administration, China
aCNCNDLKPM.meaning: Power infrastructure investment completion — NEA monthly series tracking nominal completed investment in power infrastructure, complementing the current-price version with a broader definition.
aCNCNDLKPM.how_to_use: Cross-check with aCNCNHTCDM for consistency; sustained divergence between the two series may reflect price deflator issues or scope differences in project classification.

aCNCNBNYRM.description: Power infrastructure investment completion, thermal power generation equipment installed capacity
aCNCNBNYRM.meaning: Thermal power generation equipment installed capacity — NEA monthly series measuring cumulative installed megawatts of coal, gas, and oil-fired power generation, a key energy security indicator.
aCNCNBNYRM.how_to_use: Track growth pace against renewable capacity additions (solar, wind) to assess China's energy transition speed; slow thermal capacity growth alongside rising renewables signals structural energy-mix shift.

aCNHPIAR.description: House Prices, Newly built, Chg Y/Y, National Bureau of Statistics of China
aCNHPIAR.meaning: NBS nationwide newly-built residential property price index — year-on-year percentage change derived from the 70-city survey covering 35 first/second-tier and 35 third-tier cities, released monthly with a roughly 3-week lag.
aCNHPIAR.how_to_use: The primary official gauge of national house price momentum; a sustained negative reading (persistent since mid-2023) signals ongoing balance-sheet stress for households and developers alike — watch for policy response triggers.

aCNCNARBQM.description: Real estate enterprises purchase land area
aCNCNARBQM.meaning: Total land area purchased by real estate enterprises — NBS monthly cumulative series measuring gross land acquisition by developers, a leading indicator for future housing supply and local government land revenue.
aCNCNARBQM.how_to_use: Land purchases down 50%+ from peak signal the fiscal crisis for local governments who depend on land transfers; watch for stabilization as an early signal that developer confidence and credit are recovering.

aCNCNKPOMM.description: Real estate enterprises purchase land area, Hefei city (capital)
aCNCNKPOMM.meaning: Land area purchased by real estate enterprises in Hefei (Anhui capital) — a tier-2 city that has outperformed peers through strong semiconductor, EV, and advanced manufacturing investment attracting population and housing demand.
aCNCNKPOMM.how_to_use: Hefei is a rare positive outlier in the land market; compare against national aCNCNARBQM to quantify how industrial policy success translates into developer land appetite in new-economy cities.

aCNCNBFMZM.description: Real estate investment, land acquisition fee, Western Region,Cumulative
aCNCNBFMZM.meaning: Real estate investment land acquisition fee in Western China — NBS cumulative provincial breakdown capturing developer spending on land in the western region (Sichuan, Chongqing, Yunnan, etc.).
aCNCNBFMZM.how_to_use: Weak western land fees versus eastern peers highlight that fiscal stress from land market collapse is most acute in lower-tier provincial capitals; monitor for government-initiated land supply reduction as a relief measure.

aCNCNSCYNM.description: Real estate investment, land acquisition fee, Zhejiang Province
aCNCNSCYNM.meaning: Real estate investment land acquisition fee in Zhejiang Province — NBS provincial series for one of China's wealthiest provinces, where high land prices historically generated major fiscal revenue.
aCNCNSCYNM.how_to_use: Zhejiang's land fee collapse relative to its 2021 peak highlights fiscal pressure even in affluent coastal provinces; compare with aCNCNBFMZM to assess east-west land market divergence.

aCNCNVHPIM.description: Real estate, housing completion area, Nanjing city
aCNCNVHPIM.meaning: Housing completion area in Nanjing (Jiangsu capital) — NBS city-level monthly measure of floor space in residential buildings certified as complete, reflecting delivery of pre-sold units.
aCNCNVHPIM.how_to_use: Nanjing completions track the gap between developer obligations and delivery; rising completions despite falling new starts signals the deleveraging cycle — developers finishing old stock rather than starting new.

aCNCNWORBM.description: Real estate, housing completion area, Nanning city
aCNCNWORBM.meaning: Housing completion area in Nanning (Guangxi capital) — NBS city-level series for a tier-2 city bordering Vietnam, where completions reflect ASEAN-oriented industrial expansion and government infrastructure investment.
aCNCNWORBM.how_to_use: Compare against Nanjing (aCNCNVHPIM) to examine coastal versus inland completion dynamics; Nanning's completions are more tied to state-driven construction than private developer activity.

aCNCNRBQNM.description: Real estate, housing completion area, not for sale
aCNCNRBQNM.meaning: Housing completion area for non-sale purposes — NBS monthly series covering government-allocated housing, affordable units, and other non-commercial completions not subject to open market transactions.
aCNCNRBQNM.how_to_use: Rising non-sale completions relative to total completions signals a policy shift toward social/affordable housing delivery — a key component of the government's 'whitelist' and housing stabilization toolkit.

aCNCNEFOHM.description: Real estate, housing completion area, residential, Hohhot city
aCNCNEFOHM.meaning: Residential housing completion area in Hohhot (Inner Mongolia capital) — NBS city-level series for a third-tier northern city where completions are driven by government resettlement and resource-sector housing demand.
aCNCNEFOHM.how_to_use: Hohhot completions benchmark weak-end scenarios for resource-dependent provincial capitals; sustained low completions here confirm structural demand deficiency beyond cyclical policy tools.

aCNCNIVMKM.meaning: National housing completion value — NBS monthly measure of the monetary value of all completed residential construction, combining both commercial and affordable housing segments.
aCNCNIVMKM.how_to_use: Compare with aCNPUCPI (planned investment) to estimate the completion-to-pipeline ratio; a rising completion value while planned investment falls confirms the sector is drawing down inventory rather than creating new supply.

aCNCNZOZWM.description: Real estate, housing construction area, Xi'an city
aCNCNZOZWM.meaning: Total housing construction area (under construction) in Xi'an — NBS city-level series for the Northwest's largest city, reflecting both new-start and multi-year pipeline projects still in progress.
aCNCNZOZWM.how_to_use: Xi'an's large under-construction pipeline (legacy of the 2017–2020 boom) creates ongoing completion and delivery risk; monitor alongside new starts for signs of pipeline rationalization.

aCNCNTJMEM.description: Real estate, housing construction area, new start
aCNCNTJMEM.meaning: National residential housing new-start construction area — NBS monthly cumulative measure of floor space where construction began during the period, the most forward-looking supply indicator.
aCNCNTJMEM.how_to_use: New starts have collapsed 60%+ from 2021 peak — the most consequential leading indicator for future housing supply shortfalls; stabilization is required before completions can sustainably recover.

aCNCNOXKQM.description: Real estate, housing construction area, new start, Beihai city
aCNCNOXKQM.meaning: Housing new-start construction area in Beihai (Guangxi coastal city) — NBS city-level series for a third-tier coastal city whose residential market has attracted retiree and holiday-home demand.
aCNCNOXKQM.how_to_use: Beihai's new-start volatility reflects speculative holiday-home cycles; compare with aCNCNIONGM (residential under construction) to assess whether new supply additions are translating to completed stock.

aCNCNOOAM.description: Real estate, housing construction area, new start, Chg Y/Y, Cumulative
aCNCNOOAM.meaning: Housing new-start construction area YoY growth rate, cumulative — NBS official rate-of-change measure providing the percentage change versus the same period prior year on a year-to-date basis.
aCNCNOOAM.how_to_use: This is the most cited new-starts metric in NBS press releases; a less-negative print signals a slowdown in the deterioration even before a positive turn, which markets interpret as bottoming.

aCNCNGVSM1.description: Real estate, housing construction area, new start, East area
aCNCNGVSM1.meaning: Housing new-start construction area in East China — NBS regional breakdown covering Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Shandong, Fujian, Anhui, Jiangxi, and Shanghai, the most economically active zone.
aCNCNGVSM1.how_to_use: Eastern new starts carry the highest weight for national recovery given developer concentration and household income levels; compare with western/central breakdowns to detect geographic leadership in the recovery.

aCNCNKTPRM.description: Real estate, housing construction area, new start, Suzhou city
aCNCNKTPRM.meaning: Housing new-start construction area in Suzhou — a tier-2 Yangtze Delta manufacturing and technology hub adjacent to Shanghai with one of China's highest GDP-per-capita among non-tier-1 cities.
aCNCNKTPRM.how_to_use: Suzhou is a bellwether for Yangtze Delta housing demand beyond Shanghai; early new-start recovery here confirms that economic spillover from Shanghai is reaching adjacent manufacturing cities.

aCNCNRLOIM.description: Real estate, housing construction area, new start, Yinchuan city
aCNCNRLOIM.meaning: Housing new-start construction area in Yinchuan (Ningxia capital) — NBS city-level series for a small, remote northwestern provincial capital where new starts reflect government-driven construction more than private demand.
aCNCNRLOIM.how_to_use: Yinchuan is a benchmark for state-directed construction in peripheral markets; compare against aCNCNKTPRM (Suzhou) to illustrate the market-driven vs. policy-driven new-start divergence.

aCNCNLOLKM.description: Real estate, housing construction area, new start, commercial business room
aCNCNLOLKM.meaning: Housing new-start area for commercial business premises (retail, office) — NBS segment breakdown separating non-residential commercial from the headline residential new-start figure.
aCNCNLOLKM.how_to_use: Commercial new starts typically lag residential recovery; a widening gap between residential and commercial new starts signals developers are prioritizing housing over office/retail, reflecting demand composition shifts.

aCNCNMTAM.description: Real estate, housing construction area, new start, residential, Guiyang city
aCNCNMTAM.meaning: Residential housing new-start area in Guiyang (Guizhou capital) — NBS city-level series for a Southwest China provincial capital that experienced a debt-driven construction boom followed by sharp fiscal retrenchment.
aCNCNMTAM.how_to_use: Guiyang is a high-profile case of local government fiscal overextension; collapsing new starts here track the restructuring of LGFV (local government financing vehicle) debt constraining developer activity.

aCNCNRBRM.description: Real estate, housing construction area, new start, residential, Shenzhen city
aCNCNRBRM.meaning: Residential housing new-start area in Shenzhen — NBS city-level series for the most land-constrained tier-1 city, where new starts reflect highly regulated land release by the municipal government.
aCNCNRBRM.how_to_use: Shenzhen's new starts are supply-constrained by design (limited land); compare with aCNCNKTPRM (Suzhou) to distinguish between land-constrained tier-1 and land-abundant tier-2 supply dynamics.

aCNCNQQONM.description: Real estate, housing construction area, new start, residential, Wenzhou city
aCNCNQQONM.meaning: Residential housing new-start area in Wenzhou — NBS city-level series for a Zhejiang city historically known for its private entrepreneurship and speculative real estate investment culture.
aCNCNQQONM.how_to_use: Wenzhou's residential new starts are a proxy for private-sector housing investment appetite in coastal Zhejiang; compare with aCNCNKTPRM (Suzhou) to track whether Zhejiang new-start recovery is broad-based.

aCNCNTSGPM.description: Real estate, housing construction area, new start, residential, Xi'an city
aCNCNTSGPM.meaning: Residential housing new-start area in Xi'an — NBS city-level series for the Northwest's largest city, tracking supply initiation in a market that boomed during 2017–2020 on tech and manufacturing investment.
aCNCNTSGPM.how_to_use: Xi'an new starts are well below peak and must be watched for recovery signals; combine with aCNCNZOZWM (under construction) and aCNHRPXA (prices) to build a full Xi'an housing cycle picture.

aCNCNPXILM.description: Real estate, housing construction area, new start, Ürümqi
aCNCNPXILM.meaning: Housing new-start construction area in Urumqi (Xinjiang capital) — NBS city-level series for China's westernmost major city, where construction activity reflects state infrastructure investment and resource sector activity.
aCNCNPXILM.how_to_use: Urumqi new starts are largely policy-driven; compare with aCNCNRLOIM (Yinchuan) to benchmark western periphery city construction intensity and assess state-directed housing supply strategy in frontier regions.

aCNCNIONGM.description: Real estate, housing construction area, residential, Beihai city
aCNCNIONGM.meaning: Residential housing under-construction area in Beihai — NBS city-level total floor space being actively constructed in this Guangxi coastal city, encompassing all stages from foundation to topping-off.
aCNCNIONGM.how_to_use: Compare with new starts (aCNCNOXKQM) to derive the average construction duration and pipeline drawdown; a shrinking under-construction total confirms the cycle is burning off legacy inventory.

aCNCNEYCM1.description: Real estate, housing construction area, residential, Hefei city (capital)
aCNCNEYCM1.meaning: Residential housing under-construction area in Hefei — NBS city-level total reflecting the active construction pipeline in one of China's fastest-growing tier-2 cities, driven by new-economy industrial investment.
aCNCNEYCM1.how_to_use: Hefei's resilient construction pipeline distinguishes it from most tier-2 cities; use alongside aCNCNKPOMM (land purchases) to confirm Hefei as a sustained positive outlier in the housing downcycle.

aCNCNTZUBM.description: Real estate, housing construction area, residential, Nanchang city
aCNCNTZUBM.meaning: Residential housing under-construction area in Nanchang (Jiangxi capital) — NBS city-level series for a central China provincial capital with significant affordable housing and government-sponsored urban renewal activity.
aCNCNTZUBM.how_to_use: Nanchang's construction area tracks central China's state-led housing activity; compare with Nanjing (aCNCNVHPIM) to gauge central-versus-coastal completion rate divergence under the housing support program.

aCNCNUMBXM.description: Real estate, housing construction area, residential, Xi'an city
aCNCNUMBXM.meaning: Residential housing under-construction area in Xi'an — NBS city-level total for the Northwest's largest city, capturing the accumulated pipeline from the 2017–2020 boom still working through to completion.
aCNCNUMBXM.how_to_use: The large Xi'an under-construction stock represents a significant completion and debt-repayment overhang; compare with new starts (aCNCNTSGPM) and prices (aCNHRPXA) to track the cycle drawdown timeline.

aCNCNXCBKM.description: 房地产开发企业房屋施工面积_本年新开工_住宅_累计_无锡市
aCNCNXCBKM.meaning: China regional / sectoral statistic: 房地产开发企业房屋施工面积_本年新开工_住宅_累计_无锡市. Detailed regional or sectoral data series — original Chinese description preserved.
aCNCNXCBKM.how_to_use: Refer to source description for specific content. Regional and city-level data in the China dataset captures provincial and urban-level economic activity, often used by analysts tracking specific localities.

aCNCNMJYQM.description: 房地产开发企业房屋施工面积_累计同比增速_郑州市
aCNCNMJYQM.meaning: China regional / sectoral statistic: 房地产开发企业房屋施工面积_累计同比增速_郑州市. Detailed regional or sectoral data series — original Chinese description preserved.
aCNCNMJYQM.how_to_use: Refer to source description for specific content. Regional and city-level data in the China dataset captures provincial and urban-level economic activity, often used by analysts tracking specific localities.

aCNHPRICET.description: House Prices, Newly built, Chg Y/Y, National Bureau of Statistics of China/LSEG
aCNHPRICET.meaning: NBS/LSEG composite newly-built house price YoY change index — blends the NBS 70-city survey methodology with LSEG's data processing to produce a consistent, comparable national price change series.
aCNHPRICET.how_to_use: Use as the standard reference for cross-country housing price comparisons in LSEG terminals; a less-negative reading signals that the 2021–2024 correction phase may be approaching a floor, though a positive turn requires both demand recovery and developer solvency.

aCNEXPT.meaning: China macro reference series: Export Prices. Refer to the description and source for analytical context.
aCNEXPT.how_to_use: Cross-check against related series in the same category for context. China macro data is published by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS, real-economy + prices), People's Bank of China (PBoC, monetary), State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE, BoP/FX), and Ministry of Finance (fiscal).

aCNIMPV.meaning: China macro reference series: Import Prices. Refer to the description and source for analytical context.
aCNIMPV.how_to_use: Cross-check against related series in the same category for context. China macro data is published by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS, real-economy + prices), People's Bank of China (PBoC, monetary), State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE, BoP/FX), and Ministry of Finance (fiscal).

aCNTOT/C.meaning: China macro reference series: Terms of Trade. Refer to the description and source for analytical context.
aCNTOT/C.how_to_use: Cross-check against related series in the same category for context. China macro data is published by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS, real-economy + prices), People's Bank of China (PBoC, monetary), State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE, BoP/FX), and Ministry of Finance (fiscal).

aCNSTBEIR.meaning: NBS Business Climate Index (企业景气指数) — a composite of entrepreneur sentiment across all industrial sectors surveyed quarterly by China's National Bureau of Statistics. The index aggregates responses from tens of thousands of enterprises on production, orders, profits, and hiring, expressed as a diffusion index where readings above 100 indicate net optimism (the index is scaled 0-200 with 100 as neutral in some vintages, or 0-100 diffusion in others depending on release format). Published quarterly by NBS typically within 20 days of quarter-end.
aCNSTBEIR.how_to_use: Use as a broad cross-sectoral barometer of corporate confidence in China. A sustained drop below the neutral threshold across two or more consecutive quarters has historically preceded GDP growth deceleration by 1-2 quarters. Compare against the quarterly NBS Entrepreneur Confidence Index (aCNBSETPEX) — when the climate index falls while the expectation index holds, it signals current-period weakness with near-term recovery hopes. Markets use this alongside Caixin PMI for a state-vs-private sector confidence cross-check.

aCNGSBBCIR.meaning: The Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business (CKGSB) Business Conditions Index (BCI) — a monthly survey of CKGSB alumni and senior executives at Chinese and multinational firms operating in China. The index covers current business conditions, sales, profits, hiring, and investment intentions. Published monthly by CKGSB, typically mid-month for the prior month. Sample skews toward mid-to-large private firms and MNCs, offering a C-suite perspective rarely captured in government surveys.
aCNGSBBCIR.how_to_use: The CKGSB BCI is particularly valuable for gauging private-sector and MNC confidence independently of NBS official surveys. When BCI diverges sharply downward from official NBS business climate data, it often signals policy uncertainty or regulatory headwinds felt acutely by private firms. The BCI's investment intentions sub-component is a useful 3-6 month leading indicator for fixed asset investment in the private sector. Cross-check against Caixin PMI (aCNPMIBAQ) for consistency — sustained BCI below 50 while NBS PMI holds above 50 reveals the state-private divergence.

aCNMPMNMPR.description: PMI, Manufacturing Sector, From MinXin of China, Overall operating performance
aCNMPMNMPR.subcategory: MinXin PMI Manufacturing — Overall Operating Performance
aCNMPMNMPR.meaning: MinXin PMI Manufacturing Overall Operating Performance sub-index — published by China Minsheng Bank (民生银行) in partnership with the research firm behind the MinXin PMI series. MinXin focuses specifically on smaller private enterprises that are underrepresented in both the NBS (large SOE-skewed) and Caixin (~430 firms) surveys. The overall operating performance reading is the composite headline for the MinXin manufacturing survey, covering output, orders, employment, costs, and deliveries.
aCNMPMNMPR.how_to_use: The MinXin PMI serves as a third data point in the China manufacturing PMI triumvirate alongside NBS and Caixin. When MinXin diverges significantly below both NBS and Caixin, it flags acute stress in the small private manufacturing base — often a leading signal for credit stress and SME loan default cycles. A divergence of 3+ points below Caixin for 2+ months has historically coincided with targeted PBOC easing for SMEs. Compare the overall operating performance against the new orders sub-index (aCNMPMMNOR) to distinguish demand-led from cost-led weakness.

aCNMPMMEMR.description: PMI, Manufacturing Sector, From MinXin of China, employment
aCNMPMMEMR.meaning: MinXin PMI Manufacturing Employment sub-index — measures month-on-month change in headcount at small private manufacturing firms surveyed by the MinXin PMI series (China Minsheng Bank). A reading above 50 indicates net hiring; below 50 indicates net layoffs. Released monthly alongside the MinXin PMI composite.
aCNMPMMEMR.how_to_use: Employment in small private manufacturing is structurally more volatile than in large SOEs — MinXin employment sub-index tends to lead the NBS manufacturing employment sub-index (aCNPMINBSEM/A) by 1-2 months because small firms adjust headcount faster. A sustained drop below 48 signals accelerating labor market stress in the private SME sector, which historically precedes policy responses (unemployment insurance easing, social security fee reductions). Cross-reference with Caixin employment PMI for triangulation.

aCNMPMMSIR.description: PMI, Manufacturing Sector, From MinXin of China, inventory
aCNMPMMSIR.meaning: MinXin PMI Manufacturing Inventory sub-index — tracks month-on-month change in finished-goods or raw material inventories held by small private manufacturing enterprises in the MinXin survey panel. A reading above 50 indicates inventory accumulation; below 50 indicates destocking.
aCNMPMMSIR.how_to_use: Inventory dynamics at small private manufacturers are a leading indicator of the broader inventory cycle because SMEs are the first to over-order in upturns and the first to destock in downturns. When this sub-index rises sharply while new orders (aCNMPMMNOR) remain below 50, it signals unintended inventory build — a negative leading indicator for production. Compare with NBS stocks of major inputs (aCNPMISTMJI/A) to assess whether the inventory cycle is driven by input hoarding or output overhang.

aCNMPMMNOR.description: PMI, Manufacturing Sector, From MinXin of China, new orders
aCNMPMMNOR.meaning: MinXin PMI Manufacturing New Orders sub-index — measures month-on-month change in new customer orders received by small private manufacturing firms in the MinXin survey. A reading above 50 indicates order growth; below 50 indicates contraction. Released monthly by China Minsheng Bank.
aCNMPMMNOR.how_to_use: New orders is the most forward-looking sub-component of any PMI survey — it leads output by approximately 1-2 months. The MinXin new orders reading is particularly sensitive to domestic demand shifts in the SME segment, since small manufacturers sell predominantly in domestic consumer and B2B channels rather than export. When MinXin new orders diverges below NBS new orders (aCNPMINEWOD/A), it signals that large SOEs are capturing order flow while SMEs lose share — a dynamic common during demand slowdowns and credit squeezes.

aCNMPMMOTR.description: PMI, Manufacturing Sector, From MinXin of China, output
aCNMPMMOTR.meaning: MinXin PMI Manufacturing Output sub-index — measures month-on-month change in production volumes at small private manufacturing firms in the MinXin survey. A reading above 50 indicates production expansion; below 50 indicates contraction. Published monthly by China Minsheng Bank.
aCNMPMMOTR.how_to_use: Output is a coincident indicator of manufacturing activity. For small private firms it typically lags the new orders sub-index (aCNMPMMNOR) by 1-2 months. When output remains below 50 despite new orders recovering above 50, it often reflects capacity utilization constraints or working capital shortfalls at SMEs. Compare with NBS manufacturing output sub-index (aCNPMIOTPT/A) — persistent MinXin output weakness vs. NBS output strength illustrates the SOE-vs-private capacity utilization gap.

aCNMPMMDVR.description: PMI, Manufacturing Sector, From MinXin of China, suppliers' delivery time
aCNMPMMDVR.subcategory: MinXin PMI Manufacturing — Suppliers' Delivery Time
aCNMPMMDVR.units: Index (diffusion, inverted: >50 = faster delivery = easing supply)
aCNMPMMDVR.meaning: MinXin PMI Manufacturing Suppliers' Delivery Time sub-index — measures month-on-month change in the speed of supplier deliveries to small private manufacturing firms. This component is inverted in its PMI contribution: slower deliveries (supply chain stress) push the reading below 50, while faster deliveries push it above 50. Published monthly by China Minsheng Bank.
aCNMPMMDVR.how_to_use: Supplier delivery times are a supply-chain stress gauge. When deliveries slow sharply (reading falls below 48), it signals upstream bottlenecks — either raw material shortages, logistics disruptions, or supplier financial distress. During the COVID lockdown periods (2020, 2022), this sub-index fell to historic lows across all PMI surveys. A recovery back toward 50 from below confirms supply normalization. Compare with NBS supplier delivery time (aCNPMISPDLT/A) — SME suppliers typically feel logistics stress earlier than large-firm supply chains.

aCNMPMMR.description: PMI, Manufacturing Sector, From MinXin of China, total
aCNMPMMR.meaning: MinXin PMI Manufacturing headline composite index — the overall weighted diffusion index for the MinXin manufacturing survey, combining new orders, output, employment, suppliers' delivery time, and inventory sub-components. Published monthly by China Minsheng Bank. The MinXin survey focuses on small and micro private manufacturers, filling a coverage gap between the NBS large-firm official PMI and the Caixin mid-sized private firm PMI.
aCNMPMMR.how_to_use: Use as the third leg of the China manufacturing PMI triangle: NBS (large SOEs, ~3,000 firms), Caixin (private SMEs, ~430 firms), and MinXin (small/micro private, broader sample). When all three converge below 50, the contraction signal is unambiguous. When NBS holds above 50 while Caixin and MinXin are below 50, it reflects SOE resilience masking private-sector stress — a common pattern during targeted stimulus cycles. The MinXin PMI is the least followed internationally, making divergences from NBS especially informative for alpha generation.

aCNMPMNMBR.description: PMI, Non-manufacturing Sector, From MinXin of China, business activities
aCNMPMNMBR.meaning: MinXin PMI Non-manufacturing Business Activities sub-index — measures month-on-month change in business activity levels at small private services and non-manufacturing firms in the MinXin survey. Covers sectors including retail, catering, logistics, real estate services, and personal services. Published monthly by China Minsheng Bank.
aCNMPMNMBR.how_to_use: The non-manufacturing business activities reading from MinXin provides the small-private-firm perspective on China's services sector — complementing the NBS non-manufacturing PMI (aCNPMINAQ) which is dominated by large SOE services firms. When MinXin non-manufacturing business activities diverges below NBS, it reflects that small service providers (restaurants, small retailers, personal services) are under more stress than state-owned services companies. This distinction became prominent post-2020 as COVID restrictions hit small hospitality and retail much harder than state enterprises.

aCNMPMNMMR.description: PMI, Non-manufacturing Sector, From MinXin of China, employment
aCNMPMNMMR.meaning: MinXin PMI Non-manufacturing Employment sub-index — measures month-on-month change in headcount at small private services and non-manufacturing firms surveyed by MinXin. A reading above 50 indicates net services sector hiring; below 50 indicates net headcount reduction. Published monthly by China Minsheng Bank.
aCNMPMNMMR.how_to_use: Services employment at small private firms is one of the most cyclically sensitive labor market indicators in China — these firms hire and fire faster than SOEs and large corporates. A reading below 48 sustained for 2+ months typically precedes a rise in the urban survey unemployment rate for the 16-24 age cohort, which concentrates disproportionately in SME services roles. Use alongside MinXin manufacturing employment (aCNMPMMEMR) to assess broad labor market momentum in the private economy.

aCNMPMNMNR.description: PMI, Non-manufacturing Sector, From MinXin of China, new orders
aCNMPMNMNR.meaning: MinXin PMI Non-manufacturing New Orders sub-index — measures month-on-month change in new customer orders or service requests received by small private non-manufacturing firms in the MinXin survey. A reading above 50 indicates order growth; below 50 indicates contraction. Published monthly by China Minsheng Bank.
aCNMPMNMNR.how_to_use: Non-manufacturing new orders at small private firms lead business activity by approximately 1-2 months. A sharp divergence between MinXin non-manufacturing new orders and NBS non-manufacturing new orders (aCNPMINMSNO/A) indicates that order flow is concentrating among large state-owned services firms. This sub-index is particularly sensitive to consumer discretionary demand — sharp drops in hospitality, catering, and retail orders show up here before NBS data. Use with MinXin business activities (aCNMPMNMBR) to confirm demand-led vs. capacity-led services dynamics.

aCNMPMNMTR.description: PMI, Non-manufacturing Sector, From MinXin of China, stock
aCNMPMNMTR.meaning: MinXin PMI Non-manufacturing Stock sub-index — measures month-on-month change in inventory or stock levels held by small private non-manufacturing firms in the MinXin survey. For services firms, this predominantly reflects inventory of tradeable goods (retail, wholesale, catering supplies) rather than work-in-progress. Published monthly by China Minsheng Bank.
aCNMPMNMTR.how_to_use: Non-manufacturing inventory dynamics at small firms are a leading indicator of wholesale and retail cycle turns. Rising stock (>50) alongside falling new orders signals unintended inventory accumulation in small retail and wholesale businesses — a precursor to destocking and price discounting. Falling stock (<50) during a new orders recovery signals under-stocking and potential restocking demand. Compare with NBS retail sales data to validate whether stock changes reflect demand acceleration or slowing.

aCNMPMNMDR.description: PMI, Non-manufacturing Sector, From MinXin of China, supplier delivery time
aCNMPMNMDR.subcategory: MinXin PMI Non-manufacturing — Supplier Delivery Time
aCNMPMNMDR.units: Index (diffusion, inverted: >50 = faster delivery = easing supply)
aCNMPMNMDR.meaning: MinXin PMI Non-manufacturing Supplier Delivery Time sub-index — measures month-on-month change in the speed of supplier deliveries to small private non-manufacturing firms. Inverted convention: below 50 means slower deliveries (supply chain stress); above 50 means faster deliveries (supply normalization). Published monthly by China Minsheng Bank.
aCNMPMNMDR.how_to_use: For non-manufacturing SMEs, supplier delivery times reflect both physical logistics conditions and the financial health of their upstream suppliers. During credit crunches, small suppliers extend payment terms and delay deliveries to conserve cash, causing this index to drop. A sustained reading below 48 in non-manufacturing often coincides with broader B2B payment chain stress. Useful for triangulating with NBS non-manufacturing input prices (aCNPMINMIIP/A) — if deliveries slow while input prices rise, small services firms face a cost-and-supply squeeze.

aCNACREQBR.meaning: LSEG Anti-Corruption Risk database: Regulatory quality (Band) for China. Reference data used in compliance, due-diligence, and country-risk-screening workflows.
aCNACREQBR.how_to_use: Reference series for ESG, compliance, and KYC processes. Not a macroeconomic indicator. China's Anti-Corruption Risk profile reflects the post-2012 anti-graft campaign; sources include World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators, Transparency International CPI, and others.

aCNAMTOTNR.meaning: LSEG Anti-Money Laundering Risk database: Overall for China. AML/KYC compliance reference.
aCNAMTOTNR.how_to_use: Reference series for AML compliance workflows. Not a macroeconomic indicator. China is FATF-monitored; recent FATF assessments highlighted partial compliance.

aCNAMTOTSR.meaning: LSEG Anti-Money Laundering Risk database: Overall for China. AML/KYC compliance reference.
aCNAMTOTSR.how_to_use: Reference series for AML compliance workflows. Not a macroeconomic indicator. China is FATF-monitored; recent FATF assessments highlighted partial compliance.

aCNCRBSNSR.description: Comprehensive Risk, Business operational risk, Score
aCNCRBSNSR.meaning: LSEG Comprehensive Risk database: Business operational risk for China. Aggregated country-risk reference combining political, economic, governance, and operational dimensions.
aCNCRBSNSR.how_to_use: Reference series for enterprise risk management. Not a macroeconomic indicator. China's overall risk profile reflects geopolitical tensions, regulatory unpredictability, and capital-control regime.

aCNCRTOTNR.meaning: LSEG Comprehensive Risk database: Overall for China. Aggregated country-risk reference combining political, economic, governance, and operational dimensions.
aCNCRTOTNR.how_to_use: Reference series for enterprise risk management. Not a macroeconomic indicator. China's overall risk profile reflects geopolitical tensions, regulatory unpredictability, and capital-control regime.

aCNCRRTAR.meaning: LSEG Comprehensive Risk database: Overall for China. Aggregated country-risk reference combining political, economic, governance, and operational dimensions.
aCNCRRTAR.how_to_use: Reference series for enterprise risk management. Not a macroeconomic indicator. China's overall risk profile reflects geopolitical tensions, regulatory unpredictability, and capital-control regime.

aCNZAWCFR.description: Discontinued, IFDI, Awareness Indicator, Conferences, Score
aCNZAWCFR.meaning: China PMI sub-component: Discontinued, IFDI, Awareness Indicator, Conferences, Score. NBS or alternative-source manufacturing or non-manufacturing PMI sub-index.
aCNZAWCFR.how_to_use: Above 50 = expansion; below 50 = contraction. Sub-components (new orders, output, employment, supplier delivery times, inventories, prices) decompose the headline PMI movement.

aCNZYSDCR.description: Discontinued, IFDI, Sustainability Indicator, CSR Disclosure, Average CSR Disclosure Index Score
aCNZYSDCR.meaning: China PMI sub-component: Discontinued, IFDI, Sustainability Indicator, CSR Disclosure, Average CSR Disclosure Index Score. NBS or alternative-source manufacturing or non-manufacturing PMI sub-index.
aCNZYSDCR.how_to_use: Above 50 = expansion; below 50 = contraction. Sub-components (new orders, output, employment, supplier delivery times, inventories, prices) decompose the headline PMI movement.

aCNZAWCFP.description: IFDI, Awareness, Events, Conferences, more than 100 participants
aCNZAWCFP.meaning: Islamic Finance Development Indicator: IFDI, Awareness, Events, Conferences, more than 100 participants. Reference data on China's Islamic finance footprint (small relative to total finance — concentrated in Ningxia and Xinjiang regions).
aCNZAWCFP.how_to_use: Niche reference. China's Islamic-finance market is small but growing. Not a mainstream macroeconomic indicator.

aCNMNIBCCR.how_to_use: Cross-check against the SA version (aCNMNIBCCQ). The seasonally-adjusted version is the more market-relevant gauge.

aCNMNIBCCQ.meaning: MNI Business Sentiment, seasonally adjusted — alternative private-sector business-confidence gauge. Smaller sample than NBS or Caixin.
aCNMNIBCCQ.how_to_use: Tertiary cross-check. Useful for triangulated business-cycle reads when NBS and Caixin diverge.

aCNOBS085Q/A.meaning: NBS Manufacturing Industrial Confidence Indicator — an NBS quarterly survey-based measure of confidence among industrial enterprises in China's manufacturing sector. Unlike the monthly PMI which is a diffusion index of current conditions, this indicator captures forward-looking entrepreneurial confidence in industrial activity. Published quarterly by NBS, typically released within 20 days of quarter-end alongside the quarterly Business Climate Index.
aCNOBS085Q/A.how_to_use: Use as a quarterly confirmation of the monthly PMI trend — when the industrial confidence indicator and the NBS manufacturing PMI align in direction, the signal has higher conviction. A divergence (PMI above 50 but confidence declining) often precedes a PMI softening in the subsequent quarter. This indicator is especially useful for filtering PMI noise in months with significant seasonal distortions (Chinese New Year, Golden Week). Also compare with the Entrepreneur Expectation Index (aCNBSETPEX) to distinguish current confidence from forward expectations.

aCNBUSCLIMI.meaning: NBS Industrial Business Climate Index (工业企业景气指数) — a quarterly composite index measuring current business conditions across China's industrial sector. Compiled from NBS surveys of industrial enterprises above designated size (annual revenue ≥ CNY 20M), covering production, orders, inventories, profitability, and financing conditions. Published quarterly by NBS, typically within 20 days of quarter-end. The index uses a 100-point neutral convention; readings above 100 indicate expanding conditions.
aCNBUSCLIMI.how_to_use: The quarterly NBS Business Climate Index provides a longer-horizon, lower-noise view of industrial health compared to monthly PMI. Use it to confirm whether monthly PMI moves represent genuine trend changes or temporary fluctuations. When the Business Climate Index drops more than 5 points below 100 over two consecutive quarters, it has consistently preceded significant industrial investment slowdowns. Cross-reference with the Entrepreneur Expectation Index (aCNBSETPEX) — when climate index falls while expectations hold, recovery is anticipated; when both decline together, the downturn is more entrenched.

aCNCPMIAQ.description: Composite, From NBS of China, General PMI
aCNCPMIAQ.meaning: Composite PMI from NBS — same conceptual measure as aCNNPMIGRQ/A. Combines manufacturing + non-manufacturing.
aCNCPMIAQ.how_to_use: Cross-check against the primary release. Use whichever has fresher data; methodology and timing differences across releases are typically minor and resolved on revision.

aCNBSETPEX.meaning: NBS Industrial Entrepreneur Expectation Index (企业家信心指数) — a quarterly forward-looking survey measuring industrial entrepreneurs' expectations for business conditions in the coming quarter. Published by NBS quarterly, typically alongside the Business Climate Index within 20 days of quarter-end. The index surveys senior management at industrial enterprises above designated size on expected production, orders, profits, hiring, and capital expenditure.
aCNBSETPEX.how_to_use: This is a pure forward-looking indicator — it captures what industrial decision-makers plan to do next quarter, not what is happening now. A reading above 100 indicates net optimism about the next quarter; below 100 indicates net pessimism. The Entrepreneur Expectation Index typically leads the Business Climate Index by one quarter, making it useful for confirming or questioning PMI-based recovery calls. When expectations recover sharply from a trough while current conditions remain weak, it is a high-conviction leading indicator of industrial recovery — historically confirmed by subsequent fixed asset investment acceleration.

aCNPMIBAQ.meaning: NBS Manufacturing Sector PMI — official Chinese government PMI from National Bureau of Statistics. Released last business day of each month at 09:00 CST. Survey of ~3,000 manufacturing companies, larger sample than Caixin/Ratingdog.
aCNPMIBAQ.how_to_use: THE official China PMI. Sample skews toward large state-owned enterprises (SOEs). Above 50 = expansion. Currently hovering around 49-51 (no clear expansion). Sub-50 sustained signals manufacturing recession — uncommon but observed 2022-2024 in months. Markets watch the 50 line obsessively.

aCNPMINAQ.description: Non-manufacturing Sector, From NBS of China, business activities
aCNPMINAQ.meaning: NBS Non-manufacturing PMI Business Activities Index — the headline activity measure for China's non-manufacturing sector from the National Bureau of Statistics official PMI survey. Covers approximately 1,200 enterprises across services and construction. Released on the last business day of the reference month at 09:00 CST simultaneously with the manufacturing PMI. The non-manufacturing survey covers two broad segments: services (financial services, retail, transport, IT, real estate services, etc.) and construction.
aCNPMINAQ.how_to_use: The NBS non-manufacturing PMI is the primary high-frequency gauge of China's services and construction sector health. Above 50 indicates expansion; below 50 indicates contraction. Because China's economy is increasingly services-driven (services now ~55% of GDP), this indicator carries growing macro significance. The construction sub-component is particularly sensitive to property sector policy and infrastructure spending cycles. Compare the NBS non-manufacturing PMI with the Caixin services PMI — when Caixin services diverges below NBS, it signals private-sector services stress not captured in the state-dominated NBS sample.

aCNNPMMLN/A.description: PMI, Manufacturing Sector, From NBS of China, Large Enterprises
aCNNPMMLN/A.meaning: NBS Manufacturing PMI — Large Enterprises sub-index. Captures production at large (mostly SOE) manufacturers.
aCNNPMMLN/A.how_to_use: State-sector cycle gauge. Large enterprises typically run higher than small/medium (better access to credit, government contracts). Spread between large and small (aCNNPMMSE/A) signals the SOE-vs-private divergence.

aCNPMIIMPPM/A.description: PMI, Manufacturing Sector, From NBS of China, Main Raw Material Purchase Price
aCNPMIIMPPM/A.subcategory: NBS Manufacturing PMI — Main Raw Material Purchase Price
aCNPMIIMPPM/A.meaning: NBS Manufacturing PMI Main Raw Material Purchase Price sub-index — measures month-on-month change in the purchase prices of main raw materials paid by manufacturing firms in the NBS PMI survey (~3,000 firms, skewed to large SOEs). A reading above 50 indicates net price increases; below 50 indicates net price decreases. Released on the last business day of the reference month at 09:00 CST.
aCNPMIIMPPM/A.how_to_use: This is the earliest monthly indicator of PPI (Producer Price Index) direction — it typically leads the official NBS PPI release by approximately 2 weeks. A reading above 55 for 2+ months reliably signals PPI acceleration and margin compression for downstream manufacturers. Conversely, sustained readings below 45 signal deflationary input price pressure. Practitioners use this as a real-time PPI nowcast. Compare with the output price sub-component to assess pass-through: when input prices rise faster than output prices, industrial profit margins compress — a leading signal for profit growth deceleration.

aCNNPMMME/A.description: PMI, Manufacturing Sector, From NBS of China, Medium Enterprises
aCNNPMMME/A.meaning: NBS Manufacturing PMI — Medium Enterprises sub-index. Bridges large and small enterprise dynamics.
aCNNPMMME/A.how_to_use: Track the SME pulse without smallest-firm volatility. Medium enterprises typically track headline closely but with somewhat better credit access than smallest tier.

aCNNPMMSE/A.description: PMI, Manufacturing Sector, From NBS of China, Small Enterprises
aCNNPMMSE/A.meaning: NBS Manufacturing PMI — Small Enterprises sub-index. Captures the most credit-constrained part of Chinese manufacturing.
aCNNPMMSE/A.how_to_use: Most cyclical PMI tier — smaller firms are most sensitive to credit conditions and demand swings. Sustained sub-50 is the rule for small enterprises (chronic SME-stress narrative). Spread vs Large enterprises = SOE-vs-private divergence indicator.

aCNPMINBSEM/A.description: PMI, Manufacturing Sector, From NBS of China, employment
aCNPMINBSEM/A.meaning: NBS Manufacturing PMI Employment sub-index — measures month-on-month change in manufacturing workforce headcount across the ~3,000 firms (predominantly large SOEs and state-linked enterprises) in the NBS PMI survey. A reading above 50 indicates net hiring; below 50 indicates net job losses. Released on the last business day of the reference month at 09:00 CST.
aCNPMINBSEM/A.how_to_use: The NBS manufacturing employment PMI has remained persistently below 50 for most of the post-2015 period, reflecting structural shedding of excess labor from heavy industry. A reading below 48 for 3+ consecutive months typically coincides with rising urban unemployment and precedes PBOC easing steps targeting employment stabilization. Because the NBS sample skews to large SOEs — which are slower to fire than private firms — this sub-index tends to lag MinXin employment (aCNMPMMEMR) by 1-2 months. Compare with the NBS employment survey unemployment rate for confirmation.

aCNPMIEMP3M/A.description: PMI, Manufacturing Sector, From NBS of China, new export orders
aCNPMIEMP3M/A.subcategory: NBS Manufacturing PMI — New Export Orders
aCNPMIEMP3M/A.meaning: NBS Manufacturing PMI New Export Orders sub-index — measures month-on-month change in new orders specifically from overseas customers at manufacturing firms in the NBS PMI survey. A reading above 50 indicates growth in export orders; below 50 indicates contraction. Released on the last business day of the reference month at 09:00 CST. This sub-index is one of the most internationally traded China macro indicators.
aCNPMIEMP3M/A.how_to_use: New export orders is a leading indicator for China's goods export growth — it typically leads the official customs export data by 1-2 months. A sustained drop below 48 signals export headwinds that will show up in the trade balance within two months. Cross-reference with global demand indicators: US ISM New Orders, Eurozone PMI new export orders, and South Korea export data (released first in each month) provide context for whether China export order weakness is demand-driven or market-share-driven. During trade war episodes, this sub-index diverged sharply below domestic new orders (aCNPMINEWOD/A).

aCNPMINEWOD/A.description: PMI, Manufacturing Sector, From NBS of China, new orders
aCNPMINEWOD/A.meaning: NBS Manufacturing PMI New Orders sub-index — measures month-on-month change in total new customer orders (domestic + export) at manufacturing firms in the NBS PMI survey (~3,000 firms). A reading above 50 indicates order growth; below 50 indicates order contraction. Released on the last business day of the reference month at 09:00 CST. This is the most closely watched sub-component of the NBS manufacturing PMI.
aCNPMINEWOD/A.how_to_use: New orders is the single most forward-looking component of the NBS PMI — it leads output by 1-2 months and leads the industrial production index (IP) by approximately 6-8 weeks. A recovery in new orders above 50 while output remains below 50 is a classic leading signal for manufacturing recovery. The spread between new orders and the inventory sub-index (orders minus inventories) is a particularly powerful predictor: a widening positive spread (orders recovering, inventories falling) signals an imminent production upturn. Markets treat the new orders print as the most market-sensitive line item in the PMI release.

aCNPMIOTPT/A.description: PMI, Manufacturing Sector, From NBS of China, output
aCNPMIOTPT/A.meaning: NBS Manufacturing PMI Output sub-index — measures month-on-month change in production volumes at manufacturing firms in the NBS PMI survey (~3,000 firms, large SOE-weighted). A reading above 50 indicates production expansion; below 50 indicates production contraction. Released on the last business day of the reference month at 09:00 CST.
aCNPMIOTPT/A.how_to_use: Output is a coincident indicator of manufacturing activity, typically lagging new orders (aCNPMINEWOD/A) by 1-2 months. The output-to-new-orders spread is a key inventory-cycle signal: when output exceeds new orders for multiple months, inventory builds; when new orders exceed output, inventories draw down. The output sub-index is also the most direct bridge between the PMI survey and the NBS Industrial Production (IP) release — a sustained output PMI above 52 typically corresponds to IP growth above 6% YoY. Seasonal distortions are largest in February (Chinese New Year) when output collapses regardless of cycle.

aCNPMISTMJI/A.description: PMI, Manufacturing Sector, From NBS of China, stocks of major inputs
aCNPMISTMJI/A.subcategory: NBS Manufacturing PMI — Stocks of Major Inputs
aCNPMISTMJI/A.meaning: NBS Manufacturing PMI Stocks of Major Inputs sub-index — measures month-on-month change in raw material and major input inventories held by manufacturing firms in the NBS PMI survey. A reading above 50 indicates input inventory accumulation; below 50 indicates input destocking. Released on the last business day of the reference month at 09:00 CST.
aCNPMISTMJI/A.how_to_use: Input inventory levels reflect manufacturing firms' confidence in future production needs. Rising input stocks (>50) alongside rising new orders confirms a genuine demand-driven inventory build — bullish for commodity demand. Rising input stocks alongside falling new orders signals precautionary hoarding or speculative stockpiling — a risk that input prices are about to fall sharply. The input stocks sub-index is a leading indicator for industrial commodity demand: steel, copper, coal, and chemical feedstock spot prices often move 2-4 weeks after this sub-index shifts direction. Compare with the purchase price sub-index (aCNPMIIMPPM/A) — firms typically accelerate input purchases when prices are rising.

aCNPMISPDLT/A.description: PMI, Manufacturing Sector, From NBS of China, suppliers' delivery time
aCNPMISPDLT/A.subcategory: NBS Manufacturing PMI — Suppliers' Delivery Time
aCNPMISPDLT/A.units: Index (diffusion, inverted: >50 = faster delivery = easing supply)
aCNPMISPDLT/A.meaning: NBS Manufacturing PMI Suppliers' Delivery Time sub-index — measures month-on-month change in the speed of deliveries from upstream suppliers to manufacturing firms in the NBS PMI survey. This component is inverted in its PMI contribution: a reading above 50 means suppliers are delivering faster (supply chains easing); below 50 means deliveries are slowing (supply chain stress). Released on the last business day of the reference month at 09:00 CST.
aCNPMISPDLT/A.how_to_use: Supplier delivery times function as a real-time supply chain stress gauge. A sharp drop below 48 signals acute supply bottlenecks — either from commodity shortages, logistics disruptions, or energy rationing (as seen in September-October 2021). A rapid recovery above 50 from a trough signals supply normalization. Because this sub-index is inverted, it reduces the headline PMI when supply chains are stressed — counterintuitively, a low reading here may coexist with strong orders. Practitioners separate the 'demand-driven' PMI (new orders + output) from the 'supply-disrupted' PMI by stripping out delivery time and comparing to MinXin/Caixin equivalents.

aCNPMIMT.description: PMI, Manufacturing Sector, From NBS of China, total
aCNPMIMT.meaning: NBS Manufacturing PMI headline composite — the official Chinese manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index published by the National Bureau of Statistics. Covers approximately 3,000 manufacturing firms with a structural skew toward large state-owned and state-linked enterprises. Constructed as a weighted diffusion index from five sub-components: new orders (30%), output (25%), employment (20%), suppliers' delivery times (15%), stocks of purchases (10%). Released on the last business day of the reference month at 09:00 CST — one of China's most closely watched and market-moving monthly data releases.
aCNPMIMT.how_to_use: The NBS manufacturing PMI is China's official leading indicator of factory-sector health. A reading above 50 indicates expansion; below 50 contraction. Because the sample skews to large SOEs, NBS PMI tends to be structurally higher than Caixin PMI (which skews to private SMEs) — the NBS-Caixin spread is itself analytically important: a widening gap (NBS above Caixin) signals SOE resilience masking private-sector stress, common during periods of state-directed stimulus. Seasonal patterns are strong: February typically dips (Chinese New Year) and March rebounds sharply. Markets treat a NBS PMI print below 49.5 as a clear contraction signal warranting CNY and rates positioning.

aCNPMINMSBA/A.description: PMI, Non-manufacturing Sector, From NBS of China, business activities
aCNPMINMSBA/A.meaning: NBS Non-manufacturing PMI Business Activities sub-index — measures month-on-month change in business activity at non-manufacturing enterprises (services + construction) in the NBS survey of approximately 1,200 firms. This is the primary activity gauge within the NBS non-manufacturing PMI, distinct from the composite NBS non-manufacturing PMI headline (aCNPMINAQ). Released on the last business day of the reference month at 09:00 CST alongside the manufacturing PMI.
aCNPMINMSBA/A.how_to_use: The business activities sub-index is the most granular current-conditions gauge within the NBS non-manufacturing PMI. It breaks down into services and construction sub-components in the detailed NBS release — construction business activity is directly linked to property starts and infrastructure investment cycles, while services business activity tracks consumer-facing sectors. When business activities diverge below the business activities expectation sub-index (aCNPMINMBAE/A), it signals that firms expect recovery but current demand has not yet materialized.

aCNPMINMBAE/A.description: PMI, Non-manufacturing Sector, From NBS of China, business activities expectation
aCNPMINMBAE/A.subcategory: NBS Non-manufacturing PMI — Business Activities Expectation
aCNPMINMBAE/A.meaning: NBS Non-manufacturing PMI Business Activities Expectation sub-index — a forward-looking sub-component measuring non-manufacturing managers' expectations for business activity levels in the coming months. A reading above 50 indicates net optimism about future activity; below 50 indicates net pessimism. Released on the last business day of the reference month at 09:00 CST.
aCNPMINMBAE/A.how_to_use: The business activities expectation sub-index is the most forward-looking component of the NBS non-manufacturing PMI — it captures what services and construction managers anticipate for the near future, not what is happening today. A reading above 55 sustained for 2+ months is a strong leading signal for services sector acceleration. The spread between expectations (aCNPMINMBAE/A) and current business activities (aCNPMINMSBA/A) is a key momentum gauge: a widening positive spread (expectations above current) signals anticipated acceleration, while a narrowing or negative spread signals that prior optimism has not materialized.

aCNPMINMIIP/A.description: PMI, Non-manufacturing Sector, From NBS of China, input prices
aCNPMINMIIP/A.meaning: NBS Non-manufacturing PMI Input Prices sub-index — measures month-on-month change in the prices of inputs (labor, materials, energy) paid by non-manufacturing firms in the NBS survey. A reading above 50 indicates net input price increases; below 50 indicates net price decreases. Released on the last business day of the reference month at 09:00 CST.
aCNPMINMIIP/A.how_to_use: For non-manufacturing firms, input prices are dominated by labor costs and rental/property costs rather than commodity prices (which dominate manufacturing input costs). A rising non-manufacturing input price sub-index signals services sector cost inflation — a distinct channel from PPI-driven manufacturing cost pressures. When input prices rise while new orders hold steady, services profit margins compress. This sub-index is a useful early signal for CPI services inflation — sustained input price pressures in non-manufacturing tend to feed into CPI services prices with a 1-3 month lag. Compare with manufacturing input prices (aCNPMIIMPPM/A) to distinguish commodity-driven vs. labor-driven inflation.

aCNPMINMNEO/A.description: PMI, Non-manufacturing Sector, From NBS of China, new export orders
aCNPMINMNEO/A.subcategory: NBS Non-manufacturing PMI — New Export Orders
aCNPMINMNEO/A.meaning: NBS Non-manufacturing PMI New Export Orders sub-index — measures month-on-month change in new orders from overseas customers at non-manufacturing (services and construction) firms in the NBS survey. A reading above 50 indicates growth in services export orders; below 50 indicates contraction. Released on the last business day of the reference month at 09:00 CST.
aCNPMINMNEO/A.how_to_use: Services export orders reflect cross-border demand for China's services exports — including tourism, education, financial services, and software/IT outsourcing. This sub-index was severely impacted during COVID border closures (2020-2022) when inbound tourism collapsed. A recovery above 50 in this sub-index alongside improving global travel statistics signals reopening tailwinds for China's services trade balance. Compare with the manufacturing PMI new export orders (aCNPMIEMP3M/A) — sustained divergence (services export orders above manufacturing) would signal structural shift toward services-led external demand, a key China rebalancing metric.

aCNPMINMSNO/A.description: PMI, Non-manufacturing Sector, From NBS of China, new orders
aCNPMINMSNO/A.meaning: NBS Non-manufacturing PMI New Orders sub-index — measures month-on-month change in total new orders (domestic + export) at non-manufacturing firms in the NBS survey of approximately 1,200 services and construction firms. A reading above 50 indicates order growth; below 50 indicates contraction. Released on the last business day of the reference month at 09:00 CST.
aCNPMINMSNO/A.how_to_use: Non-manufacturing new orders is the primary leading indicator within the NBS services PMI — it leads business activities by 1-2 months. A sustained recovery of non-manufacturing new orders above 52 typically precedes services sector revenue acceleration visible in official statistics 6-8 weeks later. The new orders-to-business activities spread is directionally important: when new orders exceed current activities, demand is building; when activities exceed new orders, the pipeline is thinning. Compare with MinXin non-manufacturing new orders (aCNMPMNMNR) and Caixin services PMI new business sub-component for triangulation.

aCNNPMIGRQ/A.description: PMI, Whole Economy, From NBS of China, General PMI
aCNNPMIGRQ/A.meaning: NBS Whole-Economy General PMI (Composite) — combines manufacturing + non-manufacturing PMI. Releases alongside the manufacturing print at the end of each month.
aCNNPMIGRQ/A.how_to_use: Best aggregate cyclical gauge for the Chinese economy. Composite stays above 50 even when manufacturing PMI dips below — non-manufacturing (services + construction) typically stronger. Sustained sub-50 composite is rare; signals broad-based slowdown.

aCNSMETOTR.meaning: China Small and Medium Enterprise (SME) Overall Composite Index — Total. Published by the China Association of Small and Medium Enterprises (CASME, 中国中小企业协会) as the headline aggregate of their monthly SME survey. The survey covers thousands of SMEs across all sectors and regions, combining sub-indices for confidence, performance, marketing, cost, financing, expansion, purchasing, and risk into a single composite reading. Typically released monthly, 10-15 days after month-end.
aCNSMETOTR.how_to_use: The CASME SME Overall Index is the broadest direct measure of small and medium enterprise health in China — covering a segment that accounts for approximately 60% of GDP, 80% of urban employment, and 70% of innovation output. A reading below 100 indicates net deterioration; above 100 indicates net improvement. Sustained below-100 readings over 3+ months typically precede targeted SME support policies (tax relief, loan guarantees, social security deferrals). Compare the total composite with the financing sub-index (aCNSMEFNTR) — financing stress (below 100) without corresponding performance weakness suggests credit channel dysfunction rather than demand-led slowdown.

aCNSMECDAR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery, Confidence
aCNSMECDAR.subcategory: SME Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery — Confidence
aCNSMECDAR.meaning: CASME SME Confidence sub-index for the Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery sector. Measures the net balance of small and medium enterprises in agri-related businesses reporting improved vs. deteriorating confidence in current and near-term business conditions. Published monthly by the China Association of Small and Medium Enterprises.
aCNSMECDAR.how_to_use: Agricultural SME confidence is sensitive to seasonal cycles (planting/harvest), weather conditions, and commodity price policy (state procurement prices for grain, pork, etc.). A sharp drop in agricultural SME confidence in spring planting months can signal inadequate credit access for seasonal working capital, potentially leading to reduced planting intentions and downstream food price effects. Cross-reference with NDRC's monthly commodity prices for pork and grain — when agricultural commodity prices fall sharply, confidence and the performance sub-index (aCNSMEPFAR) tend to decline simultaneously.

aCNSMECTAR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery, Cost
aCNSMECTAR.subcategory: SME Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery — Cost
aCNSMECTAR.units: Index (diffusion/confidence scale, 100=neutral; rising = higher cost pressure)
aCNSMECTAR.meaning: CASME SME Cost sub-index for the Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery sector. Measures cost pressures (labor, materials, energy, logistics) experienced by small and medium agricultural enterprises. A reading above 100 indicates rising costs relative to neutral; persistently elevated readings signal margin squeeze in the agri-SME sector. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMECTAR.how_to_use: Agricultural SME costs are driven by fertilizer prices (phosphate, urea), diesel fuel, labor for seasonal harvesting, and animal feed ingredients (corn, soybean meal). When this sub-index rises sharply while the confidence sub-index (aCNSMECDAR) and performance sub-index (aCNSMEPFAR) fall, it indicates a classic cost-squeeze scenario for agricultural SMEs — inputs rising faster than output prices. This often precedes requests for state price support or credit subsidies for the agricultural sector.
