aCNSMEEPAR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery, Expansion
aCNSMEEPAR.subcategory: SME Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery — Expansion
aCNSMEEPAR.meaning: CASME SME Expansion sub-index for the Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery sector. Measures expansion intentions — hiring, capital investment, capacity additions — among small and medium enterprises in agri-related sectors. A reading above 100 indicates net expansion plans; below 100 indicates net contraction or investment holds. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEEPAR.how_to_use: Agricultural SME expansion intentions are a leading indicator for rural fixed investment and seasonal labor demand. When this sub-index rises ahead of planting season, it signals increased mechanization investment and farm consolidation activity. Conversely, a drop below 95 entering harvest season signals pessimism about post-harvest prices and income, which historically reduces rural consumer spending in Q4. Use alongside the financing sub-index (aCNSMEFNAR) — expansion intentions without financing confidence means investment plans are aspirational rather than funded.

aCNSMEFNAR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery, Financing
aCNSMEFNAR.subcategory: SME Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery — Financing
aCNSMEFNAR.meaning: CASME SME Financing sub-index for the Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery sector. Measures the ease of obtaining financing (bank loans, rural credit cooperatives, policy bank lending) for small and medium agri-sector enterprises. A reading above 100 indicates improving financing conditions; below 100 indicates tightening credit access. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEFNAR.how_to_use: Agricultural SME financing access is structurally challenged in China — rural collateral (land use rights) is difficult to pledge, and rural credit cooperatives have constrained balance sheets. When this sub-index drops below 95 entering spring planting, it is a leading signal for potential shortfalls in agricultural credit and subsequent PBOC rural finance policy responses (directed re-lending quotas, rural bank required reserve ratio cuts). Compare with total SME financing (aCNSMEFNTR) — if agri-sector financing stress is deeper than the overall SME average, it signals rural-specific credit channel problems.

aCNSMEMKAR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery, Marketing
aCNSMEMKAR.subcategory: SME Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery — Marketing
aCNSMEMKAR.meaning: CASME SME Marketing sub-index for the Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery sector. Measures the ease and effectiveness of sales and marketing for small and medium agri-sector enterprises — capturing order receipts, product pricing power, and sales channel access. A reading above 100 indicates improving marketing conditions; below 100 indicates deterioration. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEMKAR.how_to_use: Agricultural SME marketing conditions reflect demand-side dynamics in China's food supply chain — wholesale market prices, cold-chain logistics access, and e-commerce platform penetration for farm products. When the marketing sub-index drops sharply at harvest time, it signals oversupply in local markets and weak downstream absorption — a precursor to farm-gate price collapses. This sub-index is particularly useful for monitoring the policy effectiveness of direct-to-consumer agricultural e-commerce initiatives promoted since 2015.

aCNSMEPFAR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery, Performance
aCNSMEPFAR.subcategory: SME Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery — Performance
aCNSMEPFAR.meaning: CASME SME Performance sub-index for the Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery sector. Measures current-period business performance (revenues, profits, order fulfillment) at small and medium agri-sector enterprises. A reading above 100 indicates performance above neutral/prior period; below 100 indicates underperformance. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEPFAR.how_to_use: Agricultural SME performance is the most coincident indicator within the CASME agri-sector suite — it reflects actual revenues and profits rather than expectations. Strong performance readings at harvest time confirm good price realizations; weak readings despite adequate production volumes signal marketing and distribution bottlenecks (excess supply unable to reach consumers efficiently). Use to validate whether the confidence sub-index (aCNSMECDAR) is tracking actual outcomes or merely sentiment. Compare with the total SME performance (aCNSMEPFTR) to assess relative agri-sector performance versus the broader SME economy.

aCNSMEPCAR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery, Purchasing
aCNSMEPCAR.subcategory: SME Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery — Purchasing
aCNSMEPCAR.meaning: CASME SME Purchasing sub-index for the Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery sector. Measures procurement activity — the volume and ease of purchasing inputs (seeds, fertilizers, feed, equipment) by small and medium agri-sector enterprises. A reading above 100 indicates increased purchasing activity; below 100 indicates reduced procurement. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEPCAR.how_to_use: Agricultural SME purchasing activity follows strong seasonal patterns aligned with planting cycles: spring surge (March-May) and autumn planting (August-September). A below-100 reading in pre-planting months signals constrained input procurement — typically due to financing difficulties (cross-reference aCNSMEFNAR) or input price expectations. When purchasing activity spikes above 110 while the financing sub-index is below 100, it suggests agri-SMEs are stretching their balance sheets to secure inputs — a credit risk signal. Compare with total SME purchasing (aCNSMEPCTR) to gauge agri-sector purchasing relative to economy-wide SME procurement trends.

aCNSMERKAR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery, Risk
aCNSMERKAR.subcategory: SME Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery — Risk
aCNSMERKAR.units: Index (diffusion/confidence scale; higher reading = higher perceived risk)
aCNSMERKAR.meaning: CASME SME Risk sub-index for the Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery sector. Measures the perceived level of business risk among small and medium agri-sector enterprises — encompassing market risk, weather risk, policy risk, and financial risk. Higher readings indicate elevated risk perception; lower readings indicate reduced risk. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMERKAR.how_to_use: The risk sub-index is a leading indicator for investment and expansion pullbacks — when risk perception spikes, subsequent expansion (aCNSMEEPAR) and purchasing (aCNSMEPCAR) sub-indices typically fall 1-2 months later. Agricultural risk readings spike during: (1) extreme weather events (flooding, drought), (2) disease outbreaks (African swine fever, avian flu), (3) sharp commodity price swings, and (4) policy announcements (tariff changes on soy imports affecting feed costs). A spike in agri-sector risk above 110 is a meaningful policy trigger for NDRC and MARA intervention.

aCNSMETOAR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery, Total
aCNSMETOAR.subcategory: SME Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery — Total Composite
aCNSMETOAR.meaning: CASME SME Total Composite index for the Agriculture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry & Fishery sector — the weighted aggregate of all sub-indices (confidence, performance, marketing, cost, financing, expansion, purchasing, risk) for agri-sector SMEs. Published monthly by CASME. This is the headline reading for the agricultural SME segment within the CASME SME survey system.
aCNSMETOAR.how_to_use: Use the agricultural SME total composite as the headline gauge for small-firm agri-sector health. A sustained drop below 95 for 2+ months signals systemic stress in China's agricultural SME base — historically associated with: commodity price crashes, credit squeezes, weather disasters, or disease outbreaks. Compare with the overall SME composite (aCNSMETOTR) to assess whether agri-sector weakness is sector-specific or part of a broader SME economic slowdown. Policy makers use this index to calibrate agricultural support programs (price floors, targeted lending) under the rural revitalization strategy.

aCNSMECDTR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Confidence, Total
aCNSMECDTR.subcategory: SME Confidence Index — Total All Sectors
aCNSMECDTR.meaning: CASME SME Confidence sub-index — Total across all sectors. Aggregates confidence readings from all surveyed SME sectors into a single economy-wide SME confidence gauge. Published monthly by the China Association of Small and Medium Enterprises. This is the overall SME confidence barometer, capturing entrepreneurial sentiment about current and near-term business conditions across manufacturing, services, construction, agriculture, and other sectors.
aCNSMECDTR.how_to_use: SME confidence is one of China's most economically significant sentiment indicators — SMEs employ roughly 80% of China's urban workforce. A sustained drop below 97 for 3+ consecutive months has consistently preceded targeted policy easing (tax rebates, social security cuts, bank lending quota expansions for SMEs). When SME confidence diverges below large-enterprise confidence tracked by NBS quarterly surveys, it signals a two-speed economy where policy stimulus flows primarily to state-owned enterprises. Compare with total SME performance (aCNSMEPFTR) to distinguish sentiment-driven from fundamentals-driven confidence changes.

aCNSMECDCR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Construction, Confidence
aCNSMECDCR.meaning: CASME SME Confidence sub-index for the Construction sector. Measures the net balance of small and medium construction enterprises reporting improved vs. deteriorating confidence in current and near-term business conditions. Construction SMEs include residential contractors, infrastructure subcontractors, fit-out firms, and civil engineering specialists. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMECDCR.how_to_use: Construction SME confidence is directly tied to property developer order books, infrastructure project approvals, and payment collection cycles. When property developers face liquidity stress, construction SMEs are among the first affected via delayed payments or canceled orders. A drop in construction SME confidence below 95 typically leads actual construction starts data by 1-2 months. Compare with the financing sub-index (aCNSMEFNCR) — if financing confidence drops alongside business confidence, it signals that developers are not paying subcontractors, creating a cascading credit crunch in the construction supply chain.

aCNSMECTCR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Construction, Cost
aCNSMECTCR.meaning: CASME SME Cost sub-index for the Construction sector. Measures cost pressures — materials (steel, cement, sand/aggregate), labor (migrant workers), and equipment rental — experienced by small and medium construction enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMECTCR.how_to_use: Construction SME cost dynamics are driven primarily by steel rebar prices and migrant worker wages. When construction cost readings spike above 110, it signals either a commodity price surge or a labor shortage — check rebar futures and migrant wage data to distinguish the two. High costs with weak confidence (aCNSMECDCR) and poor performance (aCNSMEPFCR) indicate a full margin squeeze on construction SMEs. This combination historically precedes consolidation in the construction subcontractor market as smaller firms exit. Compare with total SME cost index (aCNSMECTTR) for economy-wide context.

aCNSMEEPCR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Construction, Expansion
aCNSMEEPCR.meaning: CASME SME Expansion sub-index for the Construction sector. Measures expansion intentions — new project bidding, workforce hiring, equipment investment — among small and medium construction enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEEPCR.how_to_use: Construction SME expansion intentions are a 2-3 month leading indicator for construction activity. Rising expansion intentions ahead of peak construction seasons (spring and autumn) confirm that subcontractors are positioning for new project starts. When expansion intentions remain below 95 despite rising infrastructure spending announcements, it signals that payment collection problems (from delayed developer/government payments) prevent SMEs from committing to new contracts. Use alongside financing (aCNSMEFNCR) to validate whether expansion plans are fundable.

aCNSMEFNCR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Construction, Financing
aCNSMEFNCR.meaning: CASME SME Financing sub-index for the Construction sector. Measures the ease of obtaining project financing, working capital loans, and payment collection for small and medium construction enterprises. Construction SMEs are uniquely dependent on developer and local government payment cycles. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEFNCR.how_to_use: When property developer liquidity deteriorates, construction subcontractors face payment delays that force them to seek bridging loans at higher rates. A financing sub-index below 95 sustained for 3+ months is a reliable leading indicator of broader construction supply chain distress, often preceding NBS data showing a slump in construction investment. Cross-reference with total SME financing (aCNSMEFNTR) to assess whether the stress is construction-specific or economy-wide.

aCNSMEMKCR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Construction, Marketing
aCNSMEMKCR.meaning: CASME SME Marketing sub-index for the Construction sector. Measures the ease and effectiveness of project bidding success rates and contract win rates for small and medium construction enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEMKCR.how_to_use: Construction SME marketing tracks the competitive intensity and demand environment for construction contracts. When this sub-index drops sharply, it signals project slowdowns — either developers pausing new starts or infrastructure project approvals delaying. A divergence between marketing (weak) and performance (still holding) indicates that currently active projects are progressing but the forward pipeline is thin — a 2-3 month leading indicator for activity slowdowns. Use alongside NBS non-manufacturing PMI construction activity (aCNPMINMSBA/A).

aCNSMEPFCR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Construction, Performance
aCNSMEPFCR.meaning: CASME SME Performance sub-index for the Construction sector. Measures current-period business performance (revenues, completed milestones, payment receipts) at small and medium construction enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEPFCR.how_to_use: Construction SME performance reflects actual cash flow — whether firms have received payments for completed work. Sustained below-100 performance alongside above-100 expansion intentions reveals a dangerous gap: firms taking on new projects while existing cash flows are inadequate. This pattern preceded several waves of SME construction company insolvencies in China (2015, 2018, 2022). Compare with total SME performance (aCNSMEPFTR) and NBS construction business activity PMI for validation.

aCNSMEPCCR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Construction, Purchasing
aCNSMEPCCR.meaning: CASME SME Purchasing sub-index for the Construction sector. Measures procurement activity — steel, cement, equipment, specialty materials — by small and medium construction enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEPCCR.how_to_use: Construction SME purchasing is a leading indicator for industrial materials demand. A spike in construction SME purchasing activity 4-6 weeks ahead of spring construction peak confirms restocking for anticipated demand surges. When purchasing drops sharply while projects are reportedly ongoing, it signals cash flow shortfalls preventing material procurement. Compare with the cost sub-index (aCNSMECTCR) — if purchasing falls while costs rise, SMEs face supplier financing withdrawal.

aCNSMERKCR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Construction, Risk
aCNSMERKCR.units: Index (diffusion/confidence scale; higher reading = higher perceived risk)
aCNSMERKCR.meaning: CASME SME Risk sub-index for the Construction sector. Measures the perceived level of business risk among small and medium construction enterprises — encompassing payment default risk, policy risk (regulatory changes, project cancellations), and financial risk. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMERKCR.how_to_use: Construction SME risk perception is a leading indicator for sector distress. Sustained risk readings above 110 typically precede waves of subcontractor defaults, project suspensions, and credit tightening. During the 2021-23 property crisis, this sub-index spiked sharply as construction SMEs saw developer payment defaults multiply. A spike above 115 warrants close monitoring of construction firm NPL ratios at regional banks. Compare with the overall SME risk index (aCNSMERKTR) — construction risk spiking while other sectors remain contained signals property/infrastructure-specific stress.

aCNSMETOCR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Construction, Total
aCNSMETOCR.meaning: CASME SME Total Composite index for the Construction sector — the weighted aggregate of all sub-indices for small and medium construction enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMETOCR.how_to_use: The construction SME composite is a high-frequency leading indicator for China's investment cycle. Construction SMEs are typically the first to feel demand shifts — they receive orders from developers and local governments earlier than official statistics capture. A sustained drop below 95 for 2+ months has historically preceded NBS construction investment data turning negative by 1-3 months. Compare with the total SME composite (aCNSMETOTR) and NBS non-manufacturing PMI construction sub-component to triangulate China's construction cycle.

aCNSMECTTR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Cost, Total
aCNSMECTTR.subcategory: SME Cost Index — Total All Sectors
aCNSMECTTR.meaning: CASME SME Cost sub-index — Total across all sectors. Aggregates cost pressure readings from all surveyed SME sectors into a single economy-wide SME cost gauge. Captures labor, raw material, energy, logistics, and financing costs across manufacturing, services, construction, agriculture, and other sectors. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMECTTR.how_to_use: The total SME cost index is a broad-based measure of cost inflation in China's SME economy. When this index rises above 105 for 2+ months, it signals widespread cost-push pressure, often preceding tighter SME profit margins and investment pullbacks. The SME cost index captures labor cost inflation that may not appear in official wage statistics — SMEs pay market wages and are more sensitive to labor market tightness than SOEs. Compare with the PPI and CPI to understand whether SME cost pressures are commodity-driven, labor-driven, or both.

aCNSMECDER.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Eastern China, Confidence
aCNSMECDER.meaning: CASME SME Confidence sub-index for Eastern China. Covers small and medium enterprises in China's eastern coastal provinces — including Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Shanghai, Shandong, Fujian, and Guangdong. Eastern China is China's manufacturing and trade heartland, home to export-oriented manufacturing clusters and advanced services hubs. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMECDER.how_to_use: Eastern China SME confidence is the single most globally relevant regional sub-index because eastern coastal firms are most exposed to export demand, foreign investment, and global supply chain dynamics. When eastern China confidence diverges below the national total (aCNSMECDTR), it often reflects export headwinds or regulatory pressure on coastal manufacturing. During trade tensions (2018-19, 2025), eastern China SME confidence fell sharply ahead of NBS export data deterioration, providing early warning. Compare with the NBS new export orders PMI (aCNPMIEMP3M/A) for validation.

aCNSMECTER.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Eastern China, Cost
aCNSMECTER.meaning: CASME SME Cost sub-index for Eastern China. Measures cost pressures for small and medium enterprises in China's eastern coastal provinces. Costs in eastern China are structurally higher than inland regions — land costs, labor wages, and regulatory compliance costs are elevated in Yangtze River Delta and Pearl River Delta clusters. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMECTER.how_to_use: Eastern China SME cost pressure is a leading indicator for manufacturing relocation dynamics. When eastern China costs persistently outpace inland regions, it accelerates the migration of labor-intensive manufacturing to central and western China or Southeast Asia. A sharp spike in eastern China SME costs relative to central China (aCNSMECTIR) signals accelerating structural cost pressures. Used by supply chain analysts to track China's industrial geographic rebalancing and assess competitiveness of coastal manufacturing clusters.

aCNSMEEPER.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Eastern China, Expansion
aCNSMEEPER.meaning: CASME SME Expansion sub-index for Eastern China. Measures expansion intentions — investment, hiring, capacity additions — among small and medium enterprises in China's eastern coastal provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEEPER.how_to_use: Eastern China SME expansion intentions are a leading indicator for coastal manufacturing investment and high-tech industry capex. Strong expansion intentions signal confidence in export markets and domestic technology-driven demand. A drop below 95 in eastern expansion while inland regions remain firm (aCNSMEEPIR, aCNSMEEPNR) suggests coastal-specific headwinds rather than a national investment slowdown. This regional divergence is particularly useful for infrastructure and real estate investors tracking geographic investment allocation shifts.

aCNSMEFNER.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Eastern China, Financing
aCNSMEFNER.meaning: CASME SME Financing sub-index for Eastern China. Measures the ease of obtaining financing for small and medium enterprises in China's eastern coastal provinces — where access to bank credit, equity markets, bond markets, and venture capital is structurally better than inland regions. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEFNER.how_to_use: Eastern China SME financing conditions are the most market-sensitive of all regional financing sub-indices because eastern firms have the most diversified funding access. When financing conditions deteriorate in eastern China, it signals credit channel dysfunction likely to spread nationally. A drop below 95 in eastern financing while western regions hold steady suggests banking sector risk-off behavior toward higher-risk coastal sectors. Compare with total SME financing (aCNSMEFNTR) for national context.

aCNSMEMKER.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Eastern China, Marketing
aCNSMEMKER.meaning: CASME SME Marketing sub-index for Eastern China. Measures the ease and effectiveness of sales and marketing for small and medium enterprises in China's eastern coastal provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEMKER.how_to_use: Eastern China SME marketing conditions reflect both domestic demand conditions in China's wealthiest consumer markets (Shanghai, Zhejiang, Guangdong) and export order dynamics for coastal manufacturers. When marketing conditions deteriorate in eastern China while inland regions hold, it suggests coastal demand underperformance — often due to real estate market weakness or export demand softness. Compare with NBS retail sales data for coastal provinces and the NBS new export orders PMI (aCNPMIEMP3M/A) to validate the survey signal.

aCNSMEPFER.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Eastern China, Performance
aCNSMEPFER.meaning: CASME SME Performance sub-index for Eastern China. Measures current-period business performance (revenues, profits) at small and medium enterprises in China's eastern coastal provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEPFER.how_to_use: Eastern China SME performance is a coincident indicator for China's most economically advanced regional economies. Strong eastern performance alongside weak central/western performance signals that the economic recovery is geographically concentrated in coastal hubs. A sustained performance drop in eastern China is a high-conviction signal for broader economic stress because eastern firms typically have the best access to credit and demand support — their underperformance suggests macro headwinds that will spread nationally.

aCNSMEPCER.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Eastern China, Purchasing
aCNSMEPCER.meaning: CASME SME Purchasing sub-index for Eastern China. Measures procurement activity — raw materials, components, equipment — by small and medium enterprises in China's eastern coastal provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEPCER.how_to_use: Eastern China SME purchasing is the most globally connected of all regional purchasing sub-indices because coastal manufacturers import significant portions of raw materials and components. A drop in eastern purchasing activity often leads import data by 4-6 weeks. During supply chain reconfiguration episodes, this data helps track whether firms are shifting procurement from traditional sources (Japan, South Korea for components) to domestic alternatives. Compare with NBS manufacturing PMI stocks of major inputs (aCNPMISTMJI/A) for cross-validation.

aCNSMERKER.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Eastern China, Risk
aCNSMERKER.units: Index (diffusion/confidence scale; higher reading = higher perceived risk)
aCNSMERKER.meaning: CASME SME Risk sub-index for Eastern China. Measures perceived business risk among small and medium enterprises in China's eastern coastal provinces — encompassing export market risk, regulatory risk (tech sector regulations, data laws), property market risk, and financial risk. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMERKER.how_to_use: Eastern China SME risk is highly sensitive to regulatory and geopolitical developments. The tech sector crackdowns of 2021-22 sent eastern China risk readings to historic highs as internet platform-dependent SMEs faced regulatory uncertainty. Trade tension escalations in 2018-19 and 2025 drove sharp risk spikes in coastal manufacturing SMEs. A spike above 110 in eastern risk while inland regions remain stable warrants monitoring for regulatory or trade-driven policy shifts affecting coastal industries.

aCNSMETOER.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Eastern China, Total
aCNSMETOER.meaning: CASME SME Total Composite index for Eastern China — the weighted aggregate of all sub-indices for small and medium enterprises in China's eastern coastal provinces. Published monthly by CASME. Eastern China generates roughly 45-50% of national GDP and accounts for the majority of manufacturing exports.
aCNSMETOER.how_to_use: The eastern China SME composite is the most globally significant of CASME's regional indices because it tracks China's export-manufacturing and advanced-services heartland. Use as the primary regional gauge when assessing China's trade cycle or coastal economic health. Compare with northeastern China (aCNSMETOOR, which reflects heavy industrial legacy sectors) and with middle-south China (aCNSMETOIR) to track the inland-coastal divergence characterizing China's uneven development.

aCNSMEEPTR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Expansion, Total
aCNSMEEPTR.subcategory: SME Expansion Index — Total All Sectors
aCNSMEEPTR.meaning: CASME SME Expansion sub-index — Total across all sectors. Aggregates expansion intention readings from all surveyed SME sectors into a single economy-wide expansion gauge capturing hiring plans, capital investment intentions, and capacity expansion plans. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEEPTR.how_to_use: Total SME expansion intentions are a leading indicator for private-sector fixed asset investment and employment growth. When this index rises above 100 for 2+ months, it signals that SMEs plan to expand headcount and capital, typically showing up in private investment data 1-2 quarters later. A drop below 95 signals SME investment retrenchment — when this coincides with state-owned enterprise investment accelerating, it reveals a crowding-out dynamic where policy stimulus favors SOEs. Compare with the financing sub-index (aCNSMEFNTR) — expansion intentions are only meaningful if financing is accessible.

aCNSMEFNTR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Financing, Total
aCNSMEFNTR.subcategory: SME Financing Index — Total All Sectors
aCNSMEFNTR.meaning: CASME SME Financing sub-index — Total across all sectors. Aggregates financing condition readings from all surveyed SME sectors into a single economy-wide SME financing gauge capturing bank loan availability, interest rates, payment collection, and overall credit access. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEFNTR.how_to_use: SME financing conditions are the single most policy-sensitive sub-index in the CASME survey — PBOC and CBIRC closely monitor SME credit access as a key policy target. A drop below 97 in this sub-index for 2+ months has consistently preceded PBOC actions (relending facility expansions, targeted RRR cuts, CBIRC SME loan guidance). This index leads business confidence (aCNSMECDTR) by 1-3 months — when financing deteriorates before confidence does, it signals a credit-channel problem rather than a demand-side slowdown, and serves as an early warning for banking sector SME NPL trends.

aCNSMECDHR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Hotels & Catering , Confidence
aCNSMECDHR.meaning: CASME SME Confidence sub-index for the Hotels & Catering sector. Measures the net balance of small and medium hotels, restaurants, catering firms, and food service businesses reporting improved vs. deteriorating confidence. This sector employs tens of millions of workers and is highly sensitive to consumer discretionary spending and mobility restrictions. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMECDHR.how_to_use: Hotels & Catering SME confidence is among the most sensitive of all sectoral sub-indices to consumer discretionary spending. During COVID lockdowns, this sub-index collapsed to historic lows before any other sector. Post-lockdown recovery here is a leading indicator for consumer spending recovery — it typically precedes official NBS catering revenue data by 4-6 weeks. Compare with consumer confidence (aCNCONCF) to validate whether improving hospitality SME confidence reflects actual consumer spending recovery or merely optimism.

aCNSMECTHR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Hotels & Catering , Cost
aCNSMECTHR.meaning: CASME SME Cost sub-index for the Hotels & Catering sector. Measures cost pressures — food ingredient costs, labor (kitchen and service staff), rent, and utilities — experienced by small and medium hospitality and food service enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMECTHR.how_to_use: Hotels & Catering SME costs are heavily influenced by food CPI (pork, vegetables, cooking oil), urban rent prices, and minimum wage adjustments. A cost spike above 108 directly compresses restaurant profit margins — the sector's margins are typically thin (3-8% net margin) so cost shocks can quickly drive insolvency. When food CPI rises sharply, this sub-index spikes and the performance sub-index (aCNSMEPFHR) drops simultaneously. This is a leading indicator for food CPI passthrough: if catering SMEs cannot raise menu prices to offset costs, they absorb losses rather than raising prices.

aCNSMEEPHR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Hotels & Catering , Expansion
aCNSMEEPHR.meaning: CASME SME Expansion sub-index for the Hotels & Catering sector. Measures expansion intentions — new restaurant openings, hotel room additions, franchising plans, staff hiring — among small and medium hospitality and food service enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEEPHR.how_to_use: Hotels & Catering SME expansion intentions are a forward-looking indicator for consumer services employment and urban rental demand. When expansion intentions recover sharply after a shock, it signals that consumer-facing services are poised for employment recovery — particularly important given the sector's role as a major employer of low-skilled urban migrants. A sustained expansion reading above 100 is a positive leading signal for consumer services employment growth, which feeds directly into household income and consumption.

aCNSMEFNHR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Hotels & Catering , Financing
aCNSMEFNHR.meaning: CASME SME Financing sub-index for the Hotels & Catering sector. Measures the ease of obtaining financing for small and medium hospitality and food service enterprises. This sector faces structural bank lending challenges — lack of collateral, short lease tenures, and high failure rates make banks reluctant lenders. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEFNHR.how_to_use: Financing access for hospitality SMEs is the binding constraint on sector recovery speed after external shocks. When COVID restrictions eased in 2023, confidence and expansion intentions recovered rapidly but financing conditions lagged — restaurants struggled to obtain working capital loans to restock and rehire. A divergence between improving confidence (aCNSMECDHR) and stagnant financing is a signal that recovery will be slow due to credit constraints. PBOC and local government emergency loan programs are often triggered when this sub-index drops below 93.

aCNSMEMKHR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Hotels & Catering , Marketing
aCNSMEMKHR.meaning: CASME SME Marketing sub-index for the Hotels & Catering sector. Measures the ease and effectiveness of customer acquisition, occupancy rates, table turn rates, and booking volumes for small and medium hospitality and food service enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEMKHR.how_to_use: Hospitality SME marketing conditions are a high-frequency proxy for China's domestic tourism and dining demand. Strong marketing readings during major holidays (Spring Festival, National Day Golden Week) confirm consumer spending momentum. A sharp drop in marketing conditions outside of lockdown periods signals structural consumer caution — when hospitality marketing struggles in normal operating environments, it often reflects household deleveraging pressures reducing discretionary food and travel spending.

aCNSMEPFHR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Hotels & Catering , Performance
aCNSMEPFHR.meaning: CASME SME Performance sub-index for the Hotels & Catering sector. Measures current-period business performance (revenues, occupancy, table covers) at small and medium hospitality and food service enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEPFHR.how_to_use: Hotels & Catering SME performance is one of the most direct real-time gauges of China's consumer discretionary spending — it captures actual revenue outcomes before official NBS catering and tourism revenue statistics are released (which lag by 3-4 weeks). Strong seasonality is expected: Golden Week (October) and Spring Festival typically see performance spikes. Sustained below-100 performance outside of lockdown periods is a meaningful signal of structural consumer confidence weakness, warranting comparison with consumer confidence indices (aCNCONCF).

aCNSMEPCHR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Hotels & Catering , Purchasing
aCNSMEPCHR.meaning: CASME SME Purchasing sub-index for the Hotels & Catering sector. Measures procurement activity — food ingredients, beverages, linen, cleaning supplies — by small and medium hospitality and food service enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEPCHR.how_to_use: Hospitality SME purchasing is a leading indicator for food and consumer goods wholesale demand. A spike in hospitality purchasing ahead of major holidays confirms restocking for anticipated demand surges and is typically followed by food CPI pressure 2-4 weeks later. When purchasing drops while performance holds up, it signals that SMEs are running down existing stocks — a negative leading indicator for wholesale food demand. This sub-index tracks effective food supply chain demand that does not show up in manufacturing PMI data.

aCNSMERKHR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Hotels & Catering , Risk
aCNSMERKHR.units: Index (diffusion/confidence scale; higher reading = higher perceived risk)
aCNSMERKHR.meaning: CASME SME Risk sub-index for the Hotels & Catering sector. Measures perceived business risk among small and medium hospitality and food service enterprises — including food safety risk, epidemic/lockdown risk, rent increase risk, labor cost risk, and demand volatility risk. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMERKHR.how_to_use: Hotels & Catering SME risk perception is highly sensitive to public health developments and consumer mobility. The sector showed the most extreme risk readings of any CASME sector during COVID episodes. Post-pandemic, this sub-index remains elevated relative to pre-COVID averages, reflecting lingering operational caution. A spike in risk perception above 112 absent an obvious external shock often signals that operators are anticipating policy changes (food safety crackdowns, labor regulation tightening) that will increase compliance costs.

aCNSMETOHR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Hotels & Catering , Total
aCNSMETOHR.meaning: CASME SME Total Composite index for the Hotels & Catering sector — the weighted aggregate of all sub-indices for small and medium hospitality and food service enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMETOHR.how_to_use: The Hotels & Catering SME composite is the most consumer-cycle-sensitive of all CASME sectoral composites. Use it as a high-frequency leading indicator for NBS catering revenue data and as a real-time read on consumer discretionary confidence. The composite is particularly valuable during policy transition periods — when COVID restrictions ease or consumer stimulus policies are announced, the Hotels & Catering composite typically recovers faster than manufacturing SME indices, providing early confirmation of consumer recovery.

aCNSMECDMR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Manufacturing , Confidence
aCNSMECDMR.meaning: CASME SME Confidence sub-index for the Manufacturing sector. Measures the net balance of small and medium manufacturing enterprises reporting improved vs. deteriorating confidence in current and near-term business conditions. Manufacturing SMEs form the foundation of China's industrial production capacity, particularly in consumer goods, intermediate goods, and light industry. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMECDMR.how_to_use: Manufacturing SME confidence is the most directly comparable CASME metric to PMI data. When this sub-index diverges significantly from the NBS manufacturing PMI (aCNPMIMT), it signals the state-private divergence in manufacturing: NBS PMI skews to large SOEs while CASME captures the SME layer. A sustained divergence of 5+ index points (CASME confidence below NBS PMI equivalent) is a common feature of periods when SOE capacity expansion coincides with SME margin compression. Use alongside the Caixin PMI (aCNPMIBAQ) for triangulation.

aCNSMECTMR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Manufacturing , Cost
aCNSMECTMR.meaning: CASME SME Cost sub-index for the Manufacturing sector. Measures cost pressures — raw materials, energy, labor, logistics, and financing costs — experienced by small and medium manufacturing enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMECTMR.how_to_use: Manufacturing SME cost pressure is directly linked to commodity prices (steel, copper, aluminum, chemical feedstocks), electricity prices, and logistics tariffs. When this sub-index rises above 108 for 2+ months, it typically coincides with PPI acceleration and industrial profit margin compression. SMEs feel cost pressures more acutely than large firms because they lack purchasing scale and hedging tools available to SOEs. Persistent cost pressure above 108 without corresponding price-setting ability (tracked via marketing sub-index aCNSMEMKMR) signals margin compression leading to SME financial stress. Compare with NBS PMI purchase price sub-index (aCNPMIIMPPM/A).

aCNSMEEPMR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Manufacturing , Expansion
aCNSMEEPMR.meaning: CASME SME Expansion sub-index for the Manufacturing sector. Measures expansion intentions — new production lines, equipment investment, workforce hiring — among small and medium manufacturing enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEEPMR.how_to_use: Manufacturing SME expansion intentions are a leading indicator for private-sector manufacturing investment. When this sub-index exceeds 100 for 2+ consecutive months, it signals that SME manufacturers plan to invest in capacity — which typically shows up in machinery and equipment imports 2-3 months later. The expansion sub-index is particularly sensitive to credit availability (aCNSMEFNMR) — expansion intentions without financing confidence are aspirational; expansion intentions alongside improving financing signal genuine capex cycle recovery.

aCNSMEFNMR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Manufacturing , Financing
aCNSMEFNMR.meaning: CASME SME Financing sub-index for the Manufacturing sector. Measures the ease of obtaining financing — bank loans, accounts receivable factoring, supply chain finance, equipment leasing — for small and medium manufacturing enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEFNMR.how_to_use: Manufacturing SME financing is the critical binding constraint on China's private investment cycle. PBOC's targeted SME lending policies (manufacturing-specific relending facilities, inclusive finance loan quotas) are calibrated in part using this type of survey data. A drop below 95 in manufacturing SME financing is a reliable trigger for policy responses. When manufacturing financing deteriorates while construction financing (aCNSMEFNCR) holds, it signals a sectoral credit allocation problem — banks may be over-concentrated in collateral-rich construction while under-serving manufacturing SMEs.

aCNSMEMKMR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Manufacturing , Marketing
aCNSMEMKMR.meaning: CASME SME Marketing sub-index for the Manufacturing sector. Measures the ease and effectiveness of sales and marketing — order win rates, pricing power, customer acquisition — for small and medium manufacturing enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEMKMR.how_to_use: Manufacturing SME marketing conditions reflect both domestic demand and export demand for SME products. When marketing conditions deteriorate while costs (aCNSMECTMR) rise, SME manufacturers face a classic price-cost squeeze — a leading indicator for SME profit growth and, with a lag of 2-3 months, for bank SME NPL ratios. Compare with NBS new orders PMI (aCNPMINEWOD/A) — if SME marketing deteriorates while NBS new orders hold, it confirms large SOEs are capturing order flow at the expense of SMEs.

aCNSMEPFMR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Manufacturing , Performance
aCNSMEPFMR.meaning: CASME SME Performance sub-index for the Manufacturing sector. Measures current-period business performance (revenues, profitability, order fulfillment) at small and medium manufacturing enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEPFMR.how_to_use: Manufacturing SME performance is the most coincident indicator in the CASME manufacturing suite — it reflects actual revenue and profit outcomes. Sustained below-100 performance is a leading signal for rising SME manufacturing NPLs at banks, typically with a 2-3 month lag. When performance drops while expansion intentions (aCNSMEEPMR) remain positive, firms are still planning to invest despite current weakness — often reflecting anticipation of policy support. Compare with NBS industrial profit growth data for large firms to assess the SOE-SME profit gap.

aCNSMEPCMR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Manufacturing , Purchasing
aCNSMEPCMR.meaning: CASME SME Purchasing sub-index for the Manufacturing sector. Measures procurement activity — raw materials, components, energy — by small and medium manufacturing enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEPCMR.how_to_use: Manufacturing SME purchasing is a leading indicator for industrial commodity and component demand at the SME level. Because SMEs make up the majority of China's industrial purchasers by number, a broad-based drop in SME purchasing predicts industrial demand softening 4-8 weeks ahead of hard data. When purchasing falls while costs rise (aCNSMECTMR), SMEs are reducing procurement because affordability is declining — a deflationary demand-destruction signal. Compare with NBS manufacturing PMI stocks of major inputs (aCNPMISTMJI/A) to understand the aggregate inventory picture.

aCNSMERKMR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Manufacturing , Risk
aCNSMERKMR.units: Index (diffusion/confidence scale; higher reading = higher perceived risk)
aCNSMERKMR.meaning: CASME SME Risk sub-index for the Manufacturing sector. Measures perceived business risk among small and medium manufacturing enterprises — encompassing demand risk, input cost risk, trade policy risk, regulatory risk (environmental, safety), and financial risk. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMERKMR.how_to_use: Manufacturing SME risk perception typically spikes around: (1) trade tariff escalations (supply chain disruption and export demand risk), (2) environmental crackdowns (shutdown orders for non-compliant facilities), (3) energy rationing episodes (power cuts forcing production halts), and (4) commodity price surges. When manufacturing risk spikes well above the total SME risk (aCNSMERKTR), it signals manufacturing-specific headwinds. A persistent above-115 risk reading in manufacturing typically precedes deceleration in private manufacturing investment 2-3 months later.

aCNSMETOMR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Manufacturing , Total
aCNSMETOMR.meaning: CASME SME Total Composite index for the Manufacturing sector — the weighted aggregate of all sub-indices for small and medium manufacturing enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMETOMR.how_to_use: The manufacturing SME composite should be monitored alongside the NBS and Caixin manufacturing PMIs to form a complete picture of China's industrial cycle. When the CASME manufacturing SME composite drops below 95 while the NBS PMI holds above 50, it signals that official PMI data is masking widespread SME stress — a pattern common in periods of state-directed credit allocation. For equity investors, the CASME manufacturing SME composite is more predictive of A-share small-cap manufacturing performance than the NBS PMI, which reflects large-cap SOE conditions.

aCNSMEMKTR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Marketing, Total
aCNSMEMKTR.subcategory: SME Marketing Index — Total All Sectors
aCNSMEMKTR.meaning: CASME SME Marketing sub-index — Total across all sectors. Aggregates marketing condition readings from all surveyed SME sectors into a single economy-wide SME marketing gauge capturing sales conditions, order win rates, pricing power, and demand environment across manufacturing, services, construction, agriculture, and other sectors. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEMKTR.how_to_use: Total SME marketing conditions are a broad-based measure of demand conditions faced by China's private sector. When this index drops below 97, it signals deteriorating revenue generation across the SME economy — a leading indicator for SME profit growth and, with a 2-3 month lag, for consumer spending data (since SME revenues flow into household incomes). A sharp drop in marketing conditions with rising costs (aCNSMECTTR) signals a full profit squeeze in the SME sector — the combination most reliably precedes SME financial distress waves.

aCNSMECDIR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Middle-of-south China, Confidence
aCNSMECDIR.meaning: CASME SME Confidence sub-index for Middle-of-south China (中南地区). Covers small and medium enterprises in China's central-south provinces — including Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Guangxi, Hainan, and Guangdong (depending on CASME regional classification). This region combines manufacturing, agriculture, and services SMEs in China's populous interior and southern coastal areas. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMECDIR.how_to_use: Middle-of-south China SME confidence bridges the inland-coastal divide: the region includes both highly industrialized coastal Guangdong and inland agricultural provinces. A drop in confidence here while eastern coastal regions hold suggests that interior provinces are underperforming, consistent with slower infrastructure-led recovery absorption. Compare with eastern China (aCNSMECDER) and northern China (aCNSMECDNR) confidence to identify which regional economies are leading vs. lagging the national cycle.

aCNSMECTIR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Middle-of-south China, Cost
aCNSMECTIR.meaning: CASME SME Cost sub-index for Middle-of-south China. Measures cost pressures for small and medium enterprises in China's central-south provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMECTIR.how_to_use: Middle-of-south China SME costs reflect a mix of agricultural input costs (Henan grain belt), manufacturing costs in Hubei's auto industry cluster, and labor costs in Guangdong's export manufacturing base. When costs in this region spike relative to other regions (aCNSMECTER, aCNSMECTNR), it signals regionally concentrated supply chain or labor market stress. The region's large migrant worker population means labor cost dynamics here directly affect household remittances and rural consumption.

aCNSMEEPIR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Middle-of-south China, Expansion
aCNSMEEPIR.meaning: CASME SME Expansion sub-index for Middle-of-south China. Measures expansion intentions among small and medium enterprises in China's central-south provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEEPIR.how_to_use: Middle-of-south China SME expansion intentions are sensitive to infrastructure investment cycles — the region has been a major recipient of central government infrastructure spending (Three Gorges region, Yangtze River economic belt). When expansion intentions rise here alongside strong NBS infrastructure investment approvals, it confirms that policy stimulus is translating into SME investment plans. Compare with northeastern China expansion (aCNSMEEPOR) — persistent underperformance in the northeast vs. middle-south reflects the structural divergence between rust-belt provinces and more dynamic central-south economies.

aCNSMEFNIR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Middle-of-south China, Financing
aCNSMEFNIR.meaning: CASME SME Financing sub-index for Middle-of-south China. Measures the ease of obtaining financing for small and medium enterprises in China's central-south provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEFNIR.how_to_use: Financing conditions for middle-of-south China SMEs are more dependent on regional bank health and local government fiscal capacity than coastal regions. When financing conditions here drop below 95 while eastern coastal financing (aCNSMEFNER) holds steady, it signals that provincial bank balance sheet stress or local government debt problems are restricting credit to regional SMEs. This is particularly relevant monitoring for Henan and Hunan banks, which have faced periodic asset quality stress.

aCNSMEMKIR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Middle-of-south China, Marketing
aCNSMEMKIR.meaning: CASME SME Marketing sub-index for Middle-of-south China. Measures the ease and effectiveness of sales and marketing for small and medium enterprises in China's central-south provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEMKIR.how_to_use: Middle-of-south China SME marketing conditions reflect demand dynamics in a large and diverse regional economy. The region encompasses both export-oriented coastal Guangdong manufacturers and inland consumer goods-focused enterprises. When marketing conditions here diverge sharply from national trends, it often reflects regional property market cycles — the central-south region's property market is more volatile than the northeast but less liquid than the eastern coast, making housing wealth effects on consumer demand significant.

aCNSMEPFIR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Middle-of-south China, Performance
aCNSMEPFIR.meaning: CASME SME Performance sub-index for Middle-of-south China. Measures current-period business performance (revenues, profits) at small and medium enterprises in China's central-south provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEPFIR.how_to_use: Middle-of-south China SME performance is a coincident indicator for the region's economic health — a region that combines China's most export-intensive province (Guangdong) and some of its most populous interior provinces (Henan, Hunan). Strong performance here alongside weak performance in the northeast (aCNSMEPFOR) illustrates the structural divergence between dynamic sun-belt provinces and rust-belt decline. Use the regional performance index to assess whether national recovery is geographically inclusive.

aCNSMEPCIR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Middle-of-south China, Purchasing
aCNSMEPCIR.meaning: CASME SME Purchasing sub-index for Middle-of-south China. Measures procurement activity by small and medium enterprises in China's central-south provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEPCIR.how_to_use: Purchasing activity in middle-of-south China reflects a mix of agricultural input procurement (fertilizers, seeds), auto component procurement (Hubei auto cluster), and consumer goods manufacturing inputs. A spike in purchasing in this region ahead of agricultural seasons or auto model launches is a leading indicator for regional commodity and component demand. Compare with eastern China purchasing (aCNSMEPCER) to assess whether national purchasing momentum is broad-based or coastal-concentrated.

aCNSMERKIR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Middle-of-south China, Risk
aCNSMERKIR.units: Index (diffusion/confidence scale; higher reading = higher perceived risk)
aCNSMERKIR.meaning: CASME SME Risk sub-index for Middle-of-south China. Measures perceived business risk among small and medium enterprises in China's central-south provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMERKIR.how_to_use: Middle-of-south China SME risk perception is particularly sensitive to weather and flood events (Yangtze River flooding, Henan extreme rainfall), disease outbreaks in agricultural livestock (this region is a major pork-producing zone), and property market cycles in Guangdong cities. When risk spikes here while other regions remain stable, it typically signals a regional weather or supply chain event. Compare with the total SME risk (aCNSMERKTR) to gauge whether stress is regionally isolated or spreading nationally.

aCNSMETOIR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Middle-of-south China, Total
aCNSMETOIR.meaning: CASME SME Total Composite index for Middle-of-south China — the weighted aggregate of all sub-indices for small and medium enterprises in China's central-south provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMETOIR.how_to_use: The middle-of-south China SME composite is a useful swing indicator — it is more cyclically sensitive than the northeastern composite (which is dominated by heavy industry SOEs) but less export-dependent than the eastern coastal composite. When the middle-of-south composite is outperforming the eastern coastal composite (aCNSMETOER), it suggests that domestic consumption and infrastructure investment are driving growth rather than exports. This regional relative performance is closely monitored as an indicator of China's economic rebalancing progress.

aCNSMECDOR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Northeastern China, Confidence
aCNSMECDOR.meaning: CASME SME Confidence sub-index for Northeastern China (东北地区). Covers small and medium enterprises in China's three northeastern provinces — Liaoning, Jilin, and Heilongjiang. The northeast is China's traditional heavy industrial and agricultural heartland, now facing structural challenges from SOE-dominated industries (steel, coal, petrochemicals) and demographic outmigration. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMECDOR.how_to_use: Northeastern China SME confidence is structurally the weakest of all regional CASME sub-indices, reflecting long-term de-industrialization and outmigration from the rust belt provinces. A recovery in confidence above 100 in the northeast is a contrarian signal worth monitoring — it typically coincides with commodity price cycles (higher steel and coal prices benefit northeastern heavy industry) or targeted policy revitalization programs (central government northeast revitalization plans). Compare with middle-of-south and eastern confidence to gauge the northeast's relative position in the national cycle.

aCNSMECTOR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Northeastern China, Cost
aCNSMECTOR.meaning: CASME SME Cost sub-index for Northeastern China. Measures cost pressures for small and medium enterprises in China's three northeastern provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMECTOR.how_to_use: Northeastern China SME costs are heavily influenced by energy prices (the region is a major coal and oil producer but also a major industrial consumer), harsh winter heating costs, and high logistics costs due to geographic distance from coastal markets. When northeastern costs spike relative to other regions, it is often winter energy price driven. High costs combined with weak confidence (aCNSMECDOR) and poor performance (aCNSMEPFOR) confirm the northeast's structural cost-competitiveness disadvantage relative to coastal regions.

aCNSMEEPOR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Northeastern China, Expansion
aCNSMEEPOR.meaning: CASME SME Expansion sub-index for Northeastern China. Measures expansion intentions among small and medium enterprises in China's three northeastern provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEEPOR.how_to_use: Northeastern China SME expansion intentions are chronically suppressed by structural challenges: demographic decline (working-age population migrating south), SOE dominance crowding out private investment, and a weaker private sector ecosystem. Periodic spikes in expansion above 100 typically coincide with central government northeast revitalization spending (rail, urban renewal) or commodity price cycles. Use as a barometer for whether policy stimulus is reaching the private sector in the northeast's challenging business environment.

aCNSMEFNOR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Northeastern China, Financing
aCNSMEFNOR.meaning: CASME SME Financing sub-index for Northeastern China. Measures the ease of obtaining financing for small and medium enterprises in China's three northeastern provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEFNOR.how_to_use: Northeastern China has some of China's weakest regional banking ecosystems — Liaoning, Jilin, and Heilongjiang regional banks have faced persistent asset quality issues linked to SOE loan exposure. When financing conditions drop below 92 in the northeast while other regions are above 97, it signals regional banking sector stress that can feed into broader financial system contagion concerns. Persistent financing weakness in the northeast despite PBOC relending facility support indicates structural rather than cyclical credit channel problems.

aCNSMEMKOR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Northeastern China, Marketing
aCNSMEMKOR.meaning: CASME SME Marketing sub-index for Northeastern China. Measures the ease and effectiveness of sales and marketing for small and medium enterprises in China's three northeastern provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEMKOR.how_to_use: Northeastern China SME marketing conditions reflect demand in a region with contracting demographics and limited export connectivity. Marketing conditions here are most sensitive to: agricultural commodity prices (the northeast is China's major soybean and corn belt), winter tourism (Harbin ice festival), and heavy industrial output prices (steel, aluminum from Liaoning). A recovery in marketing above 100 in the northeast is a meaningful signal of demand revival in a region prone to chronic underperformance.

aCNSMEPFOR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Northeastern China, Performance
aCNSMEPFOR.meaning: CASME SME Performance sub-index for Northeastern China. Measures current-period business performance at small and medium enterprises in China's three northeastern provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEPFOR.how_to_use: Northeastern China SME performance is a coincident indicator for the region's economic health and a structural marker of China's regional divergence challenge. Sustained below-100 performance in the northeast over multiple years reflects the long-term decline of SOE-dependent regional economies. Cyclical improvements tied to commodity price spikes (steel, coal) provide temporary relief but rarely lead to sustained performance recovery absent structural private-sector development. Compare with total SME performance (aCNSMEPFTR) to quantify the northeast's performance gap.

aCNSMEPCOR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Northeastern China, Purchasing
aCNSMEPCOR.meaning: CASME SME Purchasing sub-index for Northeastern China. Measures procurement activity by small and medium enterprises in China's three northeastern provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEPCOR.how_to_use: Northeastern China SME purchasing is a leading indicator for regional commodity and agricultural input demand. The region is a major grain producer (soybeans, corn, rice), so agricultural input purchasing has strong spring seasonality. Industrial purchasing in the northeast is closely linked to steel and petrochemical sector cycles — when CNOOC and Sinopec Northeast units ramp production, their SME supplier base increases purchasing. Compare with total SME purchasing (aCNSMEPCTR) to assess whether the northeast is contributing to or detracting from national SME procurement momentum.

aCNSMERKOR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Northeastern China, Risk
aCNSMERKOR.units: Index (diffusion/confidence scale; higher reading = higher perceived risk)
aCNSMERKOR.meaning: CASME SME Risk sub-index for Northeastern China. Measures perceived business risk among small and medium enterprises in China's three northeastern provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMERKOR.how_to_use: Northeastern China SME risk perception tends to be structurally elevated compared to other regions due to: higher SOE concentration (downstream payment risk), weaker banking environment (financing availability risk), demographic outmigration (labor market risk), and geopolitical proximity to North Korea and Russia (geopolitical risk). Cyclical spikes typically coincide with commodity price collapses (hurting heavy industry clients) or regional bank stress events. A sustained decline in northeast risk below the national average (aCNSMERKTR) would be a meaningful contrarian signal of regional structural improvement.

aCNSMETOOR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Northeastern China, Total
aCNSMETOOR.meaning: CASME SME Total Composite index for Northeastern China — the weighted aggregate of all sub-indices for small and medium enterprises in China's three northeastern provinces (Liaoning, Jilin, Heilongjiang). Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMETOOR.how_to_use: The northeastern China SME composite is China's most structurally challenged regional business survey index, reflecting decades of industrial decline and demographic outmigration in the rust belt. When the composite drops to multi-year lows, it typically triggers northeast-specific policy responses from the central government (investment plans, SOE restructuring, talent retention programs). Monitoring the northeast composite relative to the national total (aCNSMETOTR) provides a real-time assessment of China's regional inequality dynamics — a politically sensitive metric for the central government.

aCNSMECDNR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Northern China, Confidence
aCNSMECDNR.meaning: CASME SME Confidence sub-index for Northern China (华北地区). Covers small and medium enterprises in China's northern provinces — including Beijing, Tianjin, Hebei, Shanxi, and Inner Mongolia. This region spans the capital city cluster, the coal-producing interior, and steel-heavy Hebei province. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMECDNR.how_to_use: Northern China SME confidence captures a strategically important region that includes China's capital (Beijing), the Jing-Jin-Ji megacity cluster, and its major energy and steel production base (Shanxi coal, Hebei steel). When northern China confidence drops while eastern coastal confidence holds, it often reflects coal/steel sector downturns or capital market regulatory changes affecting Beijing-based SMEs. The region's proximity to the political center makes it sensitive to regulatory announcements; a recovery here often signals policy normalization.

aCNSMECTNR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Northern China, Cost
aCNSMECTNR.meaning: CASME SME Cost sub-index for Northern China. Measures cost pressures for small and medium enterprises in China's northern provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMECTNR.how_to_use: Northern China SME costs are heavily influenced by coal prices (Shanxi is China's leading coal producer), steel prices (Hebei is China's largest steel-producing province), and environmental compliance costs (Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei air quality requirements have imposed significant retrofit costs on industrial SMEs). When environmental enforcement intensifies, cost sub-indices in northern China spike sharply as SMEs face compliance investments. This spike in northern costs relative to other regions is a leading indicator for heavier environmental policy tightening cycles.

aCNSMEEPNR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Northern China, Expansion
aCNSMEEPNR.meaning: CASME SME Expansion sub-index for Northern China. Measures expansion intentions among small and medium enterprises in China's northern provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEEPNR.how_to_use: Northern China SME expansion intentions are sensitive to national policy cycles given the region's proximity to Beijing — regulatory uncertainty or policy announcements affecting steel, coal, real estate, or internet sectors (all concentrated in this region) can rapidly shift expansion intentions. A recovery in northern expansion is often a leading indicator of regulatory normalization. Compare with eastern expansion (aCNSMEEPER) — when both recover together, it signals a broad private-sector capex recovery rather than a region-specific policy bounce.

aCNSMEFNNR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Northern China, Financing
aCNSMEFNNR.meaning: CASME SME Financing sub-index for Northern China. Measures the ease of obtaining financing for small and medium enterprises in China's northern provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEFNNR.how_to_use: Northern China SME financing reflects the health of Beijing-based bank headquarters and capital markets — the region hosts the headquarters of all major Chinese state banks and most large brokers. Paradoxically, being close to the financial center does not always help SME credit access: northern China SMEs often face intense competition for loans from state-directed heavy industry clients. When northern financing conditions improve, it often reflects PBOC policy signal amplification through Beijing-headquartered banks' SME loan expansion campaigns.

aCNSMEMKNR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Northern China, Marketing
aCNSMEMKNR.meaning: CASME SME Marketing sub-index for Northern China. Measures the ease and effectiveness of sales and marketing for small and medium enterprises in China's northern provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEMKNR.how_to_use: Northern China SME marketing conditions reflect demand dynamics in a region with a large capital city consumer market (Beijing, Tianjin), major B2B industrial demand (steel, coal, chemicals in Hebei and Shanxi), and significant real estate exposure. Beijing real estate market cycles have outsized effects on northern China SME marketing — real estate-related services (construction materials, home furnishings, property agents) make up a large share of northern SME revenues. A recovery in northern marketing often tracks the Beijing property transaction cycle.

aCNSMEPFNR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Northern China, Performance
aCNSMEPFNR.meaning: CASME SME Performance sub-index for Northern China. Measures current-period business performance at small and medium enterprises in China's northern provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEPFNR.how_to_use: Northern China SME performance tracks actual revenue and profit outcomes in a region with significant cyclical exposure to coal, steel, and real estate. During commodity upcycles, northern SME performance can surge strongly as upstream energy and metals industries drive regional demand. During downturns (coal demand slowdowns, steel overcapacity episodes), northern performance can drop sharply. The northern performance index is often a leading indicator for energy and materials sector capex trends — compare with coal and steel output data for validation.

aCNSMEPCNR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Northern China, Purchasing
aCNSMEPCNR.meaning: CASME SME Purchasing sub-index for Northern China. Measures procurement activity by small and medium enterprises in China's northern provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEPCNR.how_to_use: Northern China SME purchasing is a leading indicator for industrial commodity demand in the region — particularly steel, coal, and chemicals. Pre-winter purchasing spikes (September-October) are structural as northern SMEs stockpile heating fuel and materials before cold weather logistics disruption. Environmental-season purchasing dips (November-March during northern China industrial output restrictions) are also a regular pattern. Compare with total SME purchasing (aCNSMEPCTR) to assess whether northern purchasing cycles are in phase with the national trend.

aCNSMERKNR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Northern China, Risk
aCNSMERKNR.units: Index (diffusion/confidence scale; higher reading = higher perceived risk)
aCNSMERKNR.meaning: CASME SME Risk sub-index for Northern China. Measures perceived business risk among small and medium enterprises in China's northern provinces. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMERKNR.how_to_use: Northern China SME risk perception is highly sensitive to regulatory and policy announcements — the region's proximity to Beijing makes SMEs more attuned to regulatory environment shifts (tech crackdowns, real estate regulation, environmental enforcement). Risk spikes in the north often precede national policy announcements by signaling regulatory pre-positioning. A persistent risk spike in the north while other regions remain stable is worth monitoring for potential national-level policy shifts.

aCNSMETONR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Northern China, Total
aCNSMETONR.meaning: CASME SME Total Composite index for Northern China — the weighted aggregate of all sub-indices for small and medium enterprises in China's northern provinces (Beijing, Tianjin, Hebei, Shanxi, Inner Mongolia). Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMETONR.how_to_use: The northern China SME composite straddles the capital-city consumer economy and the heavy industrial heartland, making it a useful composite signal for both policy-driven cycles (regulatory/fiscal policy from Beijing) and commodity cycles (coal from Shanxi, steel from Hebei). When the northern composite diverges sharply from the eastern coastal composite (aCNSMETOER), it can signal either regulatory environment differences or sectoral (energy vs. tech/manufacturing) performance divergence. The northern composite is also sensitive to Beijing's own real estate and services cycle.

aCNSMEPFTR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Performance, Total
aCNSMEPFTR.subcategory: SME Performance Index — Total All Sectors
aCNSMEPFTR.meaning: CASME SME Performance sub-index — Total across all sectors. Aggregates performance readings from all surveyed SME sectors into a single economy-wide SME performance gauge capturing revenues, profitability, and order fulfillment across manufacturing, services, construction, agriculture, and other sectors. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEPFTR.how_to_use: Total SME performance is the most coincident indicator in the CASME survey suite — it reflects actual business outcomes rather than sentiment or intentions. Sustained below-100 performance is a leading signal for SME credit deterioration at banks — NPL ratios typically begin rising 2-3 months after the performance index drops below 97 for an extended period. When performance diverges below confidence (aCNSMECDTR) for multiple months, it signals that SME optimism is not backed by real business results — a warning sign for confidence reversal.

aCNSMEPCTR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Purchasing, Total
aCNSMEPCTR.subcategory: SME Purchasing Index — Total All Sectors
aCNSMEPCTR.meaning: CASME SME Purchasing sub-index — Total across all sectors. Aggregates purchasing activity readings from all surveyed SME sectors into a single economy-wide SME procurement gauge capturing raw material, component, and equipment procurement across all industries. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEPCTR.how_to_use: Total SME purchasing is an early leading indicator for industrial commodity and materials demand. Because small and medium firms collectively account for the majority of China's industrial purchasers by number (though large SOEs dominate by volume), broad-based drops in SME purchasing predict industrial demand softening 4-8 weeks ahead of hard data. The purchasing index tends to lead the NBS manufacturing PMI stocks of major inputs (aCNPMISTMJI/A) by 3-4 weeks. Compare purchasing trends with the expansion sub-index (aCNSMEEPTR) — purchasing without expansion signals restocking; purchasing alongside expansion signals genuine demand recovery.

aCNSMERKTR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Risk, Total
aCNSMERKTR.subcategory: SME Risk Index — Total All Sectors
aCNSMERKTR.units: Index (diffusion/confidence scale; higher reading = higher perceived risk)
aCNSMERKTR.meaning: CASME SME Risk sub-index — Total across all sectors. Aggregates risk perception readings from all surveyed SME sectors into a single economy-wide SME risk gauge capturing demand risk, cost risk, policy risk, financing risk, and operational risk across all industries. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMERKTR.how_to_use: Total SME risk perception is a leading indicator for investment and expansion pullbacks — when risk perception spikes above 110 economy-wide, subsequent expansion (aCNSMEEPTR) and purchasing (aCNSMEPCTR) sub-indices typically fall 1-2 months later. A broad-based spike in total SME risk that is not driven by any single sector or region signals a systemic shock or policy uncertainty event. Comparing total risk with sector-specific risk (construction: aCNSMERKCR, manufacturing: aCNSMERKMR) helps identify whether risk is concentrated or widespread.

aCNSMECDVR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Service industry, Confidence
aCNSMECDVR.meaning: CASME SME Confidence sub-index for the Service Industry sector. Measures the net balance of small and medium services enterprises reporting improved vs. deteriorating confidence. The service sector encompasses a broad range of SMEs: logistics, retail, IT services, business services, finance/insurance intermediaries, personal services, and education. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMECDVR.how_to_use: Services SME confidence is increasingly the most important indicator in the CASME survey as China's economy shifts toward services-led growth (services now ~55% of GDP). When services SME confidence diverges below manufacturing SME confidence (aCNSMECDMR), it signals a consumer and business services demand slowdown that may not show up in factory-focused PMI data. Compare with the NBS non-manufacturing PMI business activities (aCNPMINMSBA/A) and Caixin services PMI (aCNNPMIGRQ/A) for triangulation across survey methodologies.

aCNSMECTVR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Service industry, Cost
aCNSMECTVR.meaning: CASME SME Cost sub-index for the Service Industry sector. Measures cost pressures — labor costs (dominant in services), rent, technology infrastructure, and regulatory compliance costs — experienced by small and medium services enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMECTVR.how_to_use: Services SME costs are predominantly labor-driven — wages account for 40-60% of total costs for most services businesses. When this sub-index rises above 108 for 2+ months, it typically signals labor market tightness in services employment, which feeds into CPI services inflation with a 1-3 month lag. Compare with the manufacturing cost sub-index (aCNSMECTMR) — persistent services costs rising faster than manufacturing costs signals services sector wage inflation overtaking goods sector wage inflation, consistent with China's structural rebalancing toward higher-value services jobs.

aCNSMEEPVR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Service industry, Expansion
aCNSMEEPVR.meaning: CASME SME Expansion sub-index for the Service Industry sector. Measures expansion intentions — new service offerings, branch openings, workforce hiring, technology investment — among small and medium services enterprises. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEEPVR.how_to_use: Services SME expansion intentions are a leading indicator for the services labor market and technology investment cycle. When services expansion exceeds manufacturing expansion (aCNSMEEPMR), it confirms the structural shift toward services-led growth. Strong services expansion intentions are also a leading indicator for commercial real estate demand (office and retail leasing) — small services firms account for a significant share of SME leasing demand. Compare with NBS non-manufacturing new orders PMI (aCNPMINMSNO/A) to validate whether expansion plans reflect actual order improvement.

aCNSMEFNVR.description: Small and Medium Enterprises, Service industry, Financing
aCNSMEFNVR.meaning: CASME SME Financing sub-index for the Service Industry sector. Measures the ease of obtaining financing for small and medium services enterprises. Services SMEs face structural challenges in bank lending — intangible assets (brand, human capital, software) are difficult to pledge as collateral, and services firms have more volatile revenues than manufacturers. Published monthly by CASME.
aCNSMEFNVR.how_to_use: Services SME financing conditions are particularly sensitive to the growth of non-bank financial products — internet lending platforms (Ant Group, JD Finance), supply chain finance, and factoring have been growing sources of credit for services SMEs.
